steps: Confirm properties.supportsHttpsTrafficOnly=false on the exact storage account. Missing or malformed values are UNKNOWN to this native check.
Inventory REST/HTTP and Azure Files SMB or NFS clients and migrate incompatible clients to encrypted connections before enforcement.
Enable secure transfer, verify authorized clients, recollect the account and confirm supportsHttpsTrafficOnly=true.

cli.label: Require secure transfer after client migration

caveats: Enabling secure transfer rejects insecure REST/HTTP requests and may disrupt older SMB clients or file workloads. Azure Files protocol encryption settings can change the effective scope; validate the account configuration and rollback with the workload owner.
The native predicate checks only the account flag; it does not measure client protocol compatibility or successful encrypted access.

remediation_details.summary: Set the flagged Azure Storage account minimum TLS version to TLS1_2 after checking legacy clients.
steps: Confirm properties.minimumTlsVersion is explicitly TLS1_0 or TLS1_1 on the exact storage account. An absent or unknown enum is UNKNOWN to this native check.
Review Storage request logs and application inventories for clients negotiating older TLS versions; upgrade their runtimes and test TLS1_2 access.
Set minimumTlsVersion to TLS1_2, validate authorized clients, recollect and rerun the check.

cli.label: Require at least TLS 1.2 after migration

caveats: Clients unable to negotiate TLS 1.2 can lose access. Inspect request logs and coordinate rollout with storage application owners before changing the minimum.
The native predicate is a configuration test, not a client connection test. Current Azure service retirement of older TLS protocols does not itself prove this configured field meets policy.

checks.remediation: Review the exact Azure Owner role assignment and replace unnecessary standing Owner access with a narrower approved role or time-bound eligibility.

remediation_details.summary: Review the exact Azure Owner role assignment and replace unnecessary standing Owner access with a narrower approved role or time-bound eligibility.
steps: Verify properties.roleDefinitionId ends in built-in Owner ID 8e3af657-a8ff-443c-a75c-2fe8c4bcb635 and identify the exact principalId, assignment scope, condition and assignment resource ID. This check fails any declared Owner assignment and does not evaluate inherited grants, groups or PIM eligibility.

With the identity and resource owners, document the principal tasks and emergency access needs. Assign a narrower built-in or reviewed custom role at the smallest workable scope, or establish approved time-bound PIM eligibility; test the replacement before revoking standing Owner.

Only after confirming the replacement and preserving break-glass coverage, remove the exact reviewed Owner assignment by its assignment ID. Recollect and verify the same principal and scope; inspect effective access separately.

cli.label: Inspect assignments at the reviewed scope
Remove only this verified standing Owner assignment after replacement

caveats: Owner can be necessary for subscription administration or emergency recovery. Removing it can lock out operators or automation; preserve a tested break-glass route, replacement access and rollback before deletion.
Never delete by principal, role name or broad scope. Check the exact assignment ID and owner approval; the finding alone does not prove the grant is unnecessary.
The native predicate checks one declared assignment and reports no effective-access calculation. Group membership, inherited roles, deny assignments and PIM eligibility require separate review.

checks.remediation: Replace a literal wildcard in the flagged custom Azure RBAC role with owner-reviewed Actions or DataActions required by its assigned principals.

remediation_details.summary: Replace a literal wildcard in the flagged custom Azure RBAC role with owner-reviewed Actions or DataActions required by its assigned principals.
steps: Inspect properties.type=CustomRole and every properties.permissions[] block of the exact role. This native check fails if at least one literal * appears in actions or dataActions and none of those wildcard blocks has notActions/notDataActions exclusions; any such exclusion makes the whole evaluation MANUAL, even if another block still contains an unrestricted wildcard.

Inventory assignments and each principal workload, then have the RBAC owner select the minimum supported control-plane Actions and data-plane DataActions. Draft a complete role JSON retaining the same role ID, assignableScopes and unrelated reviewed permission blocks while replacing the broad grant.

Apply the reviewed role definition, validate every dependent principal, re-read permissions and recollect. Separately review excluded and patterned grants, because an exclusion is not a deny and this predicate does not prove least privilege.

cli.label: Read the exact custom role definition
Apply the owner-reviewed full custom role definition

caveats: Updating a custom role affects all current assignments and can remove required control-plane or data-plane access. Stage workload tests and a rollback, and obtain owner review of the complete definition.
Do not treat notActions or notDataActions as explicit denies; they only subtract operations from that role grant and may not restrict permissions granted through other roles.
The scan does not identify which permissions are needed. Do not add or substitute new privileged Actions to make the check pass.

checks.rationale: Reviews declared custom-role permission blocks. A wildcard with no exclusions in its own permission plane yields FAIL, even when a separate block or the other plane contains exclusions. This does not establish an assigned principal or effective authorization.
checks.description: Reviews declared custom-role permission blocks. A wildcard with no exclusions in its own permission plane yields FAIL, even when a separate block or the other plane contains exclusions. This does not establish an assigned principal or effective authorization.
checks.pass_when: PASS when complete readable permission blocks contain no wildcard actions or dataActions. Wildcards with corresponding exclusions require MANUAL review; unavailable relevant facts produce UNKNOWN.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when any readable block declares actions=[*] without notActions exclusions, or dataActions=[*] without notDataActions exclusions. Exclusions in a different block or permission plane do not remove that finding.

alternative.sql: SELECT row_id, CASE WHEN json_type(payload, '$') IS DISTINCT FROM 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$.collection_status'), 'collected') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty') OR coalesce(json_type(payload, '$._coverage'), 'OBJECT') <> 'OBJECT' OR json_type(payload, '$.shieldedInstanceConfig') IS DISTINCT FROM 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$.shieldedInstanceConfig.collection_status'), 'collected') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty') OR coalesce(json_type(payload, '$.shieldedInstanceConfig._coverage'), 'OBJECT') <> 'OBJECT' OR (json_type(payload, '$._coverage.shieldedInstanceConfig') IS NOT NULL AND (json_type(payload, '$._coverage.shieldedInstanceConfig') <> 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$._coverage.shieldedInstanceConfig.status'), 'unknown') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty'))) OR (json_type(payload, '$.shieldedInstanceConfig._coverage.enableVtpm') IS NOT NULL AND (json_type(payload, '$.shieldedInstanceConfig._coverage.enableVtpm') <> 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$.shieldedInstanceConfig._coverage.enableVtpm.status'), 'unknown') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty'))) OR coalesce(json_type(payload, '$.shieldedInstanceConfig.enableVtpm'), 'NULL') NOT IN ('BOOLEAN') THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN json_extract_string(payload, '$.shieldedInstanceConfig.enableVtpm') IN ('true') THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS status, json_extract(payload, '$.shieldedInstanceConfig.enableVtpm') AS configured FROM facts ORDER BY row_id

checks.remediation: Set pod containers[*].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation=false in the owning PodSpec.

caveats: This predicate reads declared PodSpec fields across regular, init and ephemeral containers; it does not prove runtime isolation or admission enforcement.
Changing security context or ServiceAccount identity can interrupt the workload; confirm the actual owner and test the rollout.

iac.code: Set containers[*].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation=false under spec in the reviewed pod declaration and roll out through its owner.
iac.label: Update the owning manifest or Helm values

steps: Inspect spec on the named pod; locate each flagged container or Pod-level containers[*].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation=false declaration and identify the owning manifest/controller.
Set allowPrivilegeEscalation=false after removing incompatible privileged or SYS_ADMIN requirements.
Roll out the reviewed owner manifest, test workload behavior and admission, then rerun the check against the new declaration.
remediation_details.summary: Set pod containers[*].securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation=false in the owning PodSpec.

checks.rationale: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) does not explicitly set securityContext.allowPrivilegeEscalation: false (the API default is true). With escalation allowed, setuid binaries and file capabilities inside the image can raise the process above its starting privileges (no_new_privs is not set).

caveats: The evaluator reads the Pod or controller template declaration, not future admission or runtime isolation.
Removing privilege, root identity or host networking/ports may interrupt workloads; test the replacement path and rollback before rollout.

iac.code: Set containers[*].ports[*].hostPort=0 or absent under spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec in the reviewed cronjob manifest or Helm values.
iac.label: Update the Pod template owner

steps: Inspect spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec on the named cronjob, including init and ephemeral containers, and identify the durable owner.
Remove nonzero hostPort declarations in each flagged container and use a reviewed Service or ingress path.
Roll out the reviewed owner manifest, test application behavior and admission, then rerun the check.
remediation_details.summary: Set cronjob spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec.containers[*].ports[*].hostPort=0 or absent in the owning Pod declaration.

checks.rationale: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template at spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec has any container (regular, init or ephemeral) with a non-zero ports[].hostPort. For each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule, the container is published directly on every scheduled node's IP, bypassing Service and NetworkPolicy controls.
checks.description: Flags a CronJob whose Pod template at spec.jobTemplate.spec.template.spec has any container (regular, init or ephemeral) with a non-zero ports[].hostPort. For each Job Pod the CronJob spawns on schedule, the container is published directly on every scheduled node's IP, bypassing Service and NetworkPolicy controls.
checks.pass_when: All hostPort values are 0 or omitted.
checks.fail_when: Any container declares hostPort between 1 and 65535.
checks.not_applicable_when: Only when the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

checks.rationale: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) declares a non-zero ports[].hostPort. hostPort publishes the container on the node IP outside Service and NetworkPolicy control and can shadow node services.

checks.title: Pod containers preserve default proc filesystem masks
checks.remediation: Restore the default procMount mask for each flagged Linux container.

caveats: The evaluator reads declared configuration, not admission or runtime enforcement. Pod security, storage and identity changes can interrupt workloads; stage a tested rollback.

iac.code: Change spec.containers/initContainers/ephemeralContainers[].securityContext.procMount in the owning pod manifest or Helm values, not only the live object.
iac.label: Change the existing managed declaration

steps: Inspect spec.containers/initContainers/ephemeralContainers[].securityContext.procMount on the named pod and identify its durable manifest or controller owner.
Remove an Unmasked procMount override or set procMount=Default in the owning Pod template after testing applications that read /proc.
Apply the reviewed owner change, test dependent workloads and rerun the native declaration check.
remediation_details.summary: Restore the default procMount mask for each flagged Linux container.

checks.rationale: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) sets securityContext.procMount to Unmasked. An unmasked /proc exposes kernel interfaces (e.g. /proc/sys, /proc/kcore) normally hidden by the runtime, aiding information leaks and container escape.
checks.description: Flags a Pod where any container (regular, init or ephemeral) sets securityContext.procMount to Unmasked. An unmasked /proc exposes kernel interfaces (e.g. /proc/sys, /proc/kcore) normally hidden by the runtime, aiding information leaks and container escape.
checks.pass_when: All containers use procMount Default (or omit it).
checks.fail_when: Any container sets procMount: Unmasked.
checks.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results). Unknown procMount values are UNKNOWN.

checks.title: Pod avoids custom SELinux user and role identities
checks.remediation: Remove custom SELinux user and role overrides from the flagged Pod or Linux containers.

caveats: The evaluator reads declared configuration, not admission or runtime enforcement. Pod security, storage and identity changes can interrupt workloads; stage a tested rollback.

iac.code: Change spec.securityContext.seLinuxOptions.user/role and containers[].securityContext.seLinuxOptions.user/role in the owning pod manifest or Helm values, not only the live object.
iac.label: Change the existing managed declaration

steps: Inspect spec.securityContext.seLinuxOptions.user/role and containers[].securityContext.seLinuxOptions.user/role on the named pod and identify its durable manifest or controller owner.
Unset only seLinuxOptions.user and seLinuxOptions.role in the Pod and flagged containers; retain separately approved SELinux type and level settings.
Apply the reviewed owner change, test dependent workloads and rerun the native declaration check.
remediation_details.summary: Remove custom SELinux user and role overrides from the flagged Pod or Linux containers.

checks.rationale: Flags a Pod where the Pod-level or any container securityContext.seLinuxOptions sets a custom user or role. Overriding the SELinux user/role can place the process in a more privileged SELinux identity and defeat the MAC confinement the node policy relies on.
checks.description: Flags a Pod where the Pod-level or any container securityContext.seLinuxOptions sets a custom user or role. Overriding the SELinux user/role can place the process in a more privileged SELinux identity and defeat the MAC confinement the node policy relies on.
checks.pass_when: No seLinuxOptions.user or .role is set anywhere.
checks.fail_when: Pod or any container sets seLinuxOptions.user or .role.
checks.not_applicable_when: When spec.os.name is windows (Linux-only control), or the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results).

checks.title: ServiceAccount disables default API token automount
frameworks: Kubernetes NSA and CISA Hardening Guidance v1.0

controls.framework: Kubernetes NSA and CISA Hardening Guidance v1.0

checks.remediation: Disable default API token automount on this ServiceAccount when its workloads do not need Kubernetes API access.

caveats: Pod-level automountServiceAccountToken overrides the ServiceAccount default; this check does not verify each Pod.
Disabling token mount can break workloads that use the Kubernetes API or projected credentials.

iac.code: Set automountServiceAccountToken: false on the owning ServiceAccount manifest after dependency review.
iac.label: Update the ServiceAccount declaration

steps: Inspect automountServiceAccountToken on the ServiceAccount and every Pod that uses it; identify workloads that call the Kubernetes API.
Set automountServiceAccountToken=false on the owning ServiceAccount and remove any unneeded Pod override after testing dependent clients.
Roll out through the ServiceAccount/workload owner, verify Pods and intended API calls, then rerun the check.
remediation_details.summary: Disable default API token automount on this ServiceAccount when its workloads do not need Kubernetes API access.

checks.rationale: A ServiceAccount is flagged when automountServiceAccountToken is true or omitted, since omission defaults to true in this evaluator. Pods using that account can receive API credentials unless they override the setting.
checks.description: A ServiceAccount is flagged when automountServiceAccountToken is true or omitted, since omission defaults to true in this evaluator. Pods using that account can receive API credentials unless they override the setting.
checks.pass_when: The ServiceAccount explicitly sets automountServiceAccountToken to false.
checks.fail_when: The field is true or absent.
checks.not_applicable_when: On a positively identified provider- or control-plane-managed object, the registration wrapper changes an underlying FAIL, MANUAL, UNKNOWN, or DENIED to NOT_APPLICABLE; an underlying PASS remains PASS.

checks.title: Namespace declares a broad limits.cpu resource quota
checks.remediation: Declare an unscoped namespace-wide ResourceQuota limits.cpu quantity.

caveats: Scoped quotas are a MANUAL result here and do not prove namespace-wide coverage.
A new quota can reject workloads whose requests or limits are missing or exceed the reviewed capacity; test admission and scheduling.

iac.code: Set spec.hard.limits.cpu to a reviewed quantity in an unscoped ResourceQuota for this namespace.
iac.label: Update the namespace ResourceQuota

steps: Inspect ResourceQuota objects for limits.cpu and their scopes/scopeSelector in the named namespace.
Choose an approved limits.cpu quantity from observed demand and capacity; declare it on a namespace-wide ResourceQuota without a limiting selector.
Apply through the namespace owner, verify new Pod admissions and quota status, then rerun the check.
remediation_details.summary: Declare an unscoped namespace-wide ResourceQuota limits.cpu quantity.

checks.rationale: Flags a Namespace with no unscoped ResourceQuota whose spec.hard sets limits.cpu, using the complete ResourceQuota inventory. Without a namespace-wide cap on total CPU limits, one tenant or compromised workload can consume cluster capacity and starve other namespaces. A quota limited by scopes/scopeSelector only yields MANUAL.
checks.description: Flags a Namespace with no unscoped ResourceQuota whose spec.hard sets limits.cpu, using the complete ResourceQuota inventory. Without a namespace-wide cap on total CPU limits, one tenant or compromised workload can consume cluster capacity and starve other namespaces. A quota limited by scopes/scopeSelector only yields MANUAL.
checks.pass_when: At least one ResourceQuota in the namespace without scopes/scopeSelector declares hard['limits.cpu'].
checks.fail_when: No ResourceQuota in the namespace declares hard['limits.cpu'] at all.
checks.not_applicable_when: When the object is provider/control-plane managed (k8s_managed re-labels non-passing results) (kube-system, kube-public, kube-node-lease, provider namespaces); incomplete quota inventory is UNKNOWN.

checks.title: Compute VM enables deletion protection
checks.remediation: Set instance deletionProtection to True on the reviewed resource.

caveats: Deletion protection does not prevent instance modification or replace backup and recovery controls.
The check reads declared configuration; runtime behavior and collection completeness require independent verification.

iac.code: Set deletion_protection = true on the owning google_compute_instance declaration.
iac.label: Update the owning declaration

steps: Inspect deletionProtection on the exact instance resource and identify its configuration owner.
Use the supported provider update to set deletionProtection to True after checking dependent clients and rollout impact.
Read deletionProtection again and rerun gcp.reviewed.compute.deletion_protection; verify dependent workloads separately.
remediation_details.summary: Set instance deletionProtection to True on the reviewed resource.

alternative.sql: SELECT row_id, CASE WHEN json_type(payload, '$') IS DISTINCT FROM 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$.collection_status'), 'collected') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty') OR coalesce(json_type(payload, '$._coverage'), 'OBJECT') <> 'OBJECT' OR (json_type(payload, '$._coverage.deletionProtection') IS NOT NULL AND (json_type(payload, '$._coverage.deletionProtection') <> 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$._coverage.deletionProtection.status'), 'unknown') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty'))) OR coalesce(json_type(payload, '$.deletionProtection'), 'NULL') NOT IN ('BOOLEAN') THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN json_extract_string(payload, '$.deletionProtection') IN ('true') THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS status, json_extract(payload, '$.deletionProtection') AS configured FROM facts ORDER BY row_id

checks.rationale: For a GCP Compute Engine VM, this evaluator flags FAIL when collected deletionProtection is false instead of true. The VM can be deleted without the configured deletion safeguard.
checks.description: For a GCP Compute Engine VM, this evaluator flags FAIL when collected deletionProtection is false instead of true. The VM can be deleted without the configured deletion safeguard.
checks.pass_when: PASS when deletionProtection is true.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when collected deletionProtection is false instead of true.

checks.title: Bucket configures a positive soft-delete retention period
checks.remediation: Set a positive, owner-approved soft-delete retention duration on the flagged Cloud Storage bucket.

caveats: The evaluator rejects only an explicit zero retention duration; it does not establish recoverability. The new duration applies to future deletions and can increase storage cost; check organization constraints and permitted duration units.

iac.code: Set soft_delete_policy.retention_duration_seconds to an approved positive duration in the owning bucket declaration.
iac.label: Change the existing managed declaration

steps: Inspect softDeletePolicy.retentionDurationSeconds on the exact bucket and confirm the organization retention and cost policy.
Choose a supported positive duration with the data owner, then update the bucket's soft-delete policy through its configuration owner.
Reread the retention duration, test an authorized recovery path and rerun the native check.
remediation_details.summary: Set a positive, owner-approved soft-delete retention duration on the flagged Cloud Storage bucket.

checks.pass_when: PASS when the retention duration is a positive integer.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when softDeletePolicy.retentionDurationSeconds is zero.

iac.code: Set logging.log_bucket to the approved existing destination on the owning source bucket declaration and grant its analytics writer through the log bucket owner.

references.title: Cloud Storage usage and storage logs

steps: Inspect logging.logBucket on the named source bucket and choose an existing log bucket with approved access, retention and cost controls.
Grant the documented Cloud Storage analytics writer role on that log bucket through its owner, then set the source bucket's logging.logBucket to it.
Reread logging.logBucket and independently verify that log objects arrive; rerun the native check.

checks.remediation: Set iam_password_policy PasswordPolicy.RequireUppercaseCharacters to True on the reviewed resource.

caveats: The update API resets every omitted password-policy option to its default. The reviewed input file must preserve every other approved setting while enabling RequireUppercaseCharacters; this affects native IAM user passwords, not federated sign-in.

steps: Inspect PasswordPolicy.RequireUppercaseCharacters on the exact iam_password_policy resource and identify its configuration owner.
Use the supported provider update to set PasswordPolicy.RequireUppercaseCharacters to True after checking dependent clients and rollout impact.
Read PasswordPolicy.RequireUppercaseCharacters again and rerun aws.iam.password_uppercase; verify dependent workloads separately.

alternative.sql: SELECT row_id, CASE WHEN json_type(payload, '$') IS DISTINCT FROM 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$.collection_status'), 'collected') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty') OR coalesce(json_type(payload, '$._coverage'), 'OBJECT') <> 'OBJECT' OR json_type(payload, '$.PasswordPolicy') IS DISTINCT FROM 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$.PasswordPolicy.collection_status'), 'collected') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty') OR coalesce(json_type(payload, '$.PasswordPolicy._coverage'), 'OBJECT') <> 'OBJECT' OR (json_type(payload, '$._coverage.PasswordPolicy') IS NOT NULL AND (json_type(payload, '$._coverage.PasswordPolicy') <> 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$._coverage.PasswordPolicy.status'), 'unknown') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty'))) OR (json_type(payload, '$.PasswordPolicy._coverage.RequireUppercaseCharacters') IS NOT NULL AND (json_type(payload, '$.PasswordPolicy._coverage.RequireUppercaseCharacters') <> 'OBJECT' OR coalesce(json_extract_string(payload, '$.PasswordPolicy._coverage.RequireUppercaseCharacters.status'), 'unknown') NOT IN ('collected', 'empty'))) OR coalesce(json_type(payload, '$.PasswordPolicy.RequireUppercaseCharacters'), 'NULL') NOT IN ('BOOLEAN') THEN 'UNKNOWN' WHEN json_extract_string(payload, '$.PasswordPolicy.RequireUppercaseCharacters') IN ('true') THEN 'PASS' ELSE 'FAIL' END AS status, json_extract(payload, '$.PasswordPolicy.RequireUppercaseCharacters') AS configured FROM facts ORDER BY row_id

checks.remediation: GuardDuty is enabled in the selected region. If no detector exists, have the regional owner enable GuardDuty; if one exists but DISABLED, review and enable it.

caveats: A nonunique detector inventory or unknown status is UNKNOWN; enabled does not prove features or findings reviewed.
No credential, certificate body, log content or live account mutation is requested.

iac.code: If no detector exists, have the regional owner enable GuardDuty; if one exists but DISABLED, review and enable it. Apply through the reviewed Terraform/CloudFormation or account-owner process after dependency checks.
iac.label: Update the existing configuration owner

steps: Inspect complete guardduty_detector inventory and Configuration.Status on the exact native resource or selected account; source target: one unique detector with Status=ENABLED.
If no detector exists, have the regional owner enable GuardDuty; if one exists but DISABLED, review and enable it.
Recollect the required native facts and rerun aws.a.guardduty.region_enabled; preserve UNKNOWN or NOT_APPLICABLE where source eligibility differs.
remediation_details.summary: GuardDuty is enabled in the selected region. If no detector exists, have the regional owner enable GuardDuty; if one exists but DISABLED, review and enable it.

checks.rationale: Scope-level check per account/region that FAILs when no GuardDuty detector exists in the region or the single detector's status is DISABLED. Without GuardDuty, threat detection for credential exfiltration, crypto-mining, malicious IP traffic and anomalous API calls is absent in that region, which attackers often target precisely because it is unused.
checks.description: Scope-level check per account/region that FAILs when no GuardDuty detector exists in the region or the single detector's status is DISABLED. Without GuardDuty, threat detection for credential exfiltration, crypto-mining, malicious IP traffic and anomalous API calls is absent in that region, which attackers often target precisely because it is unused.
checks.pass_when: PASS when exactly one detector exists in the region and its status is ENABLED.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the region has no detector or the detector status is DISABLED.

checks.remediation: An AWS Config recorder is recording without a reported failure in the selected region. Configure a recorder if absent, start recording, and resolve any lastStatus=Failure after reviewing delivery channel and role.

caveats: Pending is distinct from Success and passes this pinned source when recording; missing or ambiguous status is UNKNOWN.
No credential, certificate body, log content or live account mutation is requested.

iac.code: Configure a recorder if absent, start recording, and resolve any lastStatus=Failure after reviewing delivery channel and role. Apply through the reviewed Terraform/CloudFormation or account-owner process after dependency checks.
iac.label: Update the existing configuration owner

references.title: AWS CLI Config recorder status response

steps: Inspect complete config_recorder inventory, recorder name joined Status.ConfigurationRecordersStatus[].recording/lastStatus on the exact native resource or selected account; source target: at least one recorder; every recorder recording=true and lastStatus not Failure.
Configure a recorder if absent, start recording, and resolve any lastStatus=Failure after reviewing delivery channel and role.
Recollect the required native facts and rerun aws.a.config.region_recorder_enabled; preserve UNKNOWN or NOT_APPLICABLE where source eligibility differs.
remediation_details.summary: An AWS Config recorder is recording without a reported failure in the selected region. Configure a recorder if absent, start recording, and resolve any lastStatus=Failure after reviewing delivery channel and role.

checks.rationale: Scope-level check per account/region that FAILs when no AWS Config configuration recorder exists, or when any recorder's matching status entry shows recording=false or lastStatus=Failure. Without a working recorder, configuration changes are not captured, Config rules cannot evaluate, and resource history needed for investigations is missing.
checks.description: Scope-level check per account/region that FAILs when no AWS Config configuration recorder exists, or when any recorder's matching status entry shows recording=false or lastStatus=Failure. Without a working recorder, configuration changes are not captured, Config rules cannot evaluate, and resource history needed for investigations is missing.
checks.pass_when: PASS when Every recorder in the region is recording and none reports lastStatus Failure (Pending is accepted).
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the region has no recorder, or a recorder is not recording or reports lastStatus Failure.

checks.title: Application registration credentials declare an end date more than 30 days after the snapshot
checks.remediation: Rotate each expiring or undated application credential by its key ID and validate the replacement before retirement.

caveats: The evaluator compares credential endDateTime to snapshot time and does not read secret values, usage, sign-in success or whether the key is stored safely. A newer credential does not clear the finding while the old flagged credential remains.

Graph addPassword returns secretText exactly once. Do not paste, log or interpolate it in a report or copied command; run secret creation in the owner’s protected workflow. Certificate addKey can require proof of possession and its private key must not be sent to Graph.
Removing an old key can break clients that have not migrated. Review the exact keyId and application object ID, test all consumers and retain a rollback path before revocation.

references.title: Microsoft Graph get application and credential metadata
Microsoft Graph addPassword and secret response
Microsoft Graph addKey and proof requirement

steps: For the exact application object ID, inspect passwordCredentials and keyCredentials metadata and evidence.credential_issues; no credentials is NOT_APPLICABLE, while a missing endDateTime or one within 30 days of the snapshot fails.

Identify every consumer of each flagged keyId and choose a new password or certificate with an explicit owner-approved expiry beyond the 30-day threshold; prefer managed or federated identity where supported.

Have the application owner add the replacement through the proper Graph addPassword or addKey workflow, store any returned secretText only in the approved secret store, and update and test every consumer without showing it in findings or command output.
After confirming usage and rollback, remove only the old reviewed keyId with the matching password or certificate removal operation; recollect application metadata and rerun this check.
remediation_details.summary: Rotate each expiring or undated application credential by its key ID and validate the replacement before retirement.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when any password or key credential has no end date or expires within 30 days of the snapshot.

checks.title: Enabled Entra ID user has a recorded successful sign-in within 90 days of the snapshot
checks.remediation: Investigate the enabled Entra user whose last recorded successful sign-in is more than 90 days old before changing access.

remediation_details.summary: Investigate the enabled Entra user whose last recorded successful sign-in is more than 90 days old before changing access.
steps: Inspect accountEnabled and signInActivity.lastSuccessfulSignInDateTime for the exact directory user object ID. The native check compares that successful interactive or non-interactive timestamp with the snapshot created_at; a failed sign-in attempt is not successful use.

Confirm the observation window and compare owner, business purpose, emergency-access status, application dependencies and independent sign-in records. A missing or pre-2023-12-01 successful timestamp remains UNKNOWN because this field was not historically backfilled.

If the account owner confirms it is unused, stage a reversible, owner-approved access change in the tenant identity workflow and retain a recovery route; do not disable the account solely from this finding.

Monitor intended access through the agreed period, recollect the same user and rerun azure.claude.entra_user_recent_sign_in; an old successful-use timestamp can remain a finding until a genuine authorized successful sign-in occurs.

cli.label: Inspect exact user state and successful sign-in metadata only

caveats: lastSignInDateTime and lastNonInteractiveSignInDateTime record attempts, including failures, and must not be substituted for lastSuccessfulSignInDateTime. The successful field starts on 2023-12-01 and is not backfilled.

Missing signInActivity, a missing or malformed successful timestamp, a timestamp outside the observed period, or inaccessible licensed Graph data cannot prove inactivity and yields UNKNOWN. Sign-in metadata alone does not prove whether an account or workload is safe to disable.

The read-only example needs tenant-approved Graph access; signInActivity details require Microsoft Entra ID P1/P2 and AuditLog.Read.All. No account mutation is supplied because the evidence cannot establish a safe disable target or recovery plan.

checks.remediation: Replace the flagged standing User Access Administrator Azure RBAC assignment with the least privileged approved access, then remove its exact assignment ID.

caveats: The evaluator checks only roleDefinitionId and does not distinguish principal type; it does not measure effective permissions from other assignments or groups.

Deleting a User Access Administrator assignment can interrupt administration or deployments. Confirm principal owner, exact assignment ID, replacement access and a documented regrant plan; never delete by role or broad scope filter.
Inherited assignments may be controlled at a parent scope and cannot be changed by a child-scope owner; the source assignment ID determines the authorized change location.

references.title: Azure CLI role assignment list and exact-ID delete
Azure role assignment scope and conditions

steps: Inspect the named role_assignment properties.roleDefinitionId, principalId, principalType and scope; this predicate targets all principal types and compares the built-in User Access Administrator role GUID.

With the access owner, identify the specific work requiring User Access Administrator and provision an appropriately scoped replacement role or time-bound eligible access before revoking this standing assignment.
Re-read assignments at the exact scope and confirm the one full role-assignment resource ID, principal and role. Revoke only that verified ID after the replacement access is tested.
Validate the principal’s intended work and emergency access, recollect this role_assignment and rerun azure.claude.iam_no_user_access_administrator_assignment.

checks.remediation: Replace the exact custom Azure RBAC role control-plane wildcard with reviewed required Actions.

caveats: The evaluator checks only literal * and *:* in control-plane Actions on CustomRole. Other broad patterns and DataActions are outside this predicate, and NotActions do not make a wildcard automatically safe.

Updating a custom role affects every current assignment and can remove required access. Preserve role ID, assignable scopes, NotActions and DataActions in the reviewed file, stage workload tests and prepare rollback.
The needed Actions cannot be inferred from a scan; the role owner must approve them. This remediation does not grant new permissions or create escalation chains.

references.title: Azure custom role Actions and scopes

steps: Inspect the flagged CustomRole properties.permissions[].actions and assignableScopes; this predicate fails a literal * or *:* in Actions and skips BuiltInRole.

Inventory each role assignment and the control-plane operations its principals actually need, including delegated automation; draft a complete role definition retaining unrelated permissions and replacing the wildcard with explicit allowed Actions.
Have the RBAC owner apply the reviewed role definition by the same role ID, then test dependent principals at each assignable scope before retiring legacy access paths.
Re-read the role definition and rerun azure.claude.iam_custom_role_no_wildcard_actions; review DataActions separately because this predicate does not inspect them.
remediation_details.summary: Replace the exact custom Azure RBAC role control-plane wildcard with reviewed required Actions.

checks.rationale: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator passes when the httpApplicationRouting add-on is absent or disabled and fails when it is enabled.
checks.description: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator passes when the httpApplicationRouting add-on is absent or disabled and fails when it is enabled.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the add-on is absent or disabled.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the HTTP application routing add-on is enabled.

checks.title: AKS Key Vault Secrets Store CSI driver enables secret rotation
checks.remediation: Enable the azureKeyvaultSecretsProvider add-on with enableSecretRotation set to true.
checks.rationale: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when `properties.addonProfiles.azureKeyvaultSecretsProvider.config.enableSecretRotation` is 'false'. Security defects can remain undetected or unpatched.
checks.description: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when `properties.addonProfiles.azureKeyvaultSecretsProvider.config.enableSecretRotation` is 'false'. Security defects can remain undetected or unpatched.
checks.pass_when: PASS when `properties.addonProfiles.azureKeyvaultSecretsProvider.config.enableSecretRotation` is 'true'.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when `properties.addonProfiles.azureKeyvaultSecretsProvider.config.enableSecretRotation` is 'false'.

checks.title: AKS enables the Container Insights (omsagent) add-on with a workspace
checks.remediation: Enable the monitoring add-on with a Log Analytics workspace.
checks.rationale: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when the `omsagent` add-on is disabled or lacks a non-null config object. Cluster logs and metrics may not be sent to monitoring.
checks.description: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when the `omsagent` add-on is disabled or lacks a non-null config object. Cluster logs and metrics may not be sent to monitoring.
checks.pass_when: PASS when `omsagent` is enabled and has a config object.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the `omsagent` add-on is disabled or lacks a non-null config object.

checks.title: AKS public API server restricts authorized IP ranges
checks.remediation: Configure apiServerAccessProfile.authorizedIPRanges or make the cluster private.
checks.rationale: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when a public API endpoint has no `authorizedIPRanges`. Unrestricted API reachability increases the chance of credential attacks against the control plane.
checks.description: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when a public API endpoint has no `authorizedIPRanges`. Unrestricted API reachability increases the chance of credential attacks against the control plane.
checks.pass_when: PASS when a public API endpoint has at least one authorized IP range.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when a public API endpoint has no `authorizedIPRanges`.
checks.not_applicable_when: The AKS API endpoint is private.

checks.title: AKS node pools allow at least 50 pods per node
checks.remediation: Create node pools with maxPods of 50 or more; maxPods cannot be changed on an existing pool.
checks.rationale: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when any agent pool sets `maxPods` below 50. Low pod density can force unnecessary node expansion and reduce workload placement flexibility.
checks.description: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when any agent pool sets `maxPods` below 50. Low pod density can force unnecessary node expansion and reduce workload placement flexibility.
checks.pass_when: PASS when every agent pool permits at least 50 pods per node.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when any agent pool sets `maxPods` below 50.

controls.framework: NIS2 - Network and Information Security Directive (Directive (EU) 2022/2555)

checks.remediation: Create node pools without enableNodePublicIP and publish workloads through load balancers or ingress.
checks.rationale: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when `properties.agentPoolProfiles[].enableNodePublicIP` is true. Untrusted network paths can reach the service or workload.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when `properties.agentPoolProfiles[].enableNodePublicIP` is true.

checks.title: AKS node pools enable encryption at host
checks.remediation: Create node pools with enableEncryptionAtHost after registering the EncryptionAtHost feature.
checks.rationale: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when any agent pool lacks `enableEncryptionAtHost=true`. Node temporary disks and cache data can remain outside host encryption protection.
checks.description: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when any agent pool lacks `enableEncryptionAtHost=true`. Node temporary disks and cache data can remain outside host encryption protection.
checks.pass_when: PASS when every agent pool enables encryption at host.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when any agent pool lacks `enableEncryptionAtHost=true`.

checks.title: AKS OS and data disks use a customer-managed disk encryption set
checks.remediation: Create the cluster with diskEncryptionSetID referencing a disk encryption set backed by a Key Vault key.
checks.rationale: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when `properties.diskEncryptionSetID` is null or absent. AKS node disks lack a specified customer-managed encryption key.
checks.description: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when `properties.diskEncryptionSetID` is null or absent. AKS node disks lack a specified customer-managed encryption key.
checks.pass_when: PASS when a nonempty disk encryption set ID is configured.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when `properties.diskEncryptionSetID` is null or absent.

checks.title: AKS uses the Azure CNI network plugin
checks.remediation: Use Azure CNI (optionally overlay or Cilium dataplane) for VNet-integrated pod networking and policy support.
checks.rationale: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when `properties.networkProfile.networkPlugin` is 'kubenet' or 'none'. Untrusted network paths can reach the service or workload.
checks.description: For an AKS cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when `properties.networkProfile.networkPlugin` is 'kubenet' or 'none'. Untrusted network paths can reach the service or workload.
checks.pass_when: PASS when `properties.networkProfile.networkPlugin` is 'azure'.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when `properties.networkProfile.networkPlugin` is 'kubenet' or 'none'.

checks.title: NSG does not allow unrestricted outbound traffic on all ports
checks.remediation: Restrict the flagged NSG all-port internet outbound Allow path with reviewed egress rules and priority.

caveats: Azure default AllowInternetOutBound cannot be removed or changed; a higher-priority custom rule can override it. Lower numeric priority means earlier evaluation.

The native predicate uses the source prefix and all destination ports, with priority-aware shadowing. It does not prove that all effective outbound paths are restricted or inspect Azure Firewall routing.

A broad outbound Deny can break updates, identity, monitoring and application dependencies; the owner must validate required Allow rules and rollback first. The reviewed priority must not collide with existing rules.

references.title: Azure CLI NSG rule list and update

steps: Inspect exposed_rules for the NSG Outbound direction and compare the all-port AllowInternetOutBound default rule at priority 65001 with existing higher-priority custom rules.
Inventory required destination prefixes, protocols and ports for attached workloads; establish explicit higher-priority Allow rules for approved egress and an owner-tested rollback.

Create an owner-approved custom outbound Deny for the remaining Internet destination with priority below 65001 in numeric value, after required narrower Allows. Do not attempt to edit or delete the Azure default rule.
Validate application egress and effective NSG rules, recollect the NSG and rerun this exact outbound check.

checks.title: Subscription-scoped activity log alert exists for Create Policy Assignment
checks.remediation: Create or correct the subscription-scoped activity log alert for Create Policy Assignment in category Administrative.

caveats: The evaluator accepts an alert declaration matching operationName=Microsoft.Authorization/policyAssignments/write and category=Administrative; it does not prove events are emitted, action groups exist, recipients receive notifications or the alert has been tested.

Subscription scope must match the finding exactly; resource-group-only scope and non-Global alert locations do not pass. An operationName match may coexist with other conditions, so the owner must verify intended specificity.
A PUT replaces the alert resource definition. Review the complete body, action group, retention and rollback before applying; creating an alert can incur monitoring charges and notification volume.

checks.remediation: Enable MySQL flexible-server audit logging on the flagged server.

remediation_details.summary: Enable MySQL flexible-server audit logging on the flagged server.
steps: Inspect the exact MySQL flexible server's configurations[] entry for audit_log_enabled; compare properties.value with the native predicate and confirm the server version offers this parameter.

Ask the database owner to test clients, logging or operational effects; set audit_log_enabled to ON through the reviewed server-parameter change route and respect the parameter's dynamic/static restart behavior.
Read back audit_log_enabled, verify the intended workload or log behavior, recollect this server and rerun azure.claude.mysql_flexible_audit_log_enabled.

cli.label: Inspect audit_log_enabled on the exact server
cli.code: az mysql flexible-server parameter show --resource-group <RESOURCE_GROUP> --server-name <SERVER_NAME> --name audit_log_enabled --subscription <SUBSCRIPTION_ID>

cli.label: Set reviewed audit_log_enabled value
cli.code: az mysql flexible-server parameter set --resource-group <RESOURCE_GROUP> --server-name <SERVER_NAME> --name audit_log_enabled --value ON --subscription <SUBSCRIPTION_ID>

caveats: The native predicate reads the collected configurations[] entry named audit_log_enabled, not effective client behavior or diagnostic delivery. Missing metadata yields UNKNOWN; an unrecognized value remains UNKNOWN.

Enabling audit logging can affect performance and collect sensitive SQL text; choose audited users/events with the owner. MySqlAuditLogs export requires a separate diagnostic setting, which this predicate does not test.

remediation_details.summary: Include CONNECTION events in the flagged MySQL flexible-server audit selection.
steps: Inspect audit_log_events on the exact server. The native predicate uppercases comma-separated tokens and fails only when CONNECTION is absent; it does not require audit_log_enabled=ON or prove log delivery.

With the database owner, add CONNECTION to the existing reviewed audit event selection without dropping required event types; separately confirm audit_log_enabled and the MySqlAuditLogs diagnostic destination.
Read back audit_log_events, verify an authorized connection produces an audit event in the intended sink, recollect and rerun this check.

cli.label: Inspect audit event selection
cli.code: az mysql flexible-server parameter show --resource-group <RESOURCE_GROUP> --server-name <SERVER_NAME> --name audit_log_events --subscription <SUBSCRIPTION_ID>

caveats: A replacement --value would overwrite the entire event list; no universal set command is supplied because existing required events are unknown.
Connection auditing can add volume and sensitive metadata. Preserve existing event types and user filters, then test routing independently of this narrow predicate.
Missing audit_log_events yields UNKNOWN; CONNECTION_V2 alone does not satisfy this exact CONNECTION matcher even if it records connection events.

caveats: Private endpoints require the Premium tier and can incur Azure Private Link charges. The endpoint Region must match its VNet, though it may differ from the namespace Region.
Do not approve a connection solely because it is Pending; confirm its private endpoint ID, owner and intended subnet. An Approved status alone does not prove DNS or message delivery.
Creating a private endpoint does not automatically disable the namespace public path. Test DNS and clients before separately changing publicNetworkAccess.

checks.title: Storage key expiration policy is exactly 90 days
checks.remediation: Set the flagged storage account key rotation reminder to exactly 90 days, after confirming both access keys have creation timestamps.

remediation_details.summary: Set the flagged storage account key rotation reminder to exactly 90 days, after confirming both access keys have creation timestamps.
steps: Inspect properties.keyPolicy.keyExpirationPeriodInDays on the exact storage account. This check requires exactly 90 days; an absent policy fails.

Inspect properties.keyCreationTime for key1 and key2. If either timestamp is null, plan staged rotation with the application owners before setting a reminder; update clients and SAS tokens in a controlled sequence.

Set the account key expiration reminder to 90 days, then recollect the account and confirm the evaluator field. Monitor actual key age separately; setting a reminder does not rotate or expire a key automatically.

cli.label: Inspect policy and both key creation timestamps
Set the key rotation reminder to 90 days after prerequisites

caveats: This key expiration policy is a reminder and compliance signal, not automatic rotation or revocation. A passing policy does not prove that either account key is younger than 90 days.

Older accounts may lack key creation timestamps; Microsoft requires rotating both keys at least once before creating the policy. Rotating a key can invalidate account and service SAS tokens signed by that key and break clients; migrate or coordinate first.

checks.title: Storage account access keys were regenerated within 90 days
frameworks: Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue C5

controls.framework: Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue C5

checks.remediation: Rotate only the flagged Azure Storage account key older than 90 days through a staged client and SAS migration.

remediation_details.summary: Rotate only the flagged Azure Storage account key older than 90 days through a staged client and SAS migration.
steps: Inspect properties.keyCreationTime for key1 and key2 on the exact account and use key_age_days to identify keys older than 90 days. If no creation times are reported, the native check is NOT_APPLICABLE; a malformed timestamp is UNKNOWN.

Inventory each client and account/service SAS signed with the aged key. Move those clients to the alternate key or Microsoft Entra authentication, prepare secure distribution of the replacement key, and validate access before regeneration.

Regenerate only the aged key after the alternate path is working, deliver the new value through the approved secret-management workflow without logging it, then update clients and SAS tokens. Repeat for the other key only after its clients have migrated; recollect creation timestamps and rerun.

cli.label: Read key creation times without listing secret values
Regenerate only the staged aged key and suppress secret output
cli.code: az storage account keys renew --account-name <STORAGE_ACCOUNT_NAME> --resource-group <RESOURCE_GROUP> --subscription <SUBSCRIPTION_ID> --key <REVIEWED_PRIMARY_OR_SECONDARY> --output none

caveats: Regenerating a key revokes access for clients and account or service SAS tokens signed by that key. Do not rotate both keys together; plan client migration, secret distribution and rollback with the account owner.

The renew command returns secret material unless output is suppressed. Never paste key values into a finding, shell history, ticket or report; use the approved secure secret-management channel to retrieve and distribute them.
The native predicate checks declared keyCreationTime ages, not whether shared-key authentication is enabled or whether all applications have moved to Microsoft Entra authentication.

checks.title: Storage account denies by default and declares virtual network rules
checks.remediation: Allow only reviewed client subnets through Azure Storage service endpoints and set the flagged account firewall default to Deny.

remediation_details.summary: Allow only reviewed client subnets through Azure Storage service endpoints and set the flagged account firewall default to Deny.
steps: Inspect properties.networkAcls.defaultAction and properties.networkAcls.virtualNetworkRules on the exact account. The native predicate fails if defaultAction is not Deny or there are no VNet rules; it does not validate rule IDs or endpoint health.

Identify all authorized clients, exceptions and break-glass access. Enable the Microsoft.Storage service endpoint on each reviewed client subnet, then add those subnet IDs as account VNet rules while preserving existing IP, resource-instance and trusted-service access decisions.
Test access from authorized and unauthorized locations before setting defaultAction=Deny. Recollect and rerun this declaration check; verify effective network access separately.

cli.label: Add a reviewed subnet rule after its service endpoint is enabled
Deny all other public network sources after client validation

caveats: Changing defaultAction to Deny can immediately block applications, monitoring or portal data operations. Stage allowed subnet rules first, test a rollback and coordinate with network and storage owners.

Storage service endpoints still use the public Storage endpoint; a VNet rule is distinct from a private endpoint. The native check only counts declared VNet rules and defaultAction, not effective connectivity.
The Microsoft.Storage endpoint may need a matching regional or global configuration and can alter subnet routing; confirm network owner requirements and storage account region.

remediation_details.summary: Resolve each unapproved private endpoint connection on the flagged Azure Storage account and verify the intended service links work.
steps: Inspect every properties.privateEndpointConnections[].properties.privateLinkServiceConnectionState.status on the exact account. This check fails if the list is empty or any status is not Approved; it does not identify which storage service a connection serves.

For an empty list, create the service-specific private endpoint and DNS integration required by authorized clients. For Pending, have the storage owner verify the endpoint resource ID, subnet and requester before approving that exact connection.

For Rejected or Disconnected connections, diagnose the underlying endpoint and owner intent, restore or recreate needed connectivity, and have the owner retire only confirmed stale connection records through a separate change. Re-read all statuses, test data operations and DNS, recollect and rerun.

cli.label: Inspect every storage private endpoint connection and status
Approve only a verified Pending connection as account owner

caveats: The native predicate requires every connection record to report Approved; an abandoned Rejected or Disconnected record can keep it failing even if another endpoint works. Do not delete a record merely to satisfy the check without validating ownership and service impact.
Approved status does not prove correct subresource, private DNS or application access. Some accounts need separate blob, dfs, file, queue, table or web endpoints.
Never approve an unexpected private endpoint request. Inspect the exact endpoint ID, requesting owner and subnet; Private Link and DNS changes can affect clients and incur charges.
The Azure CLI storage private-endpoint-connection approval command group is marked Preview; verify command availability and permissions in the operator environment before relying on it.

checks.remediation: Restrict the flagged Azure Files service to AES-256-GCM SMB channel encryption after validating every client supports it.

remediation_details.summary: Restrict the flagged Azure Files service to AES-256-GCM SMB channel encryption after validating every client supports it.
steps: Confirm type=fileServices and inspect properties.protocolSettings.smb.channelEncryption on the exact account. This native predicate requires the semicolon-separated configured set to contain only AES-256-GCM; unset means the service default permits every supported cipher.

Inventory SMB clients and test AES-256-GCM negotiation with their owners, especially older Windows and Linux clients. Microsoft requires supported Windows clients to select AES_256_GCM in their SMB client cipher configuration when this is the only server cipher. Plan a maintenance window and rollback before changing the account-wide File service setting.
Set only the SMB channel-encryption list to AES-256-GCM after client validation; verify mount and read/write access from representative clients, recollect the File service, and rerun this check.

caveats: This changes the File service SMB channel cipher list for all classic file shares in the account and may disconnect clients that cannot negotiate AES-256-GCM; Microsoft documents Windows support beginning with Windows Server 2022 and Windows 11. Validate other operating systems separately.

SMB channel encryption is distinct from Kerberos ticket encryption and from requiring encryption in transit. This check evaluates only the configured channelEncryption list and does not prove a client's negotiated cipher.

Ask the workspace owner to inventory pipelines, pools, linked services, managed private endpoints, approved Microsoft Entra tenants, data dependencies and required egress before designing a replacement workspace with managed virtual network and data exfiltration protection enabled at creation.

Data exfiltration protection restricts egress through managed private endpoints and approved tenants; it does not control ingress. Existing linked services, pipelines and SQL or Spark workloads may need changes, and some activities have documented limitations.

checks.title: Launch template default version requires IMDSv2
checks.remediation: The default EC2 launch-template version has MetadataOptions.HttpTokens other than required, allowing new instances from that version to use IMDSv1.

caveats: Launch-template versions are immutable, so no existing version is modified. A new default affects only consumers that follow default; pinned version references and already running instances need separate review.

cli.label: Inspect all versions and the current default
Create an owner-reviewed replacement version from the current default
Promote only the validated new version

iac.code: For LaunchTemplateId set the new DefaultVersionNumber only after its Versions.DefaultVersion LaunchTemplateData.MetadataOptions.HttpTokens=required and all inherited settings are validated; roll out consumers and existing instances separately.
iac.label: Review complete launch-template owner definition

steps: Inspect the exact LaunchTemplateId and resolve its DefaultVersionNumber and MetadataOptions.HttpTokens.
Have the workload owner review all metadata clients and a complete new launch-template version with HttpTokens=required, preserving other approved launch settings.
Create the reviewed new version, inspect it, promote it to default and validate newly launched instances; separately migrate existing instances.
remediation_details.summary: The default EC2 launch-template version has MetadataOptions.HttpTokens other than required, allowing new instances from that version to use IMDSv1.

checks.rationale: Flags an EC2 launch template when the default template version does not set `MetadataOptions.HttpTokens` to `required`. It can expose the instance to unauthorized access, unsafe configuration drift, or loss of operational control.
checks.description: Flags an EC2 launch template when the default template version does not set `MetadataOptions.HttpTokens` to `required`. It can expose the instance to unauthorized access, unsafe configuration drift, or loss of operational control.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when the default template version does not set `MetadataOptions.HttpTokens` to `required`.

checks.title: Launch template default version encrypts EBS volumes
checks.remediation: At least one EBS block-device mapping in the default EC2 launch-template version lacks Encrypted=true, so new volumes from that mapping may be unencrypted.

caveats: A default version without block-device mappings is NOT_APPLICABLE under this check. Version changes do not re-encrypt existing volumes or alter consumers pinned to an older version.

cli.label: Inspect all versions and the current default
Create an owner-reviewed replacement version from the current default
Promote only the validated new version

iac.code: For each default LaunchTemplateData.BlockDeviceMappings Ebs.Encrypted setting, create a new encrypted version for LaunchTemplateId and change DefaultVersionNumber only after KMS, boot and pinned-consumer testing.
iac.label: Review complete launch-template owner definition

steps: Inspect the current default version and every BlockDeviceMappings Ebs.Encrypted field, volume source and KMS key choice.
Have the storage and workload owners review a complete replacement launch-template version with encrypted EBS mappings, approved KMS access and boot compatibility.
Create and inspect the new version, promote it to default, then test new-instance launch and volume encryption; migrate existing unencrypted volumes separately.
remediation_details.summary: At least one EBS block-device mapping in the default EC2 launch-template version lacks Encrypted=true, so new volumes from that mapping may be unencrypted.

checks.rationale: Flags an EC2 launch template when an EBS mapping in the default template version lacks `Encrypted` true. It weakens protection of stored data and may leave key access outside the intended customer control.

checks.pass_when: PASS when all EBS mappings in the default version are encrypted.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when an EBS mapping in the default template version lacks `Encrypted` true.
checks.not_applicable_when: When the default launch template version has no block device mapping list.

checks.title: Every launch template version requires IMDSv2 or disables IMDS
checks.remediation: Review every launch template version that callers may select; set HttpTokens=required with HttpEndpoint=enabled, or explicitly disable the metadata endpoint, and update dependent launch settings after owner review.
checks.rationale: For every version in the complete collected launch-template version inventory, checks the explicit MetadataOptions declaration. An enabled endpoint with optional tokens fails; an explicitly disabled endpoint or enabled endpoint with required tokens is safe. Omitted or unrecognized options remain UNKNOWN because effective instance metadata settings can inherit account and AMI defaults. This does not test running instances or the separate default-version predicate.
checks.description: For every version in the complete collected launch-template version inventory, checks the explicit MetadataOptions declaration. An enabled endpoint with optional tokens fails; an explicitly disabled endpoint or enabled endpoint with required tokens is safe. Omitted or unrecognized options remain UNKNOWN because effective instance metadata settings can inherit account and AMI defaults. This does not test running instances or the separate default-version predicate.
checks.pass_when: The complete version inventory is nonempty and every version explicitly disables the endpoint or enables it with required tokens.
checks.fail_when: Any collected version explicitly enables the metadata endpoint with optional tokens, even if another version is safe or a different version is default.

checks.remediation: A launch template version sets a NetworkInterfaces.AssociatePublicIpAddress value to true, so launches from that version can request a public IPv4 address.

caveats: The evaluator fails if any version sets AssociatePublicIpAddress=true; an existing ENI reference makes it UNKNOWN because that ENI public association is not joined. Creating one safe version does not remove old unsafe versions or change running instances.

iac.code: For LaunchTemplateId, declare NetworkInterfaces.AssociatePublicIpAddress=false in every version permitted for launches, inspect referenced NetworkInterfaceId associations and migrate all version consumers.
iac.label: Review EC2 launch template no public ip owner declaration

steps: Inspect LaunchTemplateId, all Versions, each NetworkInterfaces AssociatePublicIpAddress value and references to existing NetworkInterfaceId resources.
Have the workload and network owners select private subnets, outbound access, load-balancer paths and a revised launch-template version; identify ASG/fleet version consumers.
Create a reviewed version with public IPv4 association disabled, promote it only after launch testing and migrate consumers away from unsafe older versions.
remediation_details.summary: A launch template version sets a NetworkInterfaces.AssociatePublicIpAddress value to true, so launches from that version can request a public IPv4 address.

checks.title: Instances launched from the launch template do not associate public IPs
checks.remediation: An EC2 instance tagged with this LaunchTemplateId records AssociatePublicIpAddress=true in its launched network-interface template data.

caveats: Templates with no tagged instance are NOT_APPLICABLE. The source joins instance tags and historical GetLaunchTemplateData; a new template version alone does not change previously launched instances or prove their current public-IP state.

iac.code: For LaunchTemplateId, replace tagged instances whose instance.LaunchTemplateData.NetworkInterfaces.AssociatePublicIpAddress=true using a reviewed private-network version and validate current addresses.

steps: Inspect LaunchTemplateId, tagged instances and each instance LaunchTemplateData.NetworkInterfaces.AssociatePublicIpAddress value.
Have workload and network owners design a private replacement launch path, determine current public IP dependencies and test the revised template.
Replace the affected instance through an approved rolling/blue-green cutover, then confirm the new instance launch data and address are private.

checks.remediation: An applicable EC2 network interface has SourceDestCheck=false, allowing routed traffic that does not originate from or terminate at the interface.

Enable checking only on an approved operator-controlled interface

Have the network owner determine whether this ENI is an approved NAT, firewall, router or service-owned interface that requires forwarding; preserve that design or request a policy exception.
For an operator-controlled ENI with no forwarding role, enable source/destination checking and verify workload packet flow and health.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when a supported network interface type has `SourceDestCheck` false.

checks.fail_when: An IPv4 world-source ingress rule omits FromPort, declares another port, or spans a range.

checks.remediation: An account-owned VPC has no flow log or at least one of its FlowLogStatus values is not ACTIVE.

caveats: This check skips VPCs owned by another account; it fails if any associated log is not ACTIVE even when another is healthy. A newly created log does not repair an existing failed one.

iac.code: Declare VpcId-level FlowLogId, ResourceId, destination, TrafficType, retention and delivery role; verify FlowLogStatus=ACTIVE operationally.
iac.label: Review VPC flow logs active declaration

steps: Inspect the VpcId and all associated FlowLogId, ResourceId and FlowLogStatus values, including FAILED delivery and ownership.
Have the network and logging owners choose traffic type, CloudWatch Logs or S3 destination, retention, KMS access, IAM delivery role and expected cost.
Create a reviewed VPC flow log if absent; repair a failed destination or delivery role and verify every VPC flow log becomes ACTIVE.
remediation_details.summary: An account-owned VPC has no flow log or at least one of its FlowLogStatus values is not ACTIVE.

checks.rationale: For an owned VPC, fails when no flow log is declared or any associated flow log has FlowLogStatus other than ACTIVE. A mixed ACTIVE and FAILED set fails by pinned source parity; this checks health of every declared log rather than merely existence of one active log.
checks.description: For an owned VPC, fails when no flow log is declared or any associated flow log has FlowLogStatus other than ACTIVE. A mixed ACTIVE and FAILED set fails by pinned source parity; this checks health of every declared log rather than merely existence of one active log.
checks.pass_when: The owned VPC has at least one associated flow log and every declared log is ACTIVE.
checks.fail_when: The owned VPC has no flow log, or at least one associated log is not ACTIVE.
checks.not_applicable_when: The VPC is owned by another account.

checks.remediation: A VPC containing a network interface has no flow-log record whose ResourceId equals its VpcId.

caveats: This in-use check accepts a flow-log record regardless of FlowLogStatus; failed delivery still needs operational repair. A VPC without network interfaces is not applicable.

Have the network and logging owners approve traffic type, destination, retention, KMS and delivery role for that used VPC.
Create the reviewed VPC flow log and inspect its delivery status and records after activation.

checks.title: VPC has at least one subnet
checks.remediation: A VPC VpcId has no matching subnet.VpcId in the collected subnet inventory.

caveats: The check does not establish that an empty VPC is unsafe. Creating a token subnet in an unused VPC adds cost/management burden and is not an appropriate response.

iac.code: If the VpcId is retained for workloads, declare a subnet with owner-approved CIDR, Availability Zone, route table and network controls; otherwise remove it through a dependency-reviewed retirement plan.
iac.label: Review VPC vpc has subnets declaration

steps: Inspect the VPC purpose, CIDR allocation, routes, dependencies and whether it is intentionally empty or being decommissioned.
Have the network owner either approve an appropriate subnet CIDR and Availability Zone for a needed VPC or decommission the unused VPC through a separate dependency-reviewed plan.
Create the approved subnet only when workloads need it, then verify its VpcId and effective route-table association.
remediation_details.summary: A VPC VpcId has no matching subnet.VpcId in the collected subnet inventory.

checks.rationale: Flags a VPC when no subnet has a matching VpcId. The VPC cannot host workload interfaces until a subnet is created.
checks.description: Flags a VPC when no subnet has a matching VpcId. The VPC cannot host workload interfaces until a subnet is created.
checks.pass_when: PASS when no subnet has a matching VpcId is false.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when no subnet has a matching VpcId.

checks.title: VPC has subnets in more than one Availability Zone
checks.remediation: A VPC has subnets in zero or one distinct AvailabilityZone.

caveats: The check covers every VPC, including an empty or intentionally single-zone VPC; a second empty subnet alone does not make workloads resilient. AZ-specific capacity and cross-zone traffic may add cost.

iac.code: Declare VpcId subnets with distinct AvailabilityZone values and separate owner-approved CIDRs; map workload replicas and failover to both zones.
iac.label: Review VPC subnets in multiple azs declaration

references.title: Official VPC subnets in Availability Zones

steps: Inspect the VpcId, existing subnet AvailabilityZone values, CIDR capacity and deployed workload placement.
Have the network and application owners approve a second zone, subnet CIDR, routes, security controls, service support and capacity; plan workload migration or redundant placement.
Create the reviewed second-zone subnet and deploy or migrate workload capacity into it, then verify both zones in inventory and service health.
remediation_details.summary: A VPC has subnets in zero or one distinct AvailabilityZone.

checks.rationale: Flags a VPC when its subnets span at most one distinct AvailabilityZone. A single zone outage can remove all subnet capacity for the VPC.

checks.title: VPC has both public and private subnets
checks.remediation: A VPC lacks a mix of public and private subnets under the native route-table classification.

caveats: The native classification calls a default route to either igw- or nat- public, although NAT normally provides outbound-only access; classify actual ingress separately. An empty VPC fails, and a token pair of subnets is not workload segmentation. Route changes can interrupt running applications; subnet count and routing classification alone do not prove isolation.

iac.code: Declare VpcId subnet tiers with explicit route_table.Associations and Routes.DestinationCidrBlock/GatewayId or NatGatewayId aligned to owner-approved public and private workloads; verify actual ingress and egress.
iac.label: Review VPC public and private subnets declaration

references.title: Official VPC public and private subnet example

steps: Inspect VpcId, all subnet associations and effective main or explicit route tables; map existing public listeners and internal workloads.
Have network and service owners design distinct subnet tiers, ingress paths, private egress through NAT/endpoints, CIDRs, security controls and workload placement.
Create or migrate to owner-approved subnet and route declarations, verify route paths and application connectivity from both tiers.
remediation_details.summary: A VPC lacks a mix of public and private subnets under the native route-table classification.

checks.rationale: Flags a VPC when its subnet inventory lacks both public and private subnets under the Turbot route classification. Workloads cannot be separated cleanly between internet-facing and private network tiers.
checks.description: Flags a VPC when its subnet inventory lacks both public and private subnets under the Turbot route classification. Workloads cannot be separated cleanly between internet-facing and private network tiers.
checks.pass_when: PASS when its subnet inventory lacks both public and private subnets under the Turbot route classification is false.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when its subnet inventory lacks both public and private subnets under the Turbot route classification.

iac.code: Declare VpcId subnet tiers with explicit route_table.Associations and Routes.DestinationCidrBlock/GatewayId or NatGatewayId aligned to owner-approved public and private workloads; verify actual ingress and egress.

checks.remediation: Subnet MapPublicIpOnLaunch is true, so new instances can receive a public IPv4 address by default.

caveats: This setting affects future launches; it does not remove public addresses already allocated to running interfaces. Disabling the default can break bootstrap or connectivity for workloads that rely on a public address.

iac.label: Review VPC subnet no auto public ip declaration

steps: Inspect SubnetId, MapPublicIpOnLaunch, current public IPs, launch templates and applications requiring inbound reachability.
Have the network and service owners arrange private endpoints, load balancers or other approved access paths before changing the launch default.
Disable automatic public IPv4 assignment and verify the subnet attribute; review existing public interfaces separately.
remediation_details.summary: Subnet MapPublicIpOnLaunch is true, so new instances can receive a public IPv4 address by default.
