checks.title: Account has VPCs in more than one region
checks.remediation: An account VPC inventory has VpcId records in zero or one Region.

caveats: The source counts VPC records across collected Regions and fails empty inventory; it does not prove workloads or data are resilient. Inventory must cover all enabled Regions; a token empty VPC in another Region would satisfy the count without useful recovery.

cli.label: Inspect VPCs in each approved Region

iac.code: Declare AccountId-approved VpcId resources in two required Region values, plus workload/data replication, routing, DNS and failover evidence; avoid an empty compliance-only VPC.
iac.label: Review second-Region VPC and recovery design

steps: Inspect the complete enabled-Region VPC inventory, owner account IDs, workload dependencies and actual recovery objectives.
Have application, data and network owners design a second-Region landing zone, addressing, connectivity, replication, recovery tests and cost based on the service continuity requirement.
Deploy the reviewed regional infrastructure and workload/data recovery path, test failover, and verify VpcId records in two Regions.
remediation_details.summary: An account VPC inventory has VpcId records in zero or one Region.

checks.rationale: Flags the account VPC inventory when VPCs occur in at most one Region. A regional incident can affect all deployed VPC network capacity.
checks.description: Flags the account VPC inventory when VPCs occur in at most one Region. A regional incident can affect all deployed VPC network capacity.
checks.pass_when: PASS when VPCs occur in at most one Region is false.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when VPCs occur in at most one Region.

checks.title: Account has non-default VPCs in more than one region
checks.remediation: An account with VPCs has non-default VpcId records in zero or one Region.

caveats: This branch ignores default VPCs and is not applicable when the account has no VPCs. A second empty VPC is not a disaster-recovery capability; workloads, data, replication, DNS and failover need independent review.

cli.label: Inspect VPCs in each approved Region

iac.code: Declare AccountId-approved VpcId resources in two required Region values with IsDefault=false, plus workload/data replication, routing, DNS and failover evidence; avoid an empty compliance-only VPC.
iac.label: Review second-Region VPC and recovery design

steps: Inspect the complete enabled-Region VPC inventory, owner account IDs, IsDefault flags, workload dependencies and actual recovery objectives.
Have application, data and network owners design a second-Region landing zone, addressing, connectivity, replication, recovery tests and cost based on the service continuity requirement.
Deploy the reviewed regional infrastructure and workload/data recovery path, test failover, and verify VpcId records in two Regions with IsDefault=false.
remediation_details.summary: An account with VPCs has non-default VpcId records in zero or one Region.

checks.rationale: Flags the account VPC inventory when non-default VPCs occur in at most one Region. A regional incident can affect all deployed VPC network capacity.
checks.description: Flags the account VPC inventory when non-default VPCs occur in at most one Region. A regional incident can affect all deployed VPC network capacity.

checks.remediation: An Internet Gateway InternetGatewayId has an empty Attachments list.

caveats: The source only checks whether any attachment exists; it does not verify an authorized VPC. Attaching a gateway enables a possible internet path only when routes and controls allow it, and should not be done merely to clear an unused-resource finding.

iac.code: Declare InternetGatewayId ownership and an approved Attachments[*].VpcId only for VPCs needing an internet path; decommission unused gateways through owner-managed IaC.
iac.label: Review VPC igw attached declaration

steps: Inspect InternetGatewayId, attachments, tags, intended VPC and any IaC or change record reserving the gateway.
Have the network owner decide whether the detached gateway is a staged dependency, should be attached to an approved VPC or should be retired.
If approved for active internet access, attach it to the reviewed VPC and verify routes and security controls; otherwise retire through the managed configuration after dependency review.
remediation_details.summary: An Internet Gateway InternetGatewayId has an empty Attachments list.

checks.rationale: Flags an internet gateway when it has zero VPC attachments. An unattached gateway is unused infrastructure and can hide stale network design or later unintended exposure.
checks.description: Flags an internet gateway when it has zero VPC attachments. An unattached gateway is unused infrastructure and can hide stale network design or later unintended exposure.

checks.remediation: A route table contains an IPv4 or IPv6 default route whose GatewayId starts with igw.

caveats: The source flags an authorized public route table as well as an unintended private route. A blanket route removal can cut off public load balancers, NAT instances, patching or egress; this template offers inspection only until the exact route is approved.

iac.code: Declare RouteTableId Routes[*].DestinationCidrBlock and GatewayId so only owner-approved public subnet tables have a default igw route; private tables use reviewed NAT/endpoints as needed.
iac.label: Review VPC route table no default igw route declaration

steps: Inspect RouteTableId, all subnet/main associations, default routes and the applications served by each associated subnet.
Have network and application owners classify the table as intentionally public or private and design replacement private access if any default IGW route is unapproved.
Remove or replace only the reviewed unapproved IGW default route in a maintenance change, then validate workload connectivity and effective subnet routing.
remediation_details.summary: A route table contains an IPv4 or IPv6 default route whose GatewayId starts with igw.

checks.rationale: Flags a route table when a route sends 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to an internet gateway. Subnets using the table gain a path to the public internet.
checks.description: Flags a route table when a route sends 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to an internet gateway. Subnets using the table gain a path to the public internet.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when a route sends 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 to an internet gateway.

checks.title: VPC Block Public Access blocks internet gateway traffic
checks.remediation: Regional VPC Block Public Access InternetGatewayBlockMode is neither block-ingress nor block-bidirectional.

caveats: This is a Region-wide setting; block-bidirectional also blocks outbound internet-gateway paths, while block-ingress permits certain NAT and egress-only flows. Existing public services may fail unless exclusions and alternate paths are ready. The check reads only the mode, not exclusion safety.

iac.code: Declare VpcBlockPublicAccessOptions.InternetGatewayBlockMode as block-ingress or block-bidirectional for the Region, with separately reviewed exclusions and connectivity tests.
iac.label: Review VPC block public access igw declaration

steps: Inspect the regional InternetGatewayBlockMode, existing VPC/subnet exclusions, public ingress dependencies and required outbound paths.
Have network, application and security owners approve block-ingress or block-bidirectional mode and narrowly scoped exclusions with a tested rollback plan.
Apply the approved regional mode during a maintenance window and verify connectivity and the new option state.
remediation_details.summary: Regional VPC Block Public Access InternetGatewayBlockMode is neither block-ingress nor block-bidirectional.

checks.rationale: Flags the regional VPC Block Public Access configuration when VpcBlockPublicAccessOptions.InternetGatewayBlockMode is neither block-bidirectional nor block-ingress. Internet gateway traffic can reach VPCs without an account-level block.
checks.description: Flags the regional VPC Block Public Access configuration when VpcBlockPublicAccessOptions.InternetGatewayBlockMode is neither block-bidirectional nor block-ingress. Internet gateway traffic can reach VPCs without an account-level block.
checks.pass_when: PASS when VpcBlockPublicAccessOptions.InternetGatewayBlockMode is neither block-bidirectional nor block-ingress is false.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when VpcBlockPublicAccessOptions.InternetGatewayBlockMode is neither block-bidirectional nor block-ingress.

frameworks: AWS HIPAA Final Omnibus Security Rule 2013

checks.remediation: VPC VpcId must match a collected endpoint VpcId whose ServiceName exactly equals the regional ec2 service name; no match means that endpoint was not found.

caveats: The evaluator compares exact service names and VPC IDs only; a pending, failed or wrong-type endpoint can still satisfy it. Subnet and security group IDs are operator-supplied, not finding evidence; endpoint creation incurs cost and may conflict with DNS or egress design.

cli.label: Inspect endpoints in the exact VPC
Create after VPC and service owner review

iac.code: Console/IaC fields to compare in the owned resource and referenced inventory: VpcId / vpc_endpoint[].VpcId,ServiceName. Declare the com.amazonaws.<REGION>.ec2 Interface endpoint with reviewed subnet, security group and private DNS choices in the existing VPC IaC. Confirm dependent workloads use the intended path before treating the endpoint as operational.
iac.label: Add the endpoint to the VPC owner declaration

steps: Inspect all endpoint VpcId and ServiceName values for the exact regional com.amazonaws.<REGION>.ec2 service, and identify the VPC owner and existing private DNS design.
Create an owner-reviewed Interface endpoint for ec2 in approved subnets and security groups; validate private DNS, connection paths and cost before changing production clients.
Recollect VPC endpoint inventory and rerun this exact check; test application access because this predicate does not evaluate endpoint state or type.
remediation_details.summary: VPC VpcId must match a collected endpoint VpcId whose ServiceName exactly equals the regional ec2 service name; no match means that endpoint was not found.

checks.rationale: Flags a VPC when no inventoried VPC endpoint in that VPC has ServiceName matching the regional ec2 service. Clients may need public or NAT routes to reach ec2, increasing exposure and dependency on internet egress.

checks.title: Gateway VPC endpoint policy does not allow * to everyone unconditionally
checks.remediation: A Gateway endpoint policy has an unconditional Allow with wildcard Principal and Action exactly *.

caveats: The source only fails an Allow whose normalized Action list is exactly [*], with wildcard principal and no Condition. Other broad forms may pass, and a condition key alone is not proof of effective restriction. Updating the endpoint policy replaces the complete document and can disrupt authorized traffic.

iac.code: Declare VpcEndpointId PolicyDocument.Statement[*].Principal, Action, Resource and Condition as a full owner-approved policy scoped to actual endpoint callers; preserve required access.
iac.label: Review gateway endpoint access policy

steps: Inspect VpcEndpointId, VpcEndpointType and the complete PolicyDocument, identifying exact Allow statements and legitimate S3 or DynamoDB callers.
Have the network, storage and application owners approve narrower principals, actions, resource ARNs or fixed conditions while preserving required cross-account workflows.
Apply the complete reviewed replacement policy and test allowed and denied endpoint requests before removing fallback access.
remediation_details.summary: A Gateway endpoint policy has an unconditional Allow with wildcard Principal and Action exactly *.

checks.rationale: Flags a gateway VPC endpoint when its policy unconditionally Allows Action * to a wildcard principal. The endpoint policy does not constrain which service operations can traverse the gateway.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when its policy unconditionally Allows Action * to a wildcard principal.
checks.not_applicable_when: The endpoint is not a Gateway endpoint.

checks.title: VPC endpoint policy Allow principals are bound to the audited account
frameworks: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) v1.1
National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) v2.0

controls.framework: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) v1.1
National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) v2.0

checks.remediation: Restrict endpoint policy Allow principals to the audited account, or add a positive condition that binds aws:PrincipalAccount or the account field of aws:PrincipalArn to it.
checks.rationale: For each collected VPC endpoint policy, tests whether every Allow principal names the audited account or is limited by a positive condition on aws:PrincipalAccount or the account field of aws:PrincipalArn. An unconditional foreign or wildcard Allow fails unless a Deny interaction makes the boundary unresolved. Direct principals must use supported identity ARN forms; StringLike PrincipalArn proof requires a literal prefix through the account field, while ArnLike uses ARN component matching. Source or VPC restrictions, unsupported principal or condition shapes, and malformed facts remain UNKNOWN. This tests the declared account boundary, not effective endpoint access.
checks.description: For each collected VPC endpoint policy, tests whether every Allow principal names the audited account or is limited by a positive condition on aws:PrincipalAccount or the account field of aws:PrincipalArn. An unconditional foreign or wildcard Allow fails unless a Deny interaction makes the boundary unresolved. Direct principals must use supported identity ARN forms; StringLike PrincipalArn proof requires a literal prefix through the account field, while ArnLike uses ARN component matching. Source or VPC restrictions, unsupported principal or condition shapes, and malformed facts remain UNKNOWN. This tests the declared account boundary, not effective endpoint access.
checks.pass_when: Every Allow statement has only audited-account AWS principals or a proven positive condition binding its principal account to the audited account, with no unresolved statement.
checks.fail_when: A collected Allow statement unconditionally names a wildcard or foreign AWS principal and no Deny statement can alter that grant.
checks.not_applicable_when: The endpoint has no policy.

checks.title: Account-owned VPC endpoint service requires connection acceptance
checks.remediation: An account-owned VPC endpoint service has AcceptanceRequired=false.

caveats: This setting governs new connection requests and does not retroactively revoke existing accepted connections. AWS-owned services are not applicable. Switching to manual acceptance can delay legitimate consumer onboarding.

iac.code: Declare account-owned ServiceId with AcceptanceRequired=true and a documented endpoint consumer approval workflow, preserving legitimate existing connections.
iac.label: Review VPC endpoint service acceptance required declaration

steps: Inspect ServiceId, Owner, AcceptanceRequired, current allowed principals and pending or accepted endpoint connections.
Have the service and consumer owners establish an approval process and review the impact on future consumer connections.
Require connection acceptance on the exact service and verify its setting; approve future connection requests only after consumer review.
remediation_details.summary: An account-owned VPC endpoint service has AcceptanceRequired=false.

checks.rationale: Flags an endpoint service owned by the audited account when AcceptanceRequired is false. Other principals allowed by the service can connect without explicit owner approval.
checks.description: Flags an endpoint service owned by the audited account when AcceptanceRequired is false. Other principals allowed by the service can connect without explicit owner approval.
checks.pass_when: PASS when AcceptanceRequired is false is false.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when AcceptanceRequired is false.
checks.not_applicable_when: The endpoint service is not owned by the audited account.

checks.title: Account-owned VPC endpoint service allows only the audited account
checks.remediation: An account-owned VPC endpoint service AllowedPrincipals list includes a wildcard or another account.

caveats: The native rule treats every nonlocal principal as untrusted because no trusted-account allowlist is configured; it cannot decide business authorization. Removing permission prevents new connections and may affect established consumers; review them before change.

iac.code: Declare ServiceId AllowedPrincipals as an owner-approved trust list, and document any authorized cross-account exception rather than deleting it solely to satisfy this predicate.
iac.label: Review VPC endpoint service principals trusted declaration

steps: Inspect the exact ServiceId permissions and current endpoint consumers; map every AllowedPrincipals ARN to its owner and business purpose.
Have the service and consumer owners decide which cross-account principals should remain and prepare a reviewed removal set, preserving approved connections and future onboarding.
Remove only reviewed untrusted principals and verify the remaining list and consumer connectivity.
remediation_details.summary: An account-owned VPC endpoint service AllowedPrincipals list includes a wildcard or another account.

checks.rationale: Flags an endpoint service owned by the audited account when AllowedPrincipals includes * or a principal from another account. The service can be consumed by untrusted accounts.

steps: Inspect the exact peering connection Status.Code, both VPC owners, approved connection purpose and associated routes.
Have both network owners decide whether a pending/inactive connection is needed and whether a cross-account link is explicitly authorized under the trust model.
Complete or retire the owner-approved connection and adjust route and security group access through a separate reviewed change; verify Status.Code and both OwnerId values.

caveats: This is operational tunnel state, not proof of application reachability. Unexpected telemetry shape yields UNKNOWN; an AWS-side tunnel option change can cause replacement and traffic interruption, so no blind modify command is offered.

steps: Inspect VpnConnectionId, both tunnel OutsideIpAddress and Status values, CloudWatch metrics, BGP status and customer gateway device logs.
Have the network and customer-gateway owners investigate IKE proposals, pre-shared key storage, route advertisements, firewall reachability and maintenance events without exposing key material.

remediation_details.summary: A Site-to-Site VPN connection has exactly two VgwTelemetry records but fewer than two have Status=UP.

checks.rationale: Flags a VPN connection when VpnConnection.Telemetry has two tunnels but fewer than two report Status UP. One failed tunnel removes redundancy; two failures interrupt the private link.

checks.title: Site-to-Site VPN connection has tunnel logging enabled
checks.remediation: Neither VPN tunnel has Options.TunnelOptions.LogOptions.CloudWatchLogOptions.LogEnabled=true.

caveats: The native check passes when only one tunnel logs, so it does not prove both are covered. ModifyVpnTunnelOptions changes one tunnel at a time and may replace or interrupt it; the full reviewed request must preserve IKE and pre-shared-key settings without exposing secrets in this template.

iac.code: Declare VpnConnectionId TunnelOptions[*].LogOptions.CloudWatchLogOptions.LogEnabled=true for each approved tunnel with encrypted CloudWatch destination, retention and documented maintenance impact.

steps: Inspect both tunnel logging flags, current outside IP addresses, tunnel options and the approved CloudWatch log group and access policy.
Have network and logging owners approve destination retention, KMS, data handling, cost and the possibility that tunnel-option changes replace a tunnel.
Apply a complete reviewed option document to one chosen tunnel during a maintenance window and verify its logging flag and log delivery; extend to the other tunnel for actual coverage.
remediation_details.summary: Neither VPN tunnel has Options.TunnelOptions.LogOptions.CloudWatchLogOptions.LogEnabled=true.

checks.rationale: Flags a VPN connection when none of its tunnel options has logging enabled. Tunnel failures and negotiation events may be unavailable for diagnosis.
checks.description: Flags a VPN connection when none of its tunnel options has logging enabled. Tunnel failures and negotiation events may be unavailable for diagnosis.
checks.pass_when: PASS when none of its tunnel options has logging enabled is false.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when none of its tunnel options has logging enabled.

checks.title: Network Firewall has deletion protection enabled
checks.remediation: Network Firewall DeleteProtection is false, so deletion of this firewall is not blocked by the service protection flag.

caveats: DeleteProtection guards the firewall resource only; it does not protect route tables, policies or subnets. A stale UpdateToken must trigger re-read and review rather than an unconditional retry.

steps: Inspect the exact FirewallArn, DeleteProtection value, deployment ownership and current UpdateToken.
Have the firewall owner approve enabling deletion protection and record an emergency maintenance process that can explicitly disable it.
Apply the conditional update with the fresh token, then verify DeleteProtection=true and ordinary firewall traffic remains healthy.
remediation_details.summary: Network Firewall DeleteProtection is false, so deletion of this firewall is not blocked by the service protection flag.

checks.rationale: Fails when an AWS Network Firewall has DeleteProtection set to false. Without it a single DeleteFirewall call (by mistake or by an attacker) removes inspection and filtering for the protected VPC.

steps: Inspect the exact FirewallArn, SubnetChangeProtection setting, current subnet mappings and UpdateToken.

remediation_details.summary: Network Firewall SubnetChangeProtection is false, allowing subnet associations to change without this service guard.

checks.rationale: Fails when an AWS Network Firewall has SubnetChangeProtection set to false. Unprotected subnet associations can be changed to move the firewall endpoints, letting traffic bypass inspection.

checks.fail_when: SubnetChangeProtection is false.

caveats: Users with only inactive keys are not applicable. The source uses the user-owned key list to avoid name-prefix joins; key last-used data is delayed and cannot by itself prove an active key is unused. Do not print secret key material.

iac.code: Declare UserName AccessKeys.items[*].AccessKeyId/Status rotation with at most one Active key, tested consumer migration and a separate retirement schedule.
iac.label: Review IAM user one active key declaration

references.title: Official IAM update access key API

steps: Inspect the user and both active AccessKeyId records, last-used evidence and all consuming workloads without exposing secret access keys.
Have the application and identity owners select a replacement path, migrate consumers to a single newer key or temporary role and test it before disabling the surplus key.
Set only the reviewed surplus key to Inactive, observe workload health and verify at most one Active key remains.
remediation_details.summary: An IAM user has more than one AccessKeys.items entry with Status=Active.

checks.rationale: Counts the access keys of an IAM user with Status Active and fails when there are more than one. Two active keys usually means a rotation was never finished, doubling the number of live long-lived secrets.
checks.description: Counts the access keys of an IAM user with Status Active and fails when there are more than one. Two active keys usually means a rotation was never finished, doubling the number of live long-lived secrets.
checks.pass_when: Exactly one access key is Active.
checks.fail_when: Two or more access keys are Active.
checks.not_applicable_when: The user has no Active access key.

checks.title: IAM access key was created less than 365 days before the captured date
checks.remediation: An IAM access key CreateDate is at or before the captured UTC date minus 365 days, regardless of Status.

caveats: This check includes inactive keys, so rotation of a different key does not erase the old finding. CreateDate age and delayed last-used data do not prove a key is safe to remove; no secret value is displayed or embedded.

cli.label: Inspect last use of old key

iac.code: Declare AccessKeyId/UserName/Status/CreateDate rotation evidence, role migration or replacement secret handling, and owner-approved retirement of obsolete keys.
iac.label: Review IAM access key age 365 declaration

steps: Inspect AccessKeyId, UserName, Status, CreateDate and last-used metadata, then locate every consumer through the owner inventory.
If active, have the service owner migrate to an IAM role or a newly created key via the approved secret store and verify the workload; if inactive, confirm retention or retirement policy.
After migration, deactivate the old active key and verify the replacement; retire stale inactive metadata through a separately approved credential lifecycle.
remediation_details.summary: An IAM access key CreateDate is at or before the captured UTC date minus 365 days, regardless of Status.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM access key when an IAM access key was created on or before the UTC date 365 days before the snapshot. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.description: Flags an IAM access key when an IAM access key was created on or before the UTC date 365 days before the snapshot. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.pass_when: PASS when its creation date is newer than the 365-day cutoff.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when an IAM access key was created on or before the UTC date 365 days before the snapshot.

checks.title: IAM user with AdministratorAccess attached has an MFA device
checks.remediation: An IAM user with an attached AdministratorAccess policy has no MFADevices.items entry.

caveats: The source matches an attached policy name AdministratorAccess and tests only device presence, not actual challenge enforcement. MFA activation needs user/device participation; no copied CLI command should carry seed material.

iac.code: Declare UserName privileged role model, attached AdministratorAccess disposition and MFADevices.items enrollment with recovery controls; test sign-in challenge separately.
iac.label: Review IAM admin user has mfa declaration

steps: Inspect the exact AdministratorAccess attachment and the user MFA device inventory without retrieving activation codes or secrets.
Have the identity owner select a supported phishing-resistant or other approved MFA device and plan recovery for the administrator account.
Enroll and verify MFA with the user through the approved IAM console/device process, or replace the direct AdministratorAccess grant with a reviewed privileged role.
remediation_details.summary: An IAM user with an attached AdministratorAccess policy has no MFADevices.items entry.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM user when a user with AdministratorAccess attached has no MFA device. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.description: Flags an IAM user when a user with AdministratorAccess attached has no MFA device. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.pass_when: PASS when that administrator user has at least one MFA device.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when a user with AdministratorAccess attached has no MFA device.
checks.not_applicable_when: When the IAM user has no AdministratorAccess attachment.

checks.title: IAM role does not have AdministratorAccess attached
frameworks: AWS CIS Compute Services Benchmark v1.0.0

controls.framework: AWS CIS Compute Services Benchmark v1.0.0

checks.remediation: An IAM role has an attached managed policy whose name is AdministratorAccess.

caveats: The source matches policy name after the slash, so an unrelated customer policy with that name can also fail. Detachment immediately affects every session after policy propagation; do not assume any permission is unused.

cli.label: Detach exact reviewed administrator-named policy ARN

iac.code: Declare RoleName AttachedManagedPolicies without direct AdministratorAccess after a full owner-reviewed replacement and recovery access test.
iac.label: Review IAM role no administrator access declaration

steps: Inspect RoleName, trust policy, attached AdministratorAccess ARN, all role assumers and actual required operations.
Have workload and IAM owners create and test a scoped replacement policy and retain a break-glass role with documented approvals.
Detach the exact AdministratorAccess policy only after the replacement is attached and tested; verify effective role permissions and workload health.
remediation_details.summary: An IAM role has an attached managed policy whose name is AdministratorAccess.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM role when the evaluated IAM role has AdministratorAccess attached. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.description: Flags an IAM role when the evaluated IAM role has AdministratorAccess attached. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the evaluated IAM role has no AdministratorAccess attachment.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the evaluated IAM role has AdministratorAccess attached.

checks.title: IAM role with ReadOnlyAccess is not assumable from other accounts
checks.remediation: A role with the exact ReadOnlyAccess managed policy ARN trusts a wildcard or another account in an Allow statement.

caveats: The native source treats any foreign account as a finding even when formally approved and checks only Principal.AWS in Allow statements. Its string containment test can mistake an account ID embedded in a longer principal value for a restriction; review the full trust document.

iac.code: Declare RoleName AssumeRolePolicyDocument.Statement[*].Principal.AWS as a complete reviewed trust policy, preserving approved read-only cross-account workflows by explicit exception.
iac.label: Review IAM role readonly not cross account declaration

steps: Inspect RoleName, the exact ReadOnlyAccess attachment, full AssumeRolePolicyDocument and every cross-account reader or service dependency.
Have both account owners approve named principals, external ID or organization conditions where appropriate, and a complete replacement trust document.
Apply the reviewed trust policy, test approved cross-account access and confirm no wildcard or unintended account remains.
remediation_details.summary: A role with the exact ReadOnlyAccess managed policy ARN trusts a wildcard or another account in an Allow statement.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM role when a role with ReadOnlyAccess trusts `*` or an AWS account other than its own. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.description: Flags an IAM role when a role with ReadOnlyAccess trusts `*` or an AWS account other than its own. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the role has no such external trust.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when a role with ReadOnlyAccess trusts `*` or an AWS account other than its own.
checks.not_applicable_when: When ReadOnlyAccess is not attached to the role.

checks.title: IAM role was used after the captured date minus 60 days
checks.remediation: An IAM role has no recorded RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate or its last use is at least 60 days old at the captured date.

caveats: AWS last-used tracking has a limited window and can omit rare or indirect use; an absent timestamp is not proof the role is safe to delete. The native check measures the captured date at UTC midnight, not a live utilization guarantee.

cli.label: Inspect role metadata and last use

iac.code: Declare RoleName ownership and RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate evidence with scheduled-use and disaster-recovery exceptions; retire only through a dependency-reviewed change.
iac.label: Review IAM role used within 60 days declaration

steps: Inspect RoleName, RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate, trust policy, IaC references, scheduled jobs and service-linked or recovery use.
Have each owning service confirm whether the role is dormant but needed for failover, or can be retired after a bounded observation period.
For approved retirement, remove dependencies through the owner-managed deployment and archive role policy/trust evidence before a separate decommission; otherwise document the justified exception.
remediation_details.summary: An IAM role has no recorded RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate or its last use is at least 60 days old at the captured date.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM role that has no RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate or whose last use is at or before the cutoff of 60 days before the collection midnight. Dormant roles keep their permissions and trust relationships and are a quiet persistence or takeover target nobody is watching.
checks.description: Flags an IAM role that has no RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate or whose last use is at or before the cutoff of 60 days before the collection midnight. Dormant roles keep their permissions and trust relationships and are a quiet persistence or takeover target nobody is watching.
checks.pass_when: RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate is later than the 60-day cutoff.
checks.fail_when: RoleLastUsed.LastUsedDate is absent (never used or not tracked) or is on/before the 60-day cutoff.

checks.title: IAM role trust policy does not allow any principal without a restricting condition
checks.remediation: An IAM role trust policy has a wildcard principal Allow without a source-recognized restrictive condition.

caveats: The native public-policy helper is a bounded classifier, not full IAM satisfiability. A condition key or account digits inside an arbitrary string are not sufficient proof of a trust boundary; service principals need service-specific SourceArn semantics.

iac.code: Declare RoleName/Arn AssumeRolePolicyDocument.Statement[*].Principal, Action and Condition in a full owner-approved trust document with fixed source bounds, service compatibility tests and rollback.
iac.label: Review IAM role trust role trust not public declaration

steps: Inspect RoleName and the complete trust policy, including every wildcard principal, STS action and condition value.

Have the role and calling-service owners replace the wildcard principal with named accounts, services or roles and fixed, validated aws:SourceAccount/SourceArn/PrincipalOrgID conditions where applicable.
Apply a complete reviewed trust policy, test authorized assumptions and confirm the broad Allow is removed.
remediation_details.summary: An IAM role trust policy has a wildcard principal Allow without a source-recognized restrictive condition.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM role whose AssumeRolePolicyDocument has an Allow statement with a wildcard principal ("*" or AWS "*") that is not narrowed by a StringEquals/StringLike (no '*') or ARN condition on aws:SourceOwner, aws:SourceAccount, aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:PrincipalAccount, aws:PrincipalArn or aws:SourceArn. Such a trust policy lets any AWS account call sts:AssumeRole and obtain the role's permissions.
checks.description: Flags an IAM role whose AssumeRolePolicyDocument has an Allow statement with a wildcard principal ("*" or AWS "*") that is not narrowed by a StringEquals/StringLike (no '*') or ARN condition on aws:SourceOwner, aws:SourceAccount, aws:PrincipalOrgID, aws:PrincipalAccount, aws:PrincipalArn or aws:SourceArn. Such a trust policy lets any AWS account call sts:AssumeRole and obtain the role's permissions.
checks.pass_when: No Allow statement in the trust policy has an unrestricted wildcard principal.
checks.fail_when: At least one Allow trust statement names a wildcard principal without one of the recognised account/organization/ARN restricting condition keys.

checks.remediation: An IAM group GroupName has no matching iam_user.GroupList membership.

caveats: An empty group does not currently confer membership permissions. Adding a user merely to clear the finding can create excessive access, and future identity automation may still reference the group.

iac.code: Declare GroupName purpose and iam_user.GroupList membership only for approved users; preserve staged or recovery exceptions and retire obsolete groups through managed configuration.
iac.label: Review IAM group not empty declaration

steps: Inspect GroupName, attached policies, intended job function, current user membership and provisioning references.
Have the identity owner decide whether the group is a staged entitlement, a dormant recovery group or an obsolete object.
If needed, add only a reviewed eligible user through the identity workflow; if obsolete, retire the group and its policies through a separate dependency-reviewed plan.
remediation_details.summary: An IAM group GroupName has no matching iam_user.GroupList membership.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM group when an IAM group has no users. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.description: Flags an IAM group when an IAM group has no users. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the group contains at least one user.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when an IAM group has no users.

checks.title: Root account with a console password has MFA enabled
checks.remediation: The root account has AccountPasswordPresent=1 but AccountMFAEnabled=0.

caveats: Only root with a console password is in scope; the flags do not prove the quality or phishing resistance of the device. Root MFA enrollment requires root sign-in and device possession; no device secret or activation code belongs in copied CLI.

iac.code: Declare SummaryMap.AccountPasswordPresent and AccountMFAEnabled governance for root credentials, MFA custody, recovery and periodic access review.
iac.label: Review IAM root console has mfa declaration

steps: Inspect the account summary flags and identify the root credential custodian and documented break-glass recovery process.
Have the account owner enroll an approved hardware or virtual MFA device through the root console with secure recovery and multiple custodians as policy requires.
Verify the next account summary has AccountMFAEnabled=1 and test the root emergency sign-in procedure under supervision.
remediation_details.summary: The root account has AccountPasswordPresent=1 but AccountMFAEnabled=0.

checks.rationale: Uses the IAM account summary to flag an account whose root user has a console password (AccountPasswordPresent = 1) while AccountMFAEnabled = 0. A root password without MFA means one phished or reused password gives unrestricted control of the whole account.
checks.description: Uses the IAM account summary to flag an account whose root user has a console password (AccountPasswordPresent = 1) while AccountMFAEnabled = 0. A root password without MFA means one phished or reused password gives unrestricted control of the whole account.
checks.pass_when: The root user has no password, or AccountMFAEnabled is 1.
checks.fail_when: AccountPasswordPresent is 1 and AccountMFAEnabled is 0.

checks.title: Region has an active IAM Access Analyzer with no findings
checks.remediation: The audited Region has no active IAM Access Analyzer, has an analyzer outside ACTIVE status, or has one or more active findings.

caveats: The collector requests only ACTIVE findings from ListFindingsV2; archived and resolved records are outside the normal collected branch. The scope check fails if any collected analyzer is inactive, and it does not decide whether a finding is legitimate. No blanket archive or policy rewrite command is supplied because those require resource-specific owner review.

cli.label: Inspect analyzers in the audited Region
Inspect ACTIVE findings for the reviewed analyzer
Create an owner-approved account analyzer only if none exists

iac.code: Declare an active access_analyzer for the audited Region with a documented account or organization zone of trust; review Findings[] under the ACTIVE ListFindingsV2 filter and track each resource policy owner decision separately.
iac.label: Review regional analyzer declaration

references.title: Official IAM Access Analyzer finding review
Official IAM Access Analyzer creation API

steps: List analyzers in the exact audited Region and inspect each status and zone of trust; collect active finding IDs and affected resource permissions.

If no analyzer exists, have the IAM owner approve and create an ACCOUNT analyzer. For an inactive analyzer, investigate its status before creating another. For active findings, review the actual access and resource owner before narrowing permissions or archiving explicitly intended access.
Recollect analyzer status and ACTIVE-filtered findings; verify there are no unresolved active findings and retain evidence for any approved archived exception.
remediation_details.summary: The audited Region has no active IAM Access Analyzer, has an analyzer outside ACTIVE status, or has one or more active findings.

checks.rationale: Checks the regional IAM Access Analyzer inventory. The evaluator fails when it is empty, any analyzer is not ACTIVE, or any collected Findings row is present. Standard live collection requests only ACTIVE findings; archived or resolved findings outside that filter are not assessed.
checks.description: Checks the regional IAM Access Analyzer inventory. The evaluator fails when it is empty, any analyzer is not ACTIVE, or any collected Findings row is present. Standard live collection requests only ACTIVE findings; archived or resolved findings outside that filter are not assessed.
checks.pass_when: PASS when at least one analyzer exists, every analyzer has status ACTIVE, and no collected Findings row is present. Standard live collection does not assess archived or resolved findings.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when no analyzer exists, any analyzer has status other than ACTIVE, or any collected Findings row is present regardless of that row's status. Standard live collection normally supplies only ACTIVE findings.

checks.title: Console password is used within 45 days of the captured date (Steampipe)
checks.remediation: A non-root IAM principal has an enabled console password with no use or a last-use timestamp before the captured UTC date minus 45 days.

caveats: This branch fails a never-used enabled password, uses a strict before-midnight cutoff and skips root. Credential-report use data can lag; inactivity is not proof access can be removed.

iac.code: Declare user console password_enabled lifecycle with reviewed password_last_used evidence, SSO migration and emergency-access exception; avoid revoking access solely from a delayed timestamp.
iac.label: Review IAM console password used 45 lifecycle declaration

steps: Inspect the non-root user, password_enabled and password_last_used fields; distinguish a never-used password from one older than the captured UTC midnight minus 45 days.
Confirm with the identity owner whether the console user remains required for support, recovery or a planned SSO migration; check delayed sign-in reporting.
After a tested alternate sign-in is ready, retire only the approved dormant login profile through the identity lifecycle and verify the user still has intended access.
remediation_details.summary: A non-root IAM principal has an enabled console password with no use or a last-use timestamp before the captured UTC date minus 45 days.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM credential-report row when a console-enabled user has no recorded password use or last used it before the 45-day UTC cutoff. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.description: Flags an IAM credential-report row when a console-enabled user has no recorded password use or last used it before the 45-day UTC cutoff. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the user last used the console password within 45 days.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when a console-enabled user has no recorded password use or last used it before the 45-day UTC cutoff.
checks.not_applicable_when: When the credential-report row is for the root principal.

checks.remediation: A non-root IAM user has an enabled console password whose recorded last use, or last change when never used, is more than 45 whole days old.

caveats: A never-used enabled password passes only while password_last_changed is no more than 45 whole days old; older passwords fail and unavailable change age is UNKNOWN. The Steampipe-style sibling fails never-used passwords immediately. Credential-report use data can lag.

iac.code: Declare user console password_enabled lifecycle with reviewed password_last_used and password_last_changed evidence, SSO migration and emergency-access exception; avoid revoking access solely from a delayed timestamp.
iac.label: Review IAM prowler console password used 45 lifecycle declaration

steps: Inspect the non-root user, password_enabled, password_last_used and password_last_changed; age a never-used enabled password from its last change, with missing age UNKNOWN.
Ask the identity owner to review service need, delayed sign-in reporting and SSO migration for passwords whose recorded use or never-used change age exceeds 45 whole days.
Retire a confirmed dormant login profile only after alternate access is tested, then verify sign-in policy and downstream workflows.
remediation_details.summary: A non-root IAM user has an enabled console password whose recorded last use, or last change when never used, is more than 45 whole days old.

checks.rationale: Checks non-root IAM users with a console password against a 45-whole-day age limit. Recorded use is aged from password_last_used. A never-used password is aged from password_last_changed: it passes during the grace period and fails once that age exceeds 45 whole days. A user without a console password passes; unavailable required age or snapshot-clock evidence is UNKNOWN.
checks.description: Checks non-root IAM users with a console password against a 45-whole-day age limit. Recorded use is aged from password_last_used. A never-used password is aged from password_last_changed: it passes during the grace period and fails once that age exceeds 45 whole days. A user without a console password passes; unavailable required age or snapshot-clock evidence is UNKNOWN.
checks.pass_when: No console password is enabled, or recorded password use is no more than 45 whole days old, or a never-used password was last changed no more than 45 whole days ago.
checks.fail_when: An enabled console password was last used more than 45 whole days ago, or a never-used enabled password was last changed more than 45 whole days ago.
checks.not_applicable_when: When the credential-report row is for the root principal.

checks.remediation: An active access key slot has access_key_1_last_rotated or access_key_2_last_rotated more than 90 whole days before capture.

caveats: The source includes the root row and uses credential-report slots, not stable AccessKeyId identifiers. A newly rotated different key does not clear an old active slot; secret values must stay in the approved secret store.

iac.code: Declare user access_key_1_active/access_key_2_active rotation and last-used evidence with real AccessKeyId owner mapping, role migration and tested rollback.
iac.label: Review IAM access keys rotated 90 lifecycle declaration

steps: Inspect each active credential-report slot and its last_rotated time; map the slot to a real AccessKeyId without exposing the secret value.
Have the service owner rotate the key through the secret store or replace long-lived credentials with a role, then test every consumer and recovery path.
Deactivate the old key after successful cutover and verify no active slot exceeds the 90-day threshold at the next report.
remediation_details.summary: An active access key slot has access_key_1_last_rotated or access_key_2_last_rotated more than 90 whole days before capture.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM credential-report row when an active key was last rotated more than 90 whole days ago. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.description: Flags an IAM credential-report row when an active key was last rotated more than 90 whole days ago. It can expand identity privileges, expose credentials, or make unused access available to an attacker.
checks.pass_when: PASS when every active key was rotated within 90 whole days.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when an active key was last rotated more than 90 whole days ago.

checks.remediation: An active access key slot has a recorded last use, or last rotation when never used, more than 45 whole days before capture.

caveats: A never-used active key is aged from its last rotation or creation: it passes through 45 whole days, fails when older, and is UNKNOWN when that age is unavailable. The separate initial-key check has a different predicate. The source includes root and last-used records can lag or omit rare recovery use.

iac.code: Declare user access_key_1_active/access_key_2_active rotation and last-used evidence with real AccessKeyId owner mapping, role migration and tested rollback.
iac.label: Review IAM access keys used 45 lifecycle declaration

steps: Inspect each active slot and its last_used_date and last_rotated fields; age a never-used N/A slot from last_rotated and map the slot to real key metadata.
Have the service owner verify delayed telemetry, scheduled or disaster-recovery use before declaring a stale key unnecessary.
Migrate any remaining consumers and deactivate only the reviewed stale key, then validate workloads and the next credential report.
remediation_details.summary: An active access key slot has a recorded last use, or last rotation when never used, more than 45 whole days before capture.

checks.rationale: Checks active IAM access keys against a 45-day age threshold. Recorded use is aged from last-used date; a never-used active key is aged from the credential report's last-rotated date, which records creation or last change of the current key. Missing required age evidence is UNKNOWN.
checks.description: Checks active IAM access keys against a 45-day age threshold. checks.remediation: An IAM server certificate Expiration is at or before the captured time.

caveats: The source compares the expiration instant and does not prove the certificate is currently served. IAM certificate replacement needs private-key handling outside copied commands; no key or certificate blob is embedded here. ACM cannot export an ACM-issued private key into IAM.

iac.code: Declare ServerCertificateName/Arn/Expiration inventory and consumer certificate ARN migration to a valid ACM or externally managed certificate, with PKI-controlled renewal and retirement.
iac.label: Review IAM server certificate not expired now declaration

steps: Inspect ServerCertificateName, Arn, Expiration and each live load balancer or CloudFront distribution that references the certificate.

Have the application and PKI owners obtain a valid replacement through ACM where supported, or a separately handled external certificate for legacy IAM storage; test hostname chains and renewal ownership.
Deploy the replacement to every consumer, verify TLS and rollback, then retire the expired IAM certificate only after no consumer references it.
remediation_details.summary: An IAM server certificate Expiration is at or before the captured time.

checks.rationale: Flags an IAM server certificate whose Expiration timestamp is at or before the current time. Expired certificates still attached to load balancers or CloudFront break TLS for clients and invite users to click through certificate warnings.

Enable only if the owner confirms the key remains needed

Disabled keys that are never scheduled for deletion are forgotten key material that still costs money and can be re-enabled by anyone with kms:EnableKey.
checks.description: For customer managed KMS keys, fails when KeyMetadata.Enabled is false and KeyState is not PendingDeletion (Steampipe kms_cmk_unused). checks.fail_when: Enabled is false and KeyState is anything other than PendingDeletion.

caveats: PutBucketLifecycleConfiguration replaces every existing rule; expiration and transition can incur irreversible data loss or cost. The predicate only counts enabled rules and does not assess whether the rule protects data.

cli.label: Apply the full owner-reviewed lifecycle rule set

iac.code: Set Lifecycle.Rules[*].Status to Enabled for a scoped, owner-approved rule while preserving all existing lifecycle rules and verifying retention, legal hold and noncurrent-version behavior.
iac.label: Review bucket lifecycle and versioning declaration

steps: Inspect every current lifecycle rule, its filters and data-retention obligations with the bucket owner.
Prepare a complete replacement configuration preserving approved rules and adding one scoped enabled rule with safe transition or expiration timing.
Apply the owner-reviewed configuration and verify an enabled rule without prematurely expiring current or noncurrent versions.
remediation_details.summary: The bucket has no lifecycle rule with Status Enabled, so no rule meets this configuration check.

checks.rationale: Fails when the bucket has no lifecycle rule with Status Enabled. Without lifecycle management, stale objects and old versions accumulate indefinitely, growing cost and the volume of data exposed in a breach.
checks.description: Fails when the bucket has no lifecycle rule with Status Enabled. Without lifecycle management, stale objects and old versions accumulate indefinitely, growing cost and the volume of data exposed in a breach.
checks.pass_when: At least one lifecycle rule is Enabled.
checks.fail_when: No lifecycle configuration exists or all rules are Disabled.

checks.title: Versioned S3 bucket has an enabled lifecycle rule
checks.remediation: A bucket with Versioning.Status=Enabled lacks an enabled lifecycle rule.

caveats: Unversioned and suspended buckets are NOT_APPLICABLE to this lifecycle check; separate versioning checks cover them.

Enabling versioning changes object version and delete behavior, adds storage cost and may need propagation time. Existing expiration rules can leave noncurrent versions indefinitely unless separately reviewed; lifecycle replacement can delete data.

cli.label: Apply the full owner-reviewed lifecycle rule set

iac.code: Set Versioning.Status to Enabled and preserve an owner-approved Lifecycle.Rules[*].Status Enabled rule in the complete lifecycle declaration; review noncurrent-version expiration, legal holds and cost.
iac.label: Review bucket lifecycle and versioning declaration

steps: Inspect the current versioning status and all lifecycle rules, including noncurrent-version retention requirements.
Have the bucket owner approve versioning and a complete lifecycle configuration, preserving existing rules and adding a safe enabled rule.
Enable versioning where needed, allow propagation, apply the full reviewed lifecycle document and verify both exact fields.
remediation_details.summary: A bucket with Versioning.Status=Enabled lacks an enabled lifecycle rule.

checks.rationale: Applies the lifecycle criterion only to buckets with Versioning.Status=Enabled. A version-enabled bucket without an enabled lifecycle rule fails; complete unversioned or suspended buckets are NOT_APPLICABLE and separate versioning checks cover them.
checks.description: Applies the lifecycle criterion only to buckets with Versioning.Status=Enabled. A version-enabled bucket without an enabled lifecycle rule fails; complete unversioned or suspended buckets are NOT_APPLICABLE and separate versioning checks cover them.
checks.pass_when: Versioning is Enabled and at least one lifecycle rule is Enabled.
checks.fail_when: Versioning is Enabled and no lifecycle rule is Enabled.
checks.not_applicable_when: Versioning is not Enabled, including suspended or unversioned buckets.

caveats: Object Lock is irreversible once enabled on a bucket, and versioning cannot then be suspended. The predicate checks configuration presence only, not retention duration, legal hold or whether any objects are locked. A bucket with Object Lock cannot be a server-access-logging destination.

cli.label: Apply legally approved Object Lock configuration

iac.code: Set ObjectLock.ObjectLockConfiguration through the owner-managed bucket declaration only after explicit retention/legal approval; set compatible Versioning.Status Enabled and validate irreversible Object Lock behavior.
iac.label: Review the S3 bucket owner declaration

steps: Inspect bucket versioning and Object Lock configuration, retention obligations, access logging dependencies and current object lifecycle.
Have the bucket, records and legal owners approve enabling Object Lock and any default-retention mode and period in a complete configuration.
Enable versioning if required, apply only the approved configuration, then verify the bucket response and protected-object behavior.
remediation_details.summary: The bucket has no ObjectLockConfiguration response, so the source finds no configured Object Lock.

checks.rationale: Fails when the bucket has no Object Lock configuration (GetObjectLockConfiguration returns none). Without Object Lock, objects can be deleted or overwritten by anyone with write access, so backups and logs are not protected as WORM data.
checks.description: Fails when the bucket has no Object Lock configuration (GetObjectLockConfiguration returns none). Without Object Lock, objects can be deleted or overwritten by anyone with write access, so backups and logs are not protected as WORM data.
checks.pass_when: An ObjectLockConfiguration is present.
checks.fail_when: The ObjectLock section is absent.

caveats: The source ignores URI-only group grants and is NOT_APPLICABLE when no grantee IDs exist; this is not a public-access conclusion. Disabling ACLs can break requests with custom ACLs or ACL-based cross-account access, and existing ACL grants may prevent enabling BucketOwnerEnforced until fixed.

cli.label: Inspect complete bucket ACL and owner

iac.code: Review Acl.Owner.ID and Acl.Grants[*].Grantee.ID, preserve approved owner and service grants, migrate external permissions to policies, then set OwnershipControls.OwnershipControls.Rules[*].ObjectOwnership to BucketOwnerEnforced only after owner signoff.
iac.label: Review bucket ACL and ownership declaration

references.title: AWS S3 Object Ownership and ACL migration

steps: Inspect Object Ownership, every bucket ACL grantee and the cross-account clients that rely on those grants.
Have the bucket owner migrate required access into reviewed IAM or bucket policies, preserving any log-delivery access and object-owner contracts.
Apply a complete ACL document without unintended canonical-user grants, then optionally enable BucketOwnerEnforced after prerequisite validation and verify clients.
remediation_details.summary: The bucket has ACLs enabled and at least one canonical-user grantee ID differs from Acl.Owner.ID.

checks.rationale: Fails when the bucket ACL grants permissions to canonical user IDs other than the bucket owner, unless Object Ownership is BucketOwnerEnforced (ACLs disabled). ACL grants to other canonical users are an access path outside IAM and bucket policy that is easy to miss in reviews.
checks.description: Fails when the bucket ACL grants permissions to canonical user IDs other than the bucket owner, unless Object Ownership is BucketOwnerEnforced (ACLs disabled). ACL grants to other canonical users are an access path outside IAM and bucket policy that is easy to miss in reviews.
checks.pass_when: ObjectOwnership is BucketOwnerEnforced, or every grantee ID equals the owner ID.
checks.fail_when: ACLs are enabled and a grant names a canonical user ID other than the owner.
checks.not_applicable_when: The ACL contains no grantee with a canonical user ID.

checks.title: S3 bucket ACL has no AuthenticatedUsers grant
checks.remediation: The bucket ACL grants at least one permission to the global AuthenticatedUsers group URI.

caveats: The predicate checks ACL grants directly and does not consider Block Public Access or effective routing. PutBucketAcl replaces the whole ACL; an unreviewed replacement can remove required owner, delivery or account grants.

cli.label: Inspect complete bucket ACL and owner

iac.code: Remove the AuthenticatedUsers URI from Acl.Grants[*].Grantee.URI in the full owner-reviewed bucket ACL declaration while preserving necessary Acl.Grants[*].Permission entries for known grantees.
iac.label: Review bucket ACL and ownership declaration

references.title: AWS S3 Object Ownership and ACL migration

steps: Inspect all ACL grants and confirm which principals and applications actually depend on the AuthenticatedUsers grant.
Have the bucket owner replace any intended access with explicit reviewed IAM or bucket policy statements and preserve required owner or service grants.
Apply a complete ACL document omitting AuthenticatedUsers and verify the group URI is absent while authorized clients still work.
remediation_details.summary: The bucket ACL grants at least one permission to the global AuthenticatedUsers group URI.

checks.rationale: Fails when the bucket ACL contains a grant to the global AuthenticatedUsers group (http://acs.amazonaws.com/groups/global/AuthenticatedUsers). That group means any AWS account holder anywhere, so the grant is effectively public access.
checks.description: Fails when the bucket ACL contains a grant to the global AuthenticatedUsers group (http://acs.amazonaws.com/groups/global/AuthenticatedUsers). That group means any AWS account holder anywhere, so the grant is effectively public access.
checks.pass_when: No grant targets the AuthenticatedUsers group.
checks.fail_when: At least one grant targets the AuthenticatedUsers group.

checks.title: S3 bucket Object Ownership is BucketOwnerEnforced (Prowler)
checks.remediation: The first bucket Object Ownership rule is absent or not BucketOwnerEnforced, so ACLs remain enabled under this check.

caveats: The source reads Rules[0] only; the presence of another rule is not accepted. BucketOwnerEnforced disables ACL evaluation and rejects custom ACL headers, so clients may fail until policies and uploads are migrated.

cli.label: Inspect complete bucket ACL and owner

iac.code: Set OwnershipControls.OwnershipControls.Rules[0].ObjectOwnership to BucketOwnerEnforced in the bucket declaration after ACL-to-policy migration and testing upload clients.
iac.label: Review bucket ACL and ownership declaration

references.title: AWS S3 Object Ownership and ACL migration

steps: Inspect the current ownership rule, bucket and object ACLs, request ACL headers and dependent cross-account writes.
Migrate ACL-dependent access to owner-reviewed IAM or bucket policies and remove incompatible bucket grants before changing Object Ownership.
Apply the complete approved BucketOwnerEnforced controls document, then verify new writes, object ownership and the first rule value.
remediation_details.summary: The first bucket Object Ownership rule is absent or not BucketOwnerEnforced, so ACLs remain enabled under this check.

checks.rationale: Fails when the first OwnershipControls rule's ObjectOwnership does not contain BucketOwnerEnforced, or when no ownership controls exist (Prowler). With ACLs enabled, object writers can retain ownership and grant access through ACLs that bypass the bucket policy.
checks.description: Fails when the first OwnershipControls rule's ObjectOwnership does not contain BucketOwnerEnforced, or when no ownership controls exist (Prowler). With ACLs enabled, object writers can retain ownership and grant access through ACLs that bypass the bucket policy.
checks.pass_when: OwnershipControls.Rules[0].ObjectOwnership contains BucketOwnerEnforced.
checks.fail_when: ObjectOwnership is BucketOwnerPreferred/ObjectWriter or the OwnershipControls configuration is absent.

caveats: The source counts any AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers ACL permission and Prowler-classified public policy; it does not prove current internet reachability. IgnorePublicAcls can make GetBucketAcl show effective rather than underlying grants, and block flags never delete existing grants. RestrictPublicBuckets may interrupt legitimate cross-account access.

iac.code: Review Acl.Grants[*].Grantee.URI and Policy.Policy.Statement alongside PublicAccessBlock.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.IgnorePublicAcls,RestrictPublicBuckets and account flags; preserve necessary access and apply a full owner-reviewed ACL/policy or block declaration.
iac.label: Review S3 public-access and ACL/policy declaration

references.title: AWS S3 Block Public Access behavior

steps: Inspect the account and bucket block settings, effective ACL grants and full bucket policy with the data and application owners.
Identify the actual public grant or policy statement, migrate any intentional public delivery to an approved private-origin or signed path, and approve complete replacement documents.
Remove the reviewed public ACL or policy grant and/or enable both bucket block flags, then verify the predicate and authorized clients.
remediation_details.summary: The bucket has a global-group ACL grant or public policy while neither bucket nor account has both IgnorePublicAcls and RestrictPublicBuckets enabled.

checks.rationale: Prowler public-bucket check: passes when the bucket's own block has IgnorePublicAcls and RestrictPublicBuckets; otherwise fails if the ACL grants anything to AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers or the bucket policy is public (is_policy_public), unless the account block has both settings. A public bucket exposes its objects to anyone on the internet.
checks.description: Prowler public-bucket check: passes when the bucket's own block has IgnorePublicAcls and RestrictPublicBuckets; otherwise fails if the ACL grants anything to AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers or the bucket policy is public (is_policy_public), unless the account block has both settings. A public bucket exposes its objects to anyone on the internet.
checks.pass_when: The bucket or account blocks public ACLs and policies, or there is no public group grant and no public policy.
checks.fail_when: A public group grant or public policy exists and neither the bucket nor the account has both IgnorePublicAcls and RestrictPublicBuckets.

caveats: The helper recognizes only FULL_CONTROL, READ and READ_ACP grants to two global groups. The block flags can mask but do not remove an underlying ACL grant; GetBucketAcl may show effective grants when IgnorePublicAcls is active.

Remove the group read grant or enable both bucket block flags, then verify list/read behavior and authorized access.

checks.rationale: Fails when the bucket ACL grants FULL_CONTROL, READ or READ_ACP to the AllUsers or AuthenticatedUsers group and neither the bucket nor the account has both IgnorePublicAcls and RestrictPublicBuckets. Such a grant lets anyone list the bucket's objects or read its ACL.

checks.pass_when: No public group grant has FULL_CONTROL/READ/READ_ACP, or public ACLs are neutralised at bucket or account level.
checks.fail_when: A public group grant with FULL_CONTROL/READ/READ_ACP is effective.

steps: Inspect the bucket ACL grants, complete policy, policy public status and bucket public-access-block flags; identify each proven public read grant and any condition requiring review.

Have the data and application owners approve private or signed replacement access, review mixed or patterned conditions separately, and prepare complete ACL or bucket policy documents preserving necessary grants.

checks.rationale: Steampipe public-read check: fails when an AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers grant with FULL_CONTROL, READ_ACP or READ exists without BlockPublicAcls, or when GetBucketPolicyStatus reports IsPublic, BlockPublicPolicy is off and an Allow Principal * statement grants *, *:*, s3:*, s3:get* or s3:list*. Public read exposes bucket contents to the internet.
checks.description: Steampipe public-read check: fails when an AllUsers/AuthenticatedUsers grant with FULL_CONTROL, READ_ACP or READ exists without BlockPublicAcls, or when GetBucketPolicyStatus reports IsPublic, BlockPublicPolicy is off and an Allow Principal * statement grants *, *:*, s3:*, s3:get* or s3:list*. Public read exposes bucket contents to the internet.
checks.pass_when: Public read ACL grants are blocked or absent, and the policy is not public, is blocked, or has no wildcard read statement.

checks.remediation: An S3 bucket policy Allow grants a different-account or wildcard AWS principal one of five exact bucket-permission-changing actions.

caveats: This native predicate compares five exact lowercased actions and does not match wildcard variants such as s3:*. It does not establish whether a cross-account administrator is malicious or unused; no grant should be removed without owner review.

iac.code: Review Policy.Policy.Statement[*].Effect, Principal.AWS and Action; constrain the five exact permission-changing Allows to named approved principals and conditions in a full owner-managed policy, preserving recovery administration.
iac.label: Review owner-managed bucket policy and blocks

references.title: AWS S3 Block Public Access behavior

steps: Inspect the complete policy, bucket owner account and the exact Allow statement granting DeleteBucketPolicy, PutBucketAcl, PutBucketPolicy, PutEncryptionConfiguration or PutObjectAcl.
Have the data and IAM owners identify authorized cross-account administration and replace broad principals with approved principals, scope and tested conditions.
Apply a complete reviewed policy document preserving required access, then verify the exact granting statements and bucket administration paths.
remediation_details.summary: An S3 bucket policy Allow grants a different-account or wildcard AWS principal one of five exact bucket-permission-changing actions.

checks.rationale: Fails when the bucket policy has an Allow statement whose AWS principal is * or an ARN from another account and whose actions include exactly s3:DeleteBucketPolicy, s3:PutBucketAcl, s3:PutBucketPolicy, s3:PutEncryptionConfiguration or s3:PutObjectAcl (wildcards such as s3:* are not matched). Another account able to rewrite the bucket's policy or ACL can take control of the data.
checks.description: Fails when the bucket policy has an Allow statement whose AWS principal is * or an ARN from another account and whose actions include exactly s3:DeleteBucketPolicy, s3:PutBucketAcl, s3:PutBucketPolicy, s3:PutEncryptionConfiguration or s3:PutObjectAcl (wildcards such as s3:* are not matched). Another account able to rewrite the bucket's policy or ACL can take control of the data.
checks.pass_when: No Allow statement grants one of the five permission-change actions to * or another account (no policy also passes).
checks.fail_when: An Allow statement grants one of the five actions to * or to a principal ARN of a different account.

checks.remediation: An S3 bucket policy contains a proven unrestricted wildcard-principal Allow statement.

caveats: Only supported fixed organization, account or ARN conditions certify a restriction. Literal wildcard-looking StringEquals values, policy variables, mixed lists and bounded ArnLike patterns remain UNKNOWN unless independent supported conditions settle the result. This check does not prove effective anonymous access or evaluate explicit Deny, account blocks and access points.

iac.code: Declare complete Policy.Policy.Statement[*].Principal and Condition values with owner-reviewed named principals or supported fixed restrictions; preserve recovery access and separately review UNKNOWN statements.
iac.label: Review S3 policy restrict public access declaration

steps: Inspect every bucket policy Allow statement with a wildcard principal, including its exact condition operator and values, and separate proven unrestricted statements from UNKNOWN conditions.
Have the bucket, IAM and application owners choose named principals or fixed approved organization/account/ARN restrictions and prepare the entire replacement policy, preserving legitimate access.
Apply the complete reviewed policy document, verify the repaired statement and authorized clients, and separately inspect public-access blocks without treating future-write blocks as grant removal.
remediation_details.summary: An S3 bucket policy contains a proven unrestricted wildcard-principal Allow statement.

checks.rationale: Fails when the bucket policy has an Allow statement with a wildcard in the first present of Principal AWS/CanonicalUser/Federated (or Principal "*") and no restricting condition key (aws:PrincipalOrgID, SourceAccount, PrincipalAccount, SourceOwner with string-equals operators, aws:PrincipalArn or aws:SourceArn with ARN operators). Such a statement grants its actions to anyone.
checks.description: Fails when the bucket policy has an Allow statement with a wildcard in the first present of Principal AWS/CanonicalUser/Federated (or Principal "*") and no restricting condition key (aws:PrincipalOrgID, SourceAccount, PrincipalAccount, SourceOwner with string-equals operators, aws:PrincipalArn or aws:SourceArn with ARN operators). Such a statement grants its actions to anyone.
checks.pass_when: Every wildcard-principal Allow statement carries one of the restricting operator/key pairs.
checks.fail_when: At least one wildcard-principal Allow statement has no restricting condition.
checks.not_applicable_when: The bucket has no bucket policy.

checks.title: S3 bucket policy has no public Allow statement (perimeter)
checks.remediation: A present S3 bucket policy has an Allow for a wildcard principal without an effective account, organization or ARN restriction.

caveats: A missing policy is NOT_APPLICABLE to this source. An apparently restrictive key with wildcard value does not make a public principal safe; the policy checker is a source-specific approximation and does not prove effective denial.

iac.code: Review Policy.Policy.Statement[*].Principal and Condition; use concrete nonwildcard account, organization or ARN restrictions or remove wildcard Allows in the complete owner-managed bucket policy.
iac.label: Review owner-managed bucket policy and blocks

references.title: AWS S3 Block Public Access behavior

steps: Inspect the full bucket policy, including wildcard principals, every condition operator and the actual organization, account or ARN values.
Have the bucket and application owners replace broad public access with named principals or concrete restrictive conditions after migrating any intentional public delivery.
Apply an owner-reviewed full replacement policy and validate the effective access with the expected private and denied callers.
remediation_details.summary: A present S3 bucket policy has an Allow for a wildcard principal without an effective account, organization or ARN restriction.

checks.rationale: aws-perimeter variant: fails when an Allow bucket-policy statement has a wildcard principal not restricted by aws:SourceOwner/SourceAccount/PrincipalOrgID/PrincipalAccount/PrincipalArn/SourceArn, where StringLike/ArnEquals/ArnLike values containing '*' do not count as restricting. This catches policies that look conditioned but still admit any account.
checks.description: aws-perimeter variant: fails when an Allow bucket-policy statement has a wildcard principal not restricted by aws:SourceOwner/SourceAccount/PrincipalOrgID/PrincipalAccount/PrincipalArn/SourceArn, where StringLike/ArnEquals/ArnLike values containing '*' do not count as restricting. This catches policies that look conditioned but still admit any account.
checks.pass_when: No Allow statement has an unrestricted wildcard principal.
checks.fail_when: At least one Allow statement has a wildcard principal whose conditions do not restrict it to specific accounts/ARNs.
checks.not_applicable_when: The bucket has no bucket policy.

caveats: The source uses the audited account as its only trusted account by default, so a legitimate cross-account grant can still fail. It is not proof that a grant is unused or that all possible wildcard action patterns are detected.

checks.description: Applies Prowler's is_policy_public with cross-account access disallowed, so any Allow to a principal outside the audited account (or public) fails. Cross-account bucket access is a data-sharing path that must be explicitly reviewed and trusted.
