caveats: This source only recognizes its listed PutObject, DeleteObject, s3:* and Put*/Delete* action forms; it does not prove every write pattern absent. RestrictPublicBuckets can interrupt legitimate cross-account access and does not remove an underlying public policy.

cli.label: Apply complete owner-reviewed bucket public-access blocks

iac.code: Review Policy.Policy.Statement[*].Principal, Action and Condition with both PublicAccessBlock.PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.RestrictPublicBuckets values; replace public write grants or apply an owner-approved complete block configuration after client migration.
iac.label: Review owner-managed bucket policy and blocks

references.title: AWS S3 Block Public Access behavior

steps: Inspect the bucket policy, both levels of RestrictPublicBuckets, and authorized upload or delete clients.
Have the bucket and application owners migrate public writes to named or signed upload paths and approve full replacement policy and block documents.
Remove the reviewed public-write Allow and/or enable the bucket RestrictPublicBuckets flag, then verify denied public writes and authorized clients.
remediation_details.summary: The bucket policy contains a source-recognized public write Allow and neither bucket nor account RestrictPublicBuckets masks it.

checks.rationale: Fails when the bucket policy is public for s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, s3:*, s3:Put* or s3:Delete* (is_policy_public with those actions) and RestrictPublicBuckets is false at both bucket and account level. Public write lets anyone plant malware, overwrite or delete the bucket's objects.
checks.description: Fails when the bucket policy is public for s3:PutObject, s3:DeleteObject, s3:*, s3:Put* or s3:Delete* (is_policy_public with those actions) and RestrictPublicBuckets is false at both bucket and account level. Public write lets anyone plant malware, overwrite or delete the bucket's objects.
checks.pass_when: No policy, RestrictPublicBuckets on bucket or account, or no public write statement.
checks.fail_when: A public statement grants a write/delete action and RestrictPublicBuckets is off at bucket and account level.

checks.title: S3 bucket static website hosting is disabled
checks.remediation: An S3 bucket Website configuration contains an IndexDocument.Suffix, so this check sees static website hosting enabled.

caveats: CloudFront cannot use OAC with an S3 website endpoint; it must use the regular S3 bucket origin. Removing the website configuration before origin and DNS cutover can cause an outage. The source checks only IndexDocument.Suffix, not every possible website configuration.

iac.code: Remove Website.IndexDocument.Suffix and the website configuration from the owner-managed bucket declaration only after replacing the website endpoint with a tested private S3 origin and CloudFront OAC.
iac.label: Review the owner-managed S3 resource declaration

references.title: Official AWS S3 or CloudFront operational guidance

steps: Inspect the website endpoint, index and error documents, redirects, DNS, public policy and the clients using that endpoint.
Have the web and bucket owners migrate to an ordinary private S3 bucket origin with CloudFront OAC, recreating needed index, redirect and error behavior in the distribution.
After a tested DNS and client cutover, remove the website configuration in owner-managed IaC and verify GetBucketWebsite reports no configuration.
remediation_details.summary: An S3 bucket Website configuration contains an IndexDocument.Suffix, so this check sees static website hosting enabled.

checks.rationale: Fails when the bucket has a website configuration with IndexDocument.Suffix set (static website hosting enabled). Website endpoints serve objects over plain HTTP without IAM authentication and are a common source of unintended public exposure.
checks.description: Fails when the bucket has a website configuration with IndexDocument.Suffix set (static website hosting enabled). Website endpoints serve objects over plain HTTP without IAM authentication and are a common source of unintended public exposure.
checks.pass_when: No website configuration (or no index document suffix) is present.
checks.fail_when: Website.IndexDocument.Suffix is set.

checks.title: S3 bucket object-level data events are logged by CloudTrail
checks.remediation: No visible applicable CloudTrail trail has an S3 object data-event selector matching this bucket ARN or the source-recognized all-bucket selector.

caveats: A bucket viewed outside its home Region with no matched trail yields UNKNOWN, not a proven logging gap. The source checks selector configuration, not whether the trail is currently logging, delivery succeeds or all read/write events are selected; PutEventSelectors replaces existing basic or advanced selectors.

iac.code: Review CloudTrail.EventSelectors.DataResources[*].Type and Values or AdvancedEventSelectors.FieldSelectors for AWS::S3::Object, the bucket ARN or all-bucket scope; preserve all existing selectors in the owner-managed trail and verify delivery and cost.
iac.label: Review owner-managed S3 audit declaration

references.title: Official AWS data-event or classification job API

steps: Inspect the bucket home Region and each applicable same-Region or multi-Region trail, including its complete basic or advanced event selectors and current delivery status.
Have the audit and data owners approve the bucket ARN or all-bucket S3 object selector, preserve every existing management and data event selection, and estimate event volume and charges.
Apply a complete reviewed selector set to the chosen trail, then verify matching selectors, actual delivered object events and retention.
remediation_details.summary: No visible applicable CloudTrail trail has an S3 object data-event selector matching this bucket ARN or the source-recognized all-bucket selector.

checks.rationale: Fails when no CloudTrail trail that can see the bucket logs S3 object data events for it: an event selector DataResources value equal to the bucket ARN, an all-buckets arn:<partition>:s3 value, or any advanced selector on AWS::S3::Object (multi-Region trails or trails homed in the bucket Region). Without object-level logging, GetObject/PutObject/DeleteObject activity leaves no audit trail for exfiltration or tampering investigations.
checks.description: Fails when no CloudTrail trail that can see the bucket logs S3 object data events for it: an event selector DataResources value equal to the bucket ARN, an all-buckets arn:<partition>:s3 value, or any advanced selector on AWS::S3::Object (multi-Region trails or trails homed in the bucket Region). Without object-level logging, GetObject/PutObject/DeleteObject activity leaves no audit trail for exfiltration or tampering investigations.
checks.pass_when: A relevant trail's S3 data selector names this bucket ARN, all buckets, or an advanced AWS::S3::Object selector.
checks.fail_when: No multi-Region or same-Region trail has an S3 data selector covering the bucket.

caveats: S3 access point Block Public Access settings cannot be changed after creation; bucket and account blocks may still prevent public access independently. A replacement changes name/ARN and may break clients or cross-account policies; no delete command is offered.

cli.label: Create complete owner-reviewed replacement access point

iac.code: Set PublicAccessBlockConfiguration.BlockPublicAcls,IgnorePublicAcls,BlockPublicPolicy,RestrictPublicBuckets to true in a new owner-managed S3 access point declaration, preserving Bucket, VPC and policy requirements and migrating clients to its new ARN.
iac.label: Review the owner-managed S3 resource declaration

references.title: Official AWS S3 or CloudFront operational guidance

steps: Inspect the access point, attached bucket, network origin, policy and clients using its name or ARN.
Have access point, bucket and application owners approve a replacement access point with all four public-access blocks and copied required VPC/policy behavior.
Create the reviewed replacement, verify its four flags and authorized clients, then migrate all references before separately retiring the old endpoint.
remediation_details.summary: An S3 access point has at least one PublicAccessBlockConfiguration flag absent or false, so its own four setting check fails.

checks.rationale: Fails for an S3 access point whose PublicAccessBlockConfiguration does not have all four settings (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets) set to true. An access point without a full block can carry a policy that exposes bucket objects publicly.
checks.description: Fails for an S3 access point whose PublicAccessBlockConfiguration does not have all four settings (BlockPublicAcls, IgnorePublicAcls, BlockPublicPolicy, RestrictPublicBuckets) set to true. An access point without a full block can carry a policy that exposes bucket objects publicly.
checks.pass_when: All four public access block settings are true.
checks.fail_when: Any of the four settings is false or missing.

checks.title: S3 Multi-Region Access Point blocks all public access
checks.remediation: An S3 Multi-Region Access Point has at least one PublicAccessBlock flag absent or false in its own configuration.

caveats: Multi-Region Access Point public-access flags and bucket membership cannot change after creation. CreateMultiRegionAccessPoint is asynchronous and a new alias affects routing and policies; bucket/account blocks can independently mask exposure.

cli.label: Create complete owner-reviewed replacement Multi-Region Access Point
Inspect the replacement after asynchronous creation

iac.code: Set PublicAccessBlock.BlockPublicAcls,IgnorePublicAcls,BlockPublicPolicy,RestrictPublicBuckets to true in a new owner-managed Multi-Region Access Point declaration; retain the exact Regions[*].Bucket set and migrate clients to its new Alias after status and policy checks.
iac.label: Review the owner-managed S3 resource declaration

references.title: Official AWS S3 or CloudFront operational guidance

steps: Inspect the Multi-Region Access Point alias, all backing buckets, public block settings, policy and client routing dependencies.

references.title: Aurora MySQL Advanced Auditing and supported events

steps: Inspect the exact Aurora MySQL DBClusterArn, its attached cluster parameter group, ClusterParameterGroupValues.server_audit_logging and server_audit_events. ON or 1 with a nonempty comma-separated list of supported uppercase events passes; OFF/0 or an empty event list fails, while missing or unrecognized facts stay UNKNOWN.

With the database and audit owners, select at least one supported event from CONNECT, QUERY, QUERY_DCL, QUERY_DDL, QUERY_DML and TABLE, with uppercase names and no spaces. Check existing include/exclude user settings, audit volume, retention and whether separate log delivery is required.

Change only the reviewed custom cluster parameter group values using the AWS-documented apply method; review every cluster sharing the group and whether first association requires a restart. Verify effective ON/1 and selected events, inspect a representative audit log, then recollect and rerun.

iac.code: For only the source-confirmed supported standalone DB instance, declare IAMDatabaseAuthenticationEnabled=true (or the IaC equivalent) with a separate least-privilege rds-db:connect policy and database-user migration plan; review the change and rollback.

caveats: The native evaluator passes an observed true instance flag as configuration evidence only; it does not prove any database user or client authenticates with IAM. A false flag fails only with matching regional engine/version/class SupportsIAMDatabaseAuthentication=true evidence.

Aurora and Multi-AZ DB cluster members use the cluster IAM-auth setting; known unsupported engines and RDS on Outposts are NOT_APPLICABLE. For a disabled instance flag, missing/denied/empty/conflicting capability or missing placement evidence is UNKNOWN; an observed true flag can pass as configuration evidence without capability or absent placement. Observed malformed placement and unrecognized engines remain UNKNOWN.

IAM DB auth uses short-lived tokens and extra instance memory. PostgreSQL IAM-auth users cannot also use password authentication and IAM cannot be combined with Kerberos there; test replication and connection pooling dependencies. Enabling the flag alone does not grant rds-db:connect or create a database user.

Without --apply-immediately RDS schedules the change for the next maintenance window; any immediate change needs separate availability and client-owner approval. No command is executed by the product.

checks.remediation: An RDS instance or its owning cluster uses admin or postgres as MasterUsername, or a referenced cluster is missing from complete inventory.

caveats: MasterUsername cannot be changed on an existing RDS instance or cluster through a simple modify flag; a new deployment and data migration are required. A missing cluster join fails this source even when the actual username may be safe; confirm inventory completeness first.

iac.code: Declare DBInstanceArn or rds_cluster MasterUsername replacement with a non-default value, secret custody, grants, data migration and rollback; never embed the password in this template.

steps: Inspect DBInstanceArn, Engine, DBClusterIdentifier and the effective cluster or instance MasterUsername; resolve a missing cluster join before planning change.
Have database and application owners design a replacement database with a non-default master identity, credentials in the approved secret store, data migration, grants and client cutover.
Create and migrate to the reviewed replacement only after snapshot/restore and rollback tests, then verify the effective master username and client permissions.
remediation_details.summary: An RDS instance or its owning cluster uses admin or postgres as MasterUsername, or a referenced cluster is missing from complete inventory.

checks.fail_when: An RDS instance or its cluster uses MasterUsername admin or postgres, or a referenced cluster cannot be resolved.
checks.not_applicable_when: The resource Engine is docdb, which this RDS predicate excludes.

caveats: DocumentDB is not applicable. A missing referenced cluster fails until inventory is resolved; blindly modifying the instance may not fix a cluster-level MultiAZ value. Multi-AZ can increase cost and change failover behavior.

checks.rationale: For each rds instance, the evaluator flags FAIL when neither the instance nor its resolved parent cluster has MultiAZ true, or a named parent cluster is missing from complete inventory. A zonal failure can interrupt the rds instance when the surviving zone lacks a usable replica.
checks.description: For each rds instance, the evaluator flags FAIL when neither the instance nor its resolved parent cluster has MultiAZ true, or a named parent cluster is missing from complete inventory. checks.fail_when: Neither the instance nor its resolved parent cluster has MultiAZ true, or a named parent cluster is missing from complete inventory.

checks.remediation: An RDS instance EngineLifecycleSupport is open-source-rds-extended-support.

caveats: Extended Support keeps older open-source engines available for a fee; disabling it before a supported upgrade can be rejected or disrupt availability. The source only checks the string value, not whether a future major version is operationally compatible.

iac.code: Declare DBInstanceArn EngineVersion on a supported major release and EngineLifecycleSupport=open-source-rds-extended-support-disabled after tested application migration.
iac.label: Review RDS instance extended support declaration

steps: Inspect DBInstanceArn, Engine, EngineVersion, Extended Support billing and the supported major upgrade targets.
Have the database and application owners test a supported major version, extension compatibility, parameter groups, drivers and rollback in staging.
Upgrade through the approved path, then disable Extended Support enrollment only when the engine version is eligible and verify lifecycle status and charges.
remediation_details.summary: An RDS instance EngineLifecycleSupport is open-source-rds-extended-support.

checks.rationale: For each rds instance, the evaluator flags FAIL when EngineLifecycleSupport equals open-source-rds-extended-support. Known vulnerabilities can remain exploitable in the rds instance while it runs an old release.
checks.description: For each rds instance, the evaluator flags FAIL when EngineLifecycleSupport equals open-source-rds-extended-support. Known vulnerabilities can remain exploitable in the rds instance while it runs an old release.
checks.pass_when: EngineLifecycleSupport differs from the extended-support value or is absent.
checks.fail_when: EngineLifecycleSupport equals open-source-rds-extended-support.

checks.title: RDS instance CA certificate is valid for more than three months
checks.remediation: A non-DocumentDB RDS instance CA certificate ValidTill is no later than three calendar months after capture.

caveats: DocumentDB is not applicable. The source joins CACertificateIdentifier to one collected rds_certificate and returns UNKNOWN if unresolved; exactly three calendar months remaining still fails. Client trust stores must be updated before rotation. Some engine versions support rotation without restart while others need a restart; do not assume either behavior without checking the instance capabilities.

iac.code: Declare DBInstanceArn CACertificateIdentifier joined to a supported rds_certificate.ValidTill beyond the policy window, with tested client trust and rollback.
iac.label: Review RDS ca certificate valid 3 months declaration

steps: Inspect DBInstanceArn, CACertificateIdentifier, joined certificate ValidTill, engine compatibility and all TLS-verifying client trust stores.
Have database, PKI and application owners select a supported newer CA, distribute client trust anchors first, and plan the maintenance/reboot behavior and rollback.
Modify the instance to the reviewed CA after client readiness, then test TLS verification and recheck the joined certificate expiry.
remediation_details.summary: A non-DocumentDB RDS instance CA certificate ValidTill is no later than three calendar months after capture.

checks.rationale: For each rds instance, the evaluator flags FAIL when the joined RDS CA certificate is not valid beyond snapshot time plus three calendar months. A CA rollover missed before expiry can make database TLS clients reject the server certificate and interrupt connections.
checks.description: For each rds instance, the evaluator flags FAIL when the joined RDS CA certificate is not valid beyond snapshot time plus three calendar months. A CA rollover missed before expiry can make database TLS clients reject the server certificate and interrupt connections.
checks.pass_when: ValidTill is later than snapshot time plus three calendar months.
checks.fail_when: The joined RDS CA certificate is not valid beyond snapshot time plus three calendar months.
checks.not_applicable_when: The resource is a DocumentDB engine excluded by this RDS predicate.

checks.title: RDS instance CA certificate does not expire within 7 days
checks.remediation: An RDS instance CA certificate ValidTill has seven or fewer truncated days remaining at capture.

caveats: This check includes every engine and truncates the day component of the expiry delta; a certificate close to eight days can enter the seven-day band. Missing certificate join is UNKNOWN, not proof of expiry. Some engine versions support rotation without restart while others need a restart; do not assume either behavior without checking the instance capabilities.

iac.code: Declare DBInstanceArn CACertificateIdentifier joined to a supported rds_certificate.ValidTill beyond the policy window, with tested client trust and rollback.
iac.label: Review RDS ca certificate not expiring 7 days declaration

steps: Inspect DBInstanceArn, CACertificateIdentifier, joined certificate ValidTill, engine compatibility and all TLS-verifying client trust stores.
Have database, PKI and application owners select a supported newer CA, distribute client trust anchors first, and plan the maintenance/reboot behavior and rollback.
Modify the instance to the reviewed CA after client readiness, then test TLS verification and recheck the joined certificate expiry.
remediation_details.summary: An RDS instance CA certificate ValidTill has seven or fewer truncated days remaining at capture.

checks.rationale: Compares the joined RDS CA certificate ValidTill timestamp with the exact captured snapshot instant. Expired or within-seven-day certificates fail; missing certificate or clock evidence stays UNKNOWN.
checks.description: Compares the joined RDS CA certificate ValidTill timestamp with the exact captured snapshot instant. Expired or within-seven-day certificates fail; missing certificate or clock evidence stays UNKNOWN.
checks.pass_when: ValidTill is strictly more than seven days after capture, including any positive seconds beyond seven days.
checks.fail_when: ValidTill is at or before capture plus exactly seven days.
checks.not_applicable_when: None.

checks.remediation: A public RDS instance has an active security group open to the world on its endpoint TCP port and an active subnet with a default IGW route.

caveats: DocumentDB is not applicable. This native conjunction can pass a publicly accessible instance when no matching open SG or public subnet is collected; that PASS is not a blanket internet-exposure guarantee. Disabling public access before clients migrate can cause an outage.

iac.code: Declare DBInstanceArn PubliclyAccessible=false with Endpoint.Port ingress limited to approved sources, active DBSubnetGroup.Subnets without unintended IGW routes and tested private client paths.
iac.label: Review RDS instance internet exposed network declaration

steps: Inspect DBInstanceArn, PubliclyAccessible, Endpoint.Port, active VPC security groups, exact world-open ingress rules and effective routes for active DB subnets.
Have database and application owners replace public clients with private VPN/peering/endpoints or an approved proxy and narrow the DB port ingress to reviewed sources.
After client migration, disable public accessibility and tighten the exact security group rules; verify private connectivity and no remaining world-open path.
remediation_details.summary: A public RDS instance has an active security group open to the world on its endpoint TCP port and an active subnet with a default IGW route.

checks.rationale: For each rds instance, the evaluator flags FAIL when an RDS instance is PubliclyAccessible and an active security group opens its endpoint TCP port to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 while an active DB subnet has an internet-gateway default route. This can give unintended external principals a route to the rds instance or its data.
checks.description: For each rds instance, the evaluator flags FAIL when an RDS instance is PubliclyAccessible and an active security group opens its endpoint TCP port to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 while an active DB subnet has an internet-gateway default route. This can give unintended external principals a route to the rds instance or its data.
checks.pass_when: At least one of public accessibility, world-open database-port ingress, or public DB subnet is absent.
checks.fail_when: An RDS instance is PubliclyAccessible and an active security group opens its endpoint TCP port to 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 while an active DB subnet has an internet-gateway default route.
checks.not_applicable_when: The resource is a DocumentDB engine excluded by this RDS predicate.

checks.title: RDS instance DB subnet group has no public subnet
checks.remediation: An observed RDS DB subnet group includes a subnet whose effective IPv4 default route targets an internet gateway.

caveats: This check flags direct internet-gateway route configuration only. A NAT-only default route is outbound and does not fail this predicate; route configuration alone does not establish internet reachability.
Missing, denied, partial, ambiguous or malformed subnet/route evidence returns UNKNOWN. Changing a DB subnet group can disrupt connectivity and requires a reviewed replacement or migration plan.

cli.label: Inspect the identified DB instance and DB subnet group
Inspect operator-reviewed DB subnet identities and VPCs
Inspect effective explicit or VPC main route tables

iac.code: Declare DB subnet group membership only in approved private subnets after reviewing each subnet effective route table for an IPv4 default route to igw-*. Keep NAT egress and actual RDS PubliclyAccessible/security-group exposure as separate decisions; plan migration, AZ placement and failover.
iac.label: Review RDS instance no public subnet network declaration

references.title: AWS RDS DB instances in a VPC

steps: Inspect the DB instance DBSubnetGroup.Subnets list, each exact subnet VPC, and its explicitly associated route table or VPC main table.
For each effective 0.0.0.0/0 route, distinguish a direct GatewayId=igw-* from an outbound NatGatewayId=nat-*; review PubliclyAccessible and security groups separately before inferring exposure.

If direct-IGW subnet membership violates the approved database design, have the database and network owners plan a private DB subnet group across required Availability Zones, test client access and failover, and schedule an approved migration.
remediation_details.summary: An observed RDS DB subnet group includes a subnet whose effective IPv4 default route targets an internet gateway.

checks.rationale: Checks each DB subnet-group member’s effective route table for a direct 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway. A NAT-only default route is outbound private-subnet routing and does not fail this check. Missing subnet or route evidence stays UNKNOWN.
checks.description: Checks each DB subnet-group member’s effective route table for a direct 0.0.0.0/0 route to an internet gateway. A NAT-only default route is outbound private-subnet routing and does not fail this check. Missing subnet or route evidence stays UNKNOWN.
checks.pass_when: No DB subnet-group subnet has a direct default route to an internet gateway.
checks.fail_when: At least one DB subnet-group subnet has a direct 0.0.0.0/0 route to igw-.
checks.not_applicable_when: None.

checks.title: RDS instance snapshot is not shared outside the account without review
checks.remediation: An RDS instance snapshot has one or more restore attribute values requiring account-trust review.

caveats: This native branch returns MANUAL for any share value and PASS only for no values; it cannot decide whether a named recipient account is trusted. Do not remove an approved recovery share solely to obtain PASS.

iac.code: Declare Attributes.DBSnapshotAttributesResult.DBSnapshotAttributes AttributeName=restore and full AttributeValues under owner-approved recipients, preserving recovery and KMS access; remove unapproved public or account values only.

steps: Inspect the exact instance snapshot, every Attributes.DBSnapshotAttributesResult.DBSnapshotAttributes AttributeName and AttributeValues entry, and recipients of each share.
Have the database, backup and recipient-account owners document which share values are approved, including cross-account restore and KMS access.
Remove only a confirmed untrusted value after the recipient migration plan is approved; preserve legitimate recovery paths and recheck attributes.
remediation_details.summary: An RDS instance snapshot has one or more restore attribute values requiring account-trust review.

checks.rationale: For each rds snapshot, the evaluator has no FAIL path; An instance snapshot with any restore-share value produces MANUAL. A reviewer must judge whether the external principal or snapshot share is trusted before treating the access as acceptable.
checks.description: For each rds snapshot, the evaluator has no FAIL path; An instance snapshot with any restore-share value produces MANUAL. A reviewer must judge whether the external principal or snapshot share is trusted before treating the access as acceptable.
checks.pass_when: All collected snapshot attribute value lists are empty.
checks.fail_when: This evaluator never returns FAIL; any nonempty attribute value list, including ["all"], returns MANUAL.

checks.title: RDS cluster snapshot is not shared outside the account without review
checks.remediation: An RDS cluster snapshot has one or more restore attribute values requiring account-trust review.

caveats: This native branch returns MANUAL for any share value and PASS only for no values; it cannot decide whether a named recipient account is trusted. Do not remove an approved recovery share solely to obtain PASS.

iac.code: Declare Attributes.DBClusterSnapshotAttributesResult.DBClusterSnapshotAttributes AttributeName=restore and full AttributeValues under owner-approved recipients, preserving recovery and KMS access; remove unapproved public or account values only.
iac.label: Review cluster snapshot restore sharing

steps: Inspect the exact cluster snapshot, every Attributes.DBClusterSnapshotAttributesResult.DBClusterSnapshotAttributes AttributeName and AttributeValues entry, and recipients of each share.
Have the database, backup and recipient-account owners document which share values are approved, including cross-account restore and KMS access.
Remove only a confirmed untrusted value after the recipient migration plan is approved; preserve legitimate recovery paths and recheck attributes.
remediation_details.summary: An RDS cluster snapshot has one or more restore attribute values requiring account-trust review.

checks.rationale: For each rds cluster snapshot, the evaluator has no FAIL path; A cluster snapshot with any restore-share value produces MANUAL. A reviewer must judge whether the external principal or snapshot share is trusted before treating the access as acceptable.
checks.description: For each rds cluster snapshot, the evaluator has no FAIL path; A cluster snapshot with any restore-share value produces MANUAL. A reviewer must judge whether the external principal or snapshot share is trusted before treating the access as acceptable.
checks.pass_when: All collected snapshot attribute value lists are empty.
checks.fail_when: This evaluator never returns FAIL; any nonempty attribute value list, including ["all"], returns MANUAL.

checks.remediation: A non-DocumentDB RDS cluster snapshot has StorageEncrypted=false.

caveats: Snapshot encryption is immutable for the existing snapshot; copying creates a new resource and does not convert the original finding. DocumentDB is not applicable. Deleting the old copy before KMS and restore validation can destroy recovery capability.

iac.code: Declare a new DBClusterSnapshotIdentifier copied with StorageEncrypted=true and approved KmsKeyId; preserve the unencrypted source until restore and retention owners approve retirement.
iac.label: Review encrypted cluster snapshot copy

steps: Inspect the exact cluster snapshot identifier, Engine, StorageEncrypted state, KMS access and every restore or retention dependency.
Have data and backup owners approve a customer-managed KMS key, a new encrypted copy, cross-account restore needs, lifecycle policy and a tested rollback.
Copy the source to a new encrypted snapshot, verify StorageEncrypted and restore it in an isolated environment; retire the original only through a later approved retention change.
remediation_details.summary: A non-DocumentDB RDS cluster snapshot has StorageEncrypted=false.

checks.rationale: For each rds cluster snapshot, the evaluator flags FAIL when a non-DocumentDB cluster snapshot has StorageEncrypted false. A stolen storage copy or overbroad key access can disclose data held by the rds cluster snapshot.
checks.description: For each rds cluster snapshot, the evaluator flags FAIL when a non-DocumentDB cluster snapshot has StorageEncrypted false. A stolen storage copy or overbroad key access can disclose data held by the rds cluster snapshot.
checks.pass_when: StorageEncrypted is true.
checks.fail_when: A non-DocumentDB cluster snapshot has StorageEncrypted false.
checks.not_applicable_when: The resource is a DocumentDB engine excluded by this RDS predicate.

checks.remediation: A Region with rds cluster resources has no enabled db-cluster event subscription covering maintenance, failure.

caveats: The native regional predicate accepts any one enabled db-cluster subscription whose category list is empty or includes the required set, regardless of whether SourceIds include every database or SNS delivery works. A Region without rds_cluster resources is not applicable; verify resource coverage and delivery operationally.

iac.code: Declare rds_event_subscription SourceType=db-cluster, Enabled=true, EventCategoriesList containing ['maintenance', 'failure'], SNS topic and intended SourceIds; test notification delivery.
iac.label: Review RDS db-cluster event subscription

steps: Inspect all rds_cluster resources, existing RDS event subscriptions with SourceType=db-cluster, Enabled, EventCategoriesList and SourceIds scope.
Have database and operations owners approve an SNS topic, delivery permissions, recipient/on-call routing and the maintenance, failure categories or all categories.
Create the complete reviewed subscription, verify Enabled and event delivery to the monitored recipient, and check that SourceIds cover the intended resources.
remediation_details.summary: A Region with rds cluster resources has no enabled db-cluster event subscription covering maintenance, failure.

checks.rationale: For each rds event subscription, the evaluator flags FAIL when a region with RDS clusters has no enabled db-cluster subscription covering both failure and maintenance categories. checks.remediation: A Neptune cluster fails when BackupRetentionPeriod is below seven days, reducing the available automated backup recovery window.

caveats: Other DB cluster engines are not applicable. A retention value of seven days does not prove backups completed or a recovery test passed; increasing retention can increase storage cost.

cli.label: Inspect the exact Neptune cluster configuration

iac.code: Set BackupRetentionPeriod>=7 for Engine=neptune in the cluster owner declaration. Monitor completed automated backups and test restore separately; record storage budget and recovery objective.
iac.label: Review the Neptune cluster owner declaration

steps: Confirm Engine=neptune, inspect BackupRetentionPeriod, current backups and the workload recovery objective.
Have the database owner approve retention of at least seven days, including storage cost and compliance constraints.
Modify retention in the approved window and verify fresh automated backups are created and restorable.
remediation_details.summary: A Neptune cluster fails when BackupRetentionPeriod is below seven days, reducing the available automated backup recovery window.

checks.rationale: For each neptune cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when BackupRetentionPeriod is below seven days. Deletion or corruption may leave too little recoverable history to restore the neptune cluster.
checks.description: For each neptune cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when BackupRetentionPeriod is below seven days. Deletion or corruption may leave too little recoverable history to restore the neptune cluster.
checks.pass_when: BackupRetentionPeriod is at least seven days.
checks.fail_when: BackupRetentionPeriod is below seven days.
checks.not_applicable_when: The resource Engine is not neptune.

iac.label: Review the Neptune cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect Engine, CopyTagsToSnapshot and the tags that must flow to recovery copies.
Have the database and tagging owners approve copying tags, including any tags that should not propagate to shared snapshots.
Enable tag copying and verify a subsequent snapshot receives the expected tags.

caveats: Other DB cluster engines are not applicable. AWS permits an unencrypted snapshot to be restored with a KMS key, but not an existing unencrypted cluster to be converted. iac.code: For Engine=neptune and StorageEncrypted=false, create a snapshot and restore a new cluster with an approved KMS key in the complete replacement declaration. Rebuild instances and endpoints, verify data and client access, and retain rollback.
iac.label: Review the Neptune cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect StorageEncrypted, snapshot availability, KMS policy, global-cluster membership and dependent writer/reader endpoints.
Have database and KMS owners create a reviewed cluster snapshot and plan a replacement restore with an approved KMS key; encryption cannot be enabled in place.
Restore a new encrypted cluster from the snapshot, create required instances, migrate applications and verify encryption and data before retiring the old cluster.

checks.title: Neptune cluster MultiAZ is enabled
checks.remediation: A Neptune cluster fails when MultiAZ is not true, indicating its deployed instances do not provide the requested cross-AZ failover placement.

caveats: Other DB cluster engines are not applicable. A reader adds compute cost and may not immediately change failover posture until healthy; the MultiAZ field alone does not prove application failover readiness.

cli.label: Create an owner-reviewed reader in a separate AZ

iac.code: For Engine=neptune, require MultiAZ=true and place a reviewed reader instance in a different AvailabilityZone from the writer using the cluster subnet group. Verify reader health, replication and failover behavior after creation.
iac.label: Review the Neptune cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect MultiAZ and the writer and reader DB instances with their actual AvailabilityZone values and subnet-group coverage.
Have the database owner approve a Neptune reader in a different AZ, including instance class, cost and failover testing.
Create the reviewed reader in the selected AZ and verify it joins the cluster, replicates data and makes MultiAZ true.
remediation_details.summary: A Neptune cluster fails when MultiAZ is not true, indicating its deployed instances do not provide the requested cross-AZ failover placement.

checks.rationale: For each neptune cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when MultiAZ is false. A zonal failure can interrupt the neptune cluster when the surviving zone lacks a usable replica.
checks.description: For each neptune cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when MultiAZ is false. A zonal failure can interrupt the neptune cluster when the surviving zone lacks a usable replica.
checks.pass_when: MultiAZ is true.
checks.fail_when: MultiAZ is false.

checks.remediation: A publicly accessible Redshift endpoint joins to a cluster subnet with an Internet Gateway default route and a VPC security group allowing world CIDRs on all TCP ports.

caveats: This conjunctive predicate does not fail every publicly accessible cluster or every world-open rule by itself. A route-table declaration and broad rule do not prove effective reachability; shared security groups and endpoint changes can break other clients.

cli.label: Disable public access after private-client migration

iac.code: Declare PubliclyAccessible=false and an owner-approved private client path; review subnet group routes and attached security group declarations, then stage a reversible cutover before reducing world ingress.

steps: Inspect PubliclyAccessible, endpoint, cluster subnet group and each subnet route to the Internet Gateway; inspect attached security group ingress with rule IDs.
Have network and database owners stage private access for all clients and approve disabling public accessibility and restricting the exact open security group rules.
Disable public access after client cutover, remove owner-reviewed world rules where safe, recollect subnet and route inventory and test intended private connectivity.
remediation_details.summary: A publicly accessible Redshift endpoint joins to a cluster subnet with an Internet Gateway default route and a VPC security group allowing world CIDRs on all TCP ports.

checks.rationale: Flags a Redshift cluster when a cluster has an endpoint address, is publicly accessible, has a public subnet, and an attached security group admits all-address TCP ingress. checks.description: Flags a Redshift cluster when a cluster has an endpoint address, is publicly accessible, has a public subnet, and an attached security group admits all-address TCP ingress. It can make the service reachable from untrusted networks, increasing the chance of unauthorized access or exploitation.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when a cluster has an endpoint address, is publicly accessible, has a public subnet, and an attached security group admits all-address TCP ingress.

checks.title: Redshift security groups do not allow the cluster port from 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0
checks.remediation: A Redshift attached security group has world-CIDR ingress whose protocol or port range includes the endpoint port, or port 5439 when that field is absent.

caveats: The evaluator accepts any protocol whose port range covers the endpoint port and protocol -1 without explicit ports; it does not require actual public route reachability. Shared security groups can serve other workloads, so removal needs dependency review.

cli.label: Remove only the owner-reviewed world ingress rule

iac.code: Replace world-CIDR ingress covering the Redshift endpoint port in the owning security group declaration with approved private CIDRs or group references after all attached clients are reviewed.
iac.label: Review the Redshift resource owner declaration

steps: Inspect the endpoint port and all attached security group rule IDs, IPv4 and IPv6 CIDRs, protocols and port ranges.
Have the security group owner stage approved private CIDRs or referenced groups for database clients; identify only exact world-CIDR rules covering the evaluated port.
After client migration, revoke the approved rule ID and verify intended connections and the fresh security group inventory.
remediation_details.summary: A Redshift attached security group has world-CIDR ingress whose protocol or port range includes the endpoint port, or port 5439 when that field is absent.

checks.rationale: Checks attached Redshift security group ingress for a world CIDR and a port range covering Endpoint.Port (default 5439). The evaluator counts any protocol with such a range, or protocol `-1` without FromPort.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when an attached security group has 0.0.0.0/0 or ::/0 ingress with a port range covering Endpoint.Port (default 5439), regardless of protocol, or protocol `-1` without FromPort.

checks.remediation: A MemoryDB cluster fails when AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is not true, leaving minor engine updates outside its automatic upgrade setting.

caveats: AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is present at CreateCluster but absent from UpdateCluster in the current AWS API model; no in-place flag is offered. Replacement changes endpoints and may create downtime or cost, and automatic upgrades still require compatibility monitoring.

cli.label: Create an owner-reviewed replacement cluster from a complete configuration document

iac.code: Set AutoMinorVersionUpgrade=true in the replacement cluster declaration, preserving approved engine, ACL, subnet and maintenance settings. Snapshot or migrate data, test client endpoints, stage rollback and verify the new cluster after cutover.
iac.label: Review the MemoryDB cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect AutoMinorVersionUpgrade, engine version, maintenance window, backup state and the application compatibility policy.
Have the MemoryDB owner approve a replacement cluster with AutoMinorVersionUpgrade=true because the modeled UpdateCluster API does not accept this field.
Create the reviewed replacement using a supported snapshot or migration plan, test clients and data integrity, then cut over and verify the new flag.
remediation_details.summary: A MemoryDB cluster fails when AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is not true, leaving minor engine updates outside its automatic upgrade setting.

checks.rationale: For each memorydb cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is false on a MemoryDB cluster. Known vulnerabilities can remain exploitable in the memorydb cluster while it runs an old release.
checks.description: For each memorydb cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is false on a MemoryDB cluster. Known vulnerabilities can remain exploitable in the memorydb cluster while it runs an old release.
checks.pass_when: AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is true.
checks.fail_when: AutoMinorVersionUpgrade is false on a MemoryDB cluster.

checks.title: MemoryDB cluster enables in-transit encryption (TLS)
checks.remediation: A MemoryDB cluster fails when TLSEnabled is not true, leaving client connections without the requested in-transit encryption setting.

caveats: TLSEnabled is a CreateCluster field and is absent from UpdateCluster, so it cannot be switched on in place. Replacement can change endpoints and interrupt clients; retain rollback and old-cluster data until migration is verified.

cli.label: Create an owner-reviewed replacement cluster from a complete configuration document

iac.code: Set TLSEnabled=true in a new MemoryDB cluster declaration while preserving the reviewed ACL, subnet, KMS and engine configuration. Migrate data and client endpoints through an approved cutover, verify TLS negotiation and retain a rollback path.
iac.label: Review the MemoryDB cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect TLSEnabled, current clients, ACLs, snapshots and cross-region or multi-region dependencies.
Have the database and application owners prepare TLS-capable clients and a reviewed replacement cluster with TLSEnabled=true; use a supported snapshot or migration path.
Create and validate the replacement, update client endpoints and certificates, then verify encrypted connections and data before retiring the old cluster.
remediation_details.summary: A MemoryDB cluster fails when TLSEnabled is not true, leaving client connections without the requested in-transit encryption setting.

checks.rationale: For each memorydb cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when TLSEnabled is false on a MemoryDB cluster. Client or service traffic may be intercepted or modified before it reaches the memorydb cluster.
checks.description: For each memorydb cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when TLSEnabled is false on a MemoryDB cluster. Client or service traffic may be intercepted or modified before it reaches the memorydb cluster.
checks.pass_when: TLSEnabled is true.
checks.fail_when: TLSEnabled is false on a MemoryDB cluster.

checks.remediation: OpenSearch AdvancedSecurityOptions.Enabled is false, so index, document and field access is not governed by fine-grained access control.

caveats: Fine-grained access control requires compatible encryption and HTTPS settings. Enabling it on an existing domain can break signed and basic-auth clients unless role mappings and the migration period are planned; do not place passwords in command arguments or metadata.

cli.label: Apply reviewed identity and security configuration

iac.code: Declare AdvancedSecurityOptions.Enabled=true with owner-reviewed IAM master user and role mappings, plus required encryption and HTTPS settings; keep any sensitive identity material outside copied commands.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect domain version, node-to-node encryption, HTTPS enforcement, current domain access policy and every client authentication method.
Have identity and search owners choose an IAM or internal master user, map roles for existing clients and stage the documented existing-domain migration period.
Apply an owner-reviewed advanced-security configuration, migrate and test principals before ending temporary anonymous access, then verify Enabled=true and authorization behavior.
remediation_details.summary: OpenSearch AdvancedSecurityOptions.Enabled is false, so index, document and field access is not governed by fine-grained access control.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when AdvancedSecurityOptions.Enabled is false or omitted. Without fine-grained roles, a domain-level caller can reach indices and operations beyond its intended permissions.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when AdvancedSecurityOptions.Enabled is false or omitted. Without fine-grained roles, a domain-level caller can reach indices and operations beyond its intended permissions.
checks.pass_when: AdvancedSecurityOptions.Enabled is true.
checks.fail_when: AdvancedSecurityOptions.Enabled is false or omitted.

checks.title: OpenSearch domain internal user database is disabled
checks.remediation: OpenSearch AdvancedSecurityOptions.InternalUserDatabaseEnabled is true; this control calls for federated or IAM-managed Dashboards identity instead.

caveats: The evaluator treats an absent InternalUserDatabaseEnabled field as false; absence alone does not prove federation is working. Switching the master user can disable HTTP basic authentication without deleting internal user records.

iac.code: Set AdvancedSecurityOptions.InternalUserDatabaseEnabled=false only after declaring tested IAM or SAML master identity and role mappings in the domain owner configuration.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect advanced security settings, current internal users, role mappings, Dashboards sign-in and client authentication dependencies.
Have the identity owner stage an IAM or SAML master principal and map every required role; validate access before disabling internal basic authentication.
Apply the reviewed identity change, verify the field is false and test Dashboards and application access; separately remove unused internal users if approved.
remediation_details.summary: OpenSearch AdvancedSecurityOptions.InternalUserDatabaseEnabled is true; this control calls for federated or IAM-managed Dashboards identity instead.

checks.rationale: Tests the source-specific OpenSearch internal user database disabled profile, suitable only where another owner authentication model is intended. It conflicts with the enabled profile on the same domain. Remediation: Use IAM or SAML instead of the internal user database only when that authentication profile is intended; verify the replacement identity controls.
checks.description: Tests the source-specific OpenSearch internal user database disabled profile, suitable only where another owner authentication model is intended. It conflicts with the enabled profile on the same domain. Remediation: Use IAM or SAML instead of the internal user database only when that authentication profile is intended; verify the replacement identity controls.
checks.pass_when: InternalUserDatabaseEnabled is false or omitted.
checks.fail_when: InternalUserDatabaseEnabled is true.

checks.remediation: OpenSearch ServiceSoftwareOptions.UpdateAvailable is true, indicating an unapplied service software update for this domain.

caveats: A service software patch differs from an engine-version upgrade. A pending request may take hours or days and can temporarily strain master capacity; the field may remain true until the deployment finishes.

cli.label: Schedule the approved software update in the off-peak window

iac.code: Set the owned DomainStatus.ServiceSoftwareOptions.UpdateAvailable maintenance policy and off-peak window; verify the deployed service software version after the requested update rather than treating a queued request as completion.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect CurrentVersion, NewVersion, UpdateStatus, workload health and the domain off-peak window.
Have the search owner approve capacity and an update window; review release notes and snapshot recovery for any compatibility-sensitive workload.
Schedule the available service software update, monitor its blue/green deployment and verify UpdateAvailable=false after completion.
remediation_details.summary: OpenSearch ServiceSoftwareOptions.UpdateAvailable is true, indicating an unapplied service software update for this domain.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when ServiceSoftwareOptions.UpdateAvailable is true. Known vulnerabilities can remain exploitable in the opensearch domain while it runs an old release.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when ServiceSoftwareOptions.UpdateAvailable is true. Known vulnerabilities can remain exploitable in the opensearch domain while it runs an old release.
checks.pass_when: UpdateAvailable is false.
checks.fail_when: ServiceSoftwareOptions.UpdateAvailable is true.

checks.title: OpenSearch domain has zone awareness and at least three data nodes
checks.remediation: OpenSearch has fewer than three data nodes or ClusterConfig.ZoneAwarenessEnabled is false; both values are required by this fault-tolerance check.

caveats: The predicate does not prove that nodes are healthy or distributed evenly. Zone awareness may require additional VPC subnets and multiple AZ capacity; scaling increases cost and can trigger a blue/green deployment.

cli.label: Apply owner-reviewed node and zone configuration

iac.code: Set ClusterConfig.InstanceCount to at least three and ZoneAwarenessEnabled=true with matching VPC subnet AZs and instance capacity in the owner declaration.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect node type, InstanceCount, zone awareness, VPC subnet AZs, storage pressure and shard allocation.
Have the search owner size at least three data nodes across supported AZs and approve added capacity and blue/green migration.
Apply the reviewed cluster configuration, verify InstanceCount>=3 and ZoneAwarenessEnabled=true, and inspect shard health and zone distribution.
remediation_details.summary: OpenSearch has fewer than three data nodes or ClusterConfig.ZoneAwarenessEnabled is false; both values are required by this fault-tolerance check.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when ClusterConfig.InstanceCount is below three or ZoneAwarenessEnabled is false. A zonal failure can interrupt the opensearch domain when the surviving zone lacks a usable replica.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when ClusterConfig.InstanceCount is below three or ZoneAwarenessEnabled is false. A zonal failure can interrupt the opensearch domain when the surviving zone lacks a usable replica.
checks.pass_when: At least three data nodes and zone awareness are configured.
checks.fail_when: ClusterConfig.InstanceCount is below three or ZoneAwarenessEnabled is false.

checks.title: OpenSearch domain has at least three dedicated master nodes
checks.remediation: OpenSearch dedicated master nodes are disabled or ClusterConfig.DedicatedMasterCount is below three, leaving this control without its required quorum.

caveats: The check reads configured count, not healthy master quorum. Some older instance types lack three-AZ support; plan a compatible type and node capacity before changing production.

iac.code: Declare ClusterConfig.DedicatedMasterEnabled=true, DedicatedMasterCount>=3 and a supported master instance type in the owner-managed domain configuration.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect dedicated-master enablement, count and instance type, node health, AZ support and current domain load.
Have the search owner choose three compatible dedicated master nodes and approve capacity, cost and blue/green change timing.
Apply the reviewed cluster configuration, then verify dedicated master enablement, count of at least three and healthy quorum.
remediation_details.summary: OpenSearch dedicated master nodes are disabled or ClusterConfig.DedicatedMasterCount is below three, leaving this control without its required quorum.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when dedicated master nodes are disabled or DedicatedMasterCount is below three. Too few dedicated masters can prevent cluster elections and interrupt indexing or search during a node failure.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when dedicated master nodes are disabled or DedicatedMasterCount is below three. Too few dedicated masters can prevent cluster elections and interrupt indexing or search during a node failure.
checks.pass_when: Dedicated masters are enabled with count at least three.
checks.fail_when: Dedicated master nodes are disabled or DedicatedMasterCount is below three.

checks.title: OpenSearch domain enables Cognito authentication for Dashboards
checks.remediation: OpenSearch CognitoOptions.Enabled is false, so this control finds no Cognito authentication gate for Dashboards.

caveats: This check requires Cognito specifically; a working SAML or IAM login does not make it pass. Pool IDs and service role are owner-supplied, and merely setting Enabled does not prove users can sign in.

iac.code: Declare CognitoOptions.Enabled=true with reviewed UserPoolId, IdentityPoolId and RoleArn, plus supported browser sign-in and role mapping.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect current Dashboards sign-in, CognitoOptions, user pool, identity pool, service role and domain access policy.
Have identity and search owners approve pool configuration, least-privilege roles and user migration without interrupting existing Dashboards users.
Apply reviewed CognitoOptions, test authenticated and denied browser sessions, and verify Enabled=true on the domain.
remediation_details.summary: OpenSearch CognitoOptions.Enabled is false, so this control finds no Cognito authentication gate for Dashboards.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when CognitoOptions.Enabled is not true. Weak identity controls can let an unintended principal act on the opensearch domain or its data.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when CognitoOptions.Enabled is not true. Weak identity controls can let an unintended principal act on the opensearch domain or its data.
checks.pass_when: CognitoOptions.Enabled is true.
checks.fail_when: CognitoOptions.Enabled is not true.

checks.title: OpenSearch domain enables Cognito or SAML authentication for Dashboards
checks.remediation: Neither CognitoOptions.Enabled nor AdvancedSecurityOptions.SAMLOptions.Enabled is true for OpenSearch Dashboards authentication.

caveats: The evaluator accepts either option, but does not prove correct IdP metadata or role mapping. SAML requires fine-grained access control and an identity-provider setup; do not interpolate metadata or secrets into commands.

cli.label: Apply reviewed Cognito or SAML configuration

iac.code: Declare either CognitoOptions.Enabled=true with validated pools and role or AdvancedSecurityOptions.SAMLOptions.Enabled=true with tested IdP metadata and role mappings.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect both identity option fields and existing Dashboards clients, IdP metadata and role mappings.
Have the identity owner choose and stage Cognito or SAML with a tested master user, service role or SAML metadata as appropriate.
Apply the reviewed identity path, verify at least one evaluated Enabled field is true, and test authorized and denied Dashboards sessions.
remediation_details.summary: Neither CognitoOptions.Enabled nor AdvancedSecurityOptions.SAMLOptions.Enabled is true for OpenSearch Dashboards authentication.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when neither CognitoOptions.Enabled nor AdvancedSecurityOptions.SAMLOptions.Enabled is true. Weak identity controls can let an unintended principal act on the opensearch domain or its data.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when neither CognitoOptions.Enabled nor AdvancedSecurityOptions.SAMLOptions.Enabled is true. Weak identity controls can let an unintended principal act on the opensearch domain or its data.
checks.pass_when: Either Cognito or SAML Dashboards authentication is enabled.
checks.fail_when: Neither CognitoOptions.Enabled nor AdvancedSecurityOptions.SAMLOptions.Enabled is true.

checks.remediation: OpenSearch SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS or INDEX_SLOW_LOGS publication is disabled; this check requires both log types enabled.

caveats: Enabled flags alone do not guarantee events; shard slow logs remain quiet until index thresholds are set and requests exceed them. Log publication can increase cost and reveal query data, so access and retention require review.

cli.label: Apply reviewed search and index slow log publication

iac.code: Declare SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS.Enabled=true and INDEX_SLOW_LOGS.Enabled=true with reviewed CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn values and corresponding index-level threshold policy.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect both log-publishing options, destination group ARNs, policies and current per-index slow-log thresholds.
Have the search owner approve separate or shared CloudWatch destinations, retention and meaningful index thresholds.
Enable both reviewed log types, configure thresholds on the relevant indexes and verify fields and delivered slow events.
remediation_details.summary: OpenSearch SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS or INDEX_SLOW_LOGS publication is disabled; this check requires both log types enabled.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when either SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS.Enabled or INDEX_SLOW_LOGS.Enabled is not true. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the opensearch domain is absent or delayed.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when either SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS.Enabled or INDEX_SLOW_LOGS.Enabled is not true. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the opensearch domain is absent or delayed.
checks.pass_when: Both slow-log types have Enabled true.
checks.fail_when: Either SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS.Enabled or INDEX_SLOW_LOGS.Enabled is not true.

checks.remediation: OpenSearch log publishing options are absent, or an enabled audit, slow or application log type lacks CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn.

caveats: An empty but present LogPublishingOptions map passes this evaluator; it does not require any log type to be enabled. Destination presence does not prove resource-policy permission or successful delivery.

iac.code: Declare CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn for every enabled AUDIT_LOGS, INDEX_SLOW_LOGS, SEARCH_SLOW_LOGS and ES_APPLICATION_LOGS map entry, with group policy and retention.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect the complete LogPublishingOptions map and identify every enabled type without a CloudWatch log group ARN.
Have logging and search owners approve destination groups, least-privilege service delivery policy and retention for each enabled type.
Apply the reviewed log map, verify every enabled type has an ARN and confirm actual CloudWatch events separately.
remediation_details.summary: OpenSearch log publishing options are absent, or an enabled audit, slow or application log type lacks CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when LogPublishingOptions is absent or an enabled audit, error, search-slow, or index-slow log type lacks CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the opensearch domain is absent or delayed.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when LogPublishingOptions is absent or an enabled audit, error, search-slow, or index-slow log type lacks CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the opensearch domain is absent or delayed.
checks.pass_when: Publishing options exist and every enabled log type has a log group ARN.
checks.fail_when: LogPublishingOptions is absent or an enabled audit, error, search-slow, or index-slow log type lacks CloudWatchLogsLogGroupArn.

checks.remediation: OpenSearch lacks a VPCId or a listed domain subnet has an explicit route-table association with an Internet Gateway default route.

caveats: AWS cannot move an existing public-endpoint domain into a VPC in place. This evaluator only checks explicitly associated route tables for a 0.0.0.0/0 Internet Gateway route; it does not inspect main-table inheritance or effective reachability.

cli.label: Inspect VPC subnets and route associations

iac.code: For a public endpoint, declare a replacement domain with VPCOptions.VPCId and approved private SubnetIds, then explicitly plan snapshot or reindex migration and DNS/client cutover. For an existing VPC domain, change subnets only after route review.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect VPCOptions, every domain subnet and explicit route-table association, plus client connectivity and current domain endpoint type.
For an existing public-endpoint domain, have the owner design a replacement VPC domain with private subnets, data migration, snapshot recovery and DNS/client cutover.
Create the reviewed replacement where required, migrate and validate data and private access, then verify the new VPCId and subnet routes.
remediation_details.summary: OpenSearch lacks a VPCId or a listed domain subnet has an explicit route-table association with an Internet Gateway default route.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when the domain lacks VPCOptions.VPCId or any listed VPC subnet is explicitly public under the route-table test. The network path can expose the opensearch domain to traffic from outside its intended boundary.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when the domain lacks VPCOptions.VPCId or any listed VPC subnet is explicitly public under the route-table test. The network path can expose the opensearch domain to traffic from outside its intended boundary.
checks.pass_when: VPCId exists and none of its listed subnets is public.
checks.fail_when: The domain lacks VPCOptions.VPCId or any listed VPC subnet is explicitly public under the route-table test.

checks.remediation: A public-endpoint OpenSearch domain has an AccessPolicies document that grants public principals without a sufficiently scoped trust boundary.

caveats: Domains with VPCId pass without inspecting the policy, and an absent policy also passes; neither proves private reachability. Restricting an access policy can immediately block workloads, so the replacement document needs owner approval and rollback.

cli.label: Apply owner-reviewed full access policy document

iac.code: Replace AccessPolicies with a full owner-reviewed principal, action, resource and condition policy in the domain declaration; preserve an explicit rollback and test client authentication.
iac.label: Review the domain owner declaration

steps: Inspect VPCOptions and the full current AccessPolicies JSON, explicit principals, actions, resources and conditions against the audited account.
Have the identity and search owners create a reviewed replacement policy scoped to intended principals or private source IPs; test signed and browser clients before narrowing access.
Apply the reviewed access policy, test denied public requests and intended clients, then rerun the exact policy check.
remediation_details.summary: A public-endpoint OpenSearch domain has an AccessPolicies document that grants public principals without a sufficiently scoped trust boundary.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when a domain outside a VPC has a public access-policy Allow statement. This can give unintended external principals a route to the opensearch domain or its data.
checks.description: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when a domain outside a VPC has a public access-policy Allow statement. This can give unintended external principals a route to the opensearch domain or its data.
checks.pass_when: A non-VPC domain's access policy is not public.
checks.fail_when: A domain outside a VPC has a public access-policy Allow statement.

checks.title: ActiveMQ broker uses the active/standby Multi-AZ deployment mode
checks.remediation: ActiveMQ Configuration.DeploymentMode must be ACTIVE_STANDBY_MULTI_AZ; SINGLE_INSTANCE lacks standby broker failover.

caveats: DeploymentMode is absent from UpdateBroker and cannot be changed in place; replacement can change endpoints and interrupt clients.

iac.code: Create an ActiveMQ replacement with ACTIVE_STANDBY_MULTI_AZ, migrate configuration, users and clients, test failover, then retire the original. Update endpoint, client, queue and logging dependencies in the owner-managed infrastructure declaration with a rollback plan.
iac.label: Review the broker owner declaration

steps: Confirm EngineType is ACTIVEMQ and inspect DeploymentMode on the exact broker.
Create an ActiveMQ replacement with ACTIVE_STANDBY_MULTI_AZ, migrate configuration, users and clients, test failover, then retire the original.
Recollect the broker configuration and rerun the exact check; verify client access or log delivery separately.
remediation_details.summary: ActiveMQ Configuration.DeploymentMode must be ACTIVE_STANDBY_MULTI_AZ; SINGLE_INSTANCE lacks standby broker failover.

checks.rationale: For each mq broker, the evaluator flags FAIL when an ActiveMQ broker's DeploymentMode is not ACTIVE_STANDBY_MULTI_AZ. A zonal failure can interrupt the mq broker when the surviving zone lacks a usable replica.
checks.description: For each mq broker, the evaluator flags FAIL when an ActiveMQ broker's DeploymentMode is not ACTIVE_STANDBY_MULTI_AZ. A zonal failure can interrupt the mq broker when the surviving zone lacks a usable replica.
checks.pass_when: Its DeploymentMode is ACTIVE_STANDBY_MULTI_AZ.
checks.fail_when: An ActiveMQ broker's DeploymentMode is not ACTIVE_STANDBY_MULTI_AZ.
checks.not_applicable_when: EngineType is not ACTIVEMQ.

checks.title: RabbitMQ broker uses the cluster Multi-AZ deployment mode
checks.remediation: RabbitMQ Configuration.DeploymentMode must be CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ; SINGLE_INSTANCE lacks cluster-zone redundancy.

caveats: DeploymentMode is absent from UpdateBroker; queue migration and endpoint changes can cause message loss or downtime without a cutover plan.

iac.code: Console/IaC fields to compare in the owned resource and referenced inventory: Configuration.EngineType,Configuration.DeploymentMode. Create a RabbitMQ replacement with CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ, migrate definitions and queues under owner review, test client reconnect and failover, then retire the source. Update endpoint, client, queue and logging dependencies in the owner-managed infrastructure declaration with a rollback plan.
iac.label: Review the broker owner declaration

steps: Confirm EngineType is RABBITMQ and inspect the exact DeploymentMode.
Create a RabbitMQ replacement with CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ, migrate definitions and queues under owner review, test client reconnect and failover, then retire the source.
Recollect the broker configuration and rerun the exact check; verify client access or log delivery separately.
remediation_details.summary: RabbitMQ Configuration.DeploymentMode must be CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ; SINGLE_INSTANCE lacks cluster-zone redundancy.

checks.rationale: For each mq broker, the evaluator flags FAIL when a RabbitMQ broker's DeploymentMode is not CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ. A single-instance RabbitMQ broker can stop message delivery when its host or Availability Zone fails.
checks.description: For each mq broker, the evaluator flags FAIL when a RabbitMQ broker's DeploymentMode is not CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ. A single-instance RabbitMQ broker can stop message delivery when its host or Availability Zone fails.
checks.pass_when: Its DeploymentMode is CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ.
checks.fail_when: A RabbitMQ broker's DeploymentMode is not CLUSTER_MULTI_AZ.
checks.not_applicable_when: EngineType is not RABBITMQ.

checks.title: ActiveMQ broker publishes audit logs
checks.remediation: ActiveMQ Configuration.Logs.Audit must be true; false omits audit events from CloudWatch Logs.

caveats: RabbitMQ audit logging is NOT_APPLICABLE; broker changes may apply at a maintenance window and logging adds cost.

cli.label: Apply only the owner-reviewed broker change

iac.code: Enable ActiveMQ audit log publishing under owner review, configure retention and verify that audit events arrive. Update endpoint, client, queue and logging dependencies in the owner-managed infrastructure declaration with a rollback plan.
iac.label: Review the broker owner declaration

steps: Confirm EngineType is ACTIVEMQ and inspect the Audit log flag and destination permissions.
Enable ActiveMQ audit log publishing under owner review, configure retention and verify that audit events arrive.
Recollect the broker configuration and rerun the exact check; verify client access or log delivery separately.
remediation_details.summary: ActiveMQ Configuration.Logs.Audit must be true; false omits audit events from CloudWatch Logs.

checks.rationale: For each mq broker, the evaluator flags FAIL when an ActiveMQ broker's Logs.Audit is not true. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the mq broker is absent or delayed.
checks.description: For each mq broker, the evaluator flags FAIL when an ActiveMQ broker's Logs.Audit is not true. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the mq broker is absent or delayed.
checks.pass_when: Logs.Audit is true.
checks.fail_when: An ActiveMQ broker's Logs.Audit is not true.
checks.not_applicable_when: EngineType is not ACTIVEMQ.

checks.remediation: ActiveMQ requires both General and Audit logs, while RabbitMQ requires General; missing required log publishing fails.

caveats: The correct log fields depend on broker engine; an unreviewed generic update can disable other logging or incur cost.

cli.label: Apply only the owner-reviewed broker change

iac.code: Submit an owner-reviewed log configuration with General enabled and Audit enabled for ActiveMQ, then verify CloudWatch delivery and retention. Update endpoint, client, queue and logging dependencies in the owner-managed infrastructure declaration with a rollback plan.
iac.label: Review the broker owner declaration

steps: Inspect EngineType and both log flags; evaluate the engine-specific requirement before choosing an update.
Submit an owner-reviewed log configuration with General enabled and Audit enabled for ActiveMQ, then verify CloudWatch delivery and retention.
Recollect the broker configuration and rerun the exact check; verify client access or log delivery separately.
remediation_details.summary: ActiveMQ requires both General and Audit logs, while RabbitMQ requires General; missing required log publishing fails.

checks.rationale: For each mq broker, the evaluator flags FAIL when an ActiveMQ broker lacks either Logs.General or Logs.Audit, or another broker lacks Logs.General. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the mq broker is absent or delayed.
checks.description: For each mq broker, the evaluator flags FAIL when an ActiveMQ broker lacks either Logs.General or Logs.Audit, or another broker lacks Logs.General. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the mq broker is absent or delayed.
checks.pass_when: Required general and, for ActiveMQ, audit logs are enabled.
checks.fail_when: An ActiveMQ broker lacks General or Audit logging, a RabbitMQ broker lacks General logging, or the engine is neither ActiveMQ nor RabbitMQ.

checks.title: MSK provisioned cluster encrypts data volumes with a customer managed KMS key
checks.remediation: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when its data-volume KMS key is absent or does not resolve to a CUSTOMER-managed key in the collected KMS inventory.

caveats: MSK Serverless passes this provisioned-only condition. AWS documents that the encryption-at-rest key cannot be changed on an existing cluster even though a modeled security request shape includes EncryptionAtRest. A missing KMS inventory is UNKNOWN, not proof of an AWS-managed key.

cli.label: Inspect exact cluster, version and provisioned settings

iac.code: In a new cluster declaration, set Provisioned.EncryptionInfo.EncryptionAtRest.DataVolumeKMSKeyId to a reviewed key whose kms_key.KeyManager is CUSTOMER. Preserve topic configuration, client authentication and replication, migrate offsets and verify KMS grants and data continuity.
iac.label: Review the MSK cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect DataVolumeKMSKeyId, resolve its KMS KeyManager and review the key policy and grants for the cluster.
Have the streaming and KMS owners design a replacement cluster using an approved customer-managed key; existing at-rest encryption cannot be switched in place.
Migrate topics, data, offsets, producers and consumers through a tested cutover, then verify the new cluster key and traffic.
remediation_details.summary: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when its data-volume KMS key is absent or does not resolve to a CUSTOMER-managed key in the collected KMS inventory.

checks.rationale: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when an MSK provisioned cluster does not declare a customer-managed KMS key for broker storage. An AWS-managed default key gives the account less control over key policy and disable or rotation decisions for this data.
checks.description: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when an MSK provisioned cluster does not declare a customer-managed KMS key for broker storage. An AWS-managed default key gives the account less control over key policy and disable or rotation decisions for this data.
checks.pass_when: Broker storage names a customer-managed KMS key, or the cluster is Serverless and AWS manages this setting.
checks.fail_when: An MSK provisioned cluster does not declare a customer-managed KMS key for broker storage.
