checks.remediation: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when EnhancedMonitoring is DEFAULT or omitted, leaving broker-level monitoring below the selected level.

caveats: MSK Serverless passes this provisioned-only condition. The condition checks only for a level above DEFAULT; it does not prove alarms exist or metrics are consumed. Enhanced monitoring can increase CloudWatch charges.

cli.label: Inspect exact cluster, version and provisioned settings
Set an owner-approved broker monitoring level

iac.code: Set Provisioned.EnhancedMonitoring to PER_BROKER or an approved higher level in the cluster owner declaration, retain the current-version precondition and verify useful broker metrics and alerting.
iac.label: Review the MSK cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect EnhancedMonitoring, current CloudWatch metrics usage, broker count and monitoring budget.
Have the streaming owner approve PER_BROKER or a more detailed level and any related dashboard and retention changes.
Update monitoring with the current cluster version and verify broker metrics and costs after the operation completes.
remediation_details.summary: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when EnhancedMonitoring is DEFAULT or omitted, leaving broker-level monitoring below the selected level.

checks.rationale: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when EnhancedMonitoring is DEFAULT rather than a broker-level enhanced mode. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the msk cluster is absent or delayed.
checks.description: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when EnhancedMonitoring is DEFAULT rather than a broker-level enhanced mode. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the msk cluster is absent or delayed.
checks.pass_when: EnhancedMonitoring is not DEFAULT, or the cluster is Serverless and AWS manages this setting.
checks.fail_when: EnhancedMonitoring is DEFAULT rather than a broker-level enhanced mode.

checks.remediation: A provisioned MSK cluster fails unless client-broker encryption is TLS and broker-to-broker InCluster encryption is true.

caveats: MSK Serverless passes this provisioned-only condition. AWS permits an update to client-broker encryption but not InCluster, despite the API shape containing both fields. TLS can require client truststore changes and affect throughput.

cli.label: Inspect exact cluster, version and provisioned settings
Update only client-broker TLS when InCluster is already true

iac.code: Require Provisioned.EncryptionInfo.EncryptionInTransit.ClientBroker=TLS and InCluster=true. Use UpdateSecurity only for ClientBroker when InCluster already passes; otherwise create a replacement cluster, migrate clients and verify encrypted broker traffic.
iac.label: Review the MSK cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect ClientBroker and InCluster, current authentication, all Kafka client TLS settings and the cluster update version.
If InCluster is false, have the streaming owner build a replacement cluster with both encryption settings; broker-to-broker encryption cannot be changed in place.
If only ClientBroker is not TLS, stage TLS-ready clients and apply an owner-reviewed security update; verify producers, consumers and broker links after cutover.
remediation_details.summary: A provisioned MSK cluster fails unless client-broker encryption is TLS and broker-to-broker InCluster encryption is true.

checks.rationale: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when client-broker encryption is not TLS or in-cluster encryption is not enabled. Client or service traffic may be intercepted or modified before it reaches the msk cluster.
checks.description: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when client-broker encryption is not TLS or in-cluster encryption is not enabled. Client or service traffic may be intercepted or modified before it reaches the msk cluster.
checks.pass_when: TLS client-broker and in-cluster encryption are both enabled, or the cluster is Serverless and AWS manages this setting.
checks.fail_when: Client-broker encryption is not TLS or in-cluster encryption is not enabled.

checks.title: MSK provisioned cluster client-broker encryption is TLS only
checks.remediation: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when ClientBroker is not TLS, allowing plaintext or mixed client-broker listeners.

caveats: MSK Serverless is not applicable to this provisioned-only check. AWS can update ClientBroker but not broker-to-broker InCluster encryption; changing listeners before client cutover can interrupt all traffic.

cli.label: Inspect exact cluster, version and provisioned settings

iac.code: Set Provisioned.EncryptionInfo.EncryptionInTransit.ClientBroker=TLS in the cluster owner declaration, preserve supported authentication settings and verify every producer and consumer migrates to TLS before disabling mixed listeners.
iac.label: Review the MSK cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect ClientBroker, authentication mode, cluster current version and all producer and consumer TLS readiness.
Have the streaming owner move clients to TLS listeners and approve a complete reviewed encryption-in-transit update.
Update client-broker encryption to TLS and verify intended clients still connect while plaintext access is rejected.
remediation_details.summary: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when ClientBroker is not TLS, allowing plaintext or mixed client-broker listeners.

checks.rationale: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when the MSK cluster's client-broker encryption is not TLS only. Client or service traffic may be intercepted or modified before it reaches the msk cluster.
checks.description: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when the MSK cluster's client-broker encryption is not TLS only. Client or service traffic may be intercepted or modified before it reaches the msk cluster.
checks.pass_when: Client-broker traffic uses TLS only.
checks.fail_when: The MSK cluster's client-broker encryption is not TLS only.
checks.not_applicable_when: ClusterType is SERVERLESS.

checks.remediation: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when PublicAccess.Type differs from DISABLED, leaving public broker connectivity configured.

caveats: MSK Serverless passes this condition as a private service. An unreported PublicAccess.Type is UNKNOWN, not an automatic public finding. Disabling public endpoints before client migration can interrupt producers and consumers.

cli.label: Inspect exact cluster, version and provisioned settings

iac.code: Set Provisioned.BrokerNodeGroupInfo.ConnectivityInfo.PublicAccess.Type=DISABLED in the owner declaration, preserve private VPC connectivity and migrate clients through approved network paths before the update.
iac.label: Review the MSK cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect PublicAccess.Type, current broker endpoints, client locations, VPC connectivity and cluster version.
Have network and streaming owners establish private broker access and migrate external clients before changing connectivity.
Apply a reviewed ConnectivityInfo with PublicAccess.Type=DISABLED and verify private clients work and public endpoints are unavailable.
remediation_details.summary: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when PublicAccess.Type differs from DISABLED, leaving public broker connectivity configured.

checks.rationale: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when Provisioned.BrokerNodeGroupInfo.ConnectivityInfo.PublicAccess.Type is not DISABLED. This can give unintended external principals a route to the msk cluster or its data.
checks.description: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when Provisioned.BrokerNodeGroupInfo.ConnectivityInfo.PublicAccess.Type is not DISABLED. This can give unintended external principals a route to the msk cluster or its data.
checks.pass_when: Public broker access Type is DISABLED, or the cluster is Serverless and private with IAM authentication.

checks.title: MSK provisioned cluster enables mutual TLS client authentication
checks.remediation: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when ClientAuthentication.Tls.Enabled is not true, so mutual TLS client authentication is not enabled.

caveats: MSK Serverless passes this provisioned-only condition under its managed authentication model. Enabling mTLS without broker TLS and provisioned client certificates can block all clients; preserve any IAM or SASL settings in the reviewed document.

cli.label: Inspect exact cluster, version and provisioned settings

iac.code: Set Provisioned.ClientAuthentication.Tls.Enabled=true in the cluster owner declaration with approved Private CA ARNs and client certificate lifecycle. Preserve other authentication modes and verify mutual TLS for every client.
iac.label: Review the MSK cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect existing client authentication, broker TLS setting, certificate authorities and the current cluster version.
Have identity and streaming owners approve a Private CA trust chain, certificate issuance and TLS-capable clients before enabling mTLS.
Apply a complete reviewed client-authentication update and verify authorized certificates connect while untrusted clients fail.
remediation_details.summary: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when ClientAuthentication.Tls.Enabled is not true, so mutual TLS client authentication is not enabled.

checks.rationale: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when Provisioned.ClientAuthentication.Tls.Enabled is false. Without client certificates, a broker may accept clients that cannot prove an approved identity.
checks.description: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when Provisioned.ClientAuthentication.Tls.Enabled is false. Without client certificates, a broker may accept clients that cannot prove an approved identity.
checks.pass_when: The provisioned cluster has mutual TLS client authentication enabled, or the cluster is Serverless and AWS manages this setting.
checks.fail_when: Provisioned.ClientAuthentication.Tls.Enabled is false.

checks.title: MSK cluster does not allow unauthenticated access
checks.remediation: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when ClientAuthentication.Unauthenticated.Enabled is true, allowing clients without an authentication method.

caveats: MSK Serverless passes under IAM authentication. An omitted flag is UNKNOWN in this check, not a safe false. Disabling unauthenticated access before all clients migrate can halt producers and consumers.

cli.label: Inspect exact cluster, version and provisioned settings

iac.code: Set Provisioned.ClientAuthentication.Unauthenticated.Enabled=false while preserving approved IAM, SASL or TLS mechanisms. Stage all client credential changes, then verify anonymous denial and data-flow continuity.
iac.label: Review the MSK cluster owner declaration

steps: Inspect the unauthenticated flag, active client mechanisms and current cluster version; an omitted flag requires evidence review.
Have the streaming owner migrate every client to reviewed IAM, SASL/SCRAM or mutual TLS authentication with compatible broker encryption.
Apply the reviewed client-authentication document disabling unauthenticated access and verify legitimate clients and rejected anonymous connections.
remediation_details.summary: A provisioned MSK cluster fails when ClientAuthentication.Unauthenticated.Enabled is true, allowing clients without an authentication method.

checks.rationale: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when Provisioned.ClientAuthentication.Unauthenticated.Enabled is true. Weak identity controls can let an unintended principal act on the msk cluster or its data.
checks.description: For each msk cluster, the evaluator flags FAIL when Provisioned.ClientAuthentication.Unauthenticated.Enabled is true. Weak identity controls can let an unintended principal act on the msk cluster or its data.
checks.pass_when: Unauthenticated client access is false, or the cluster is Serverless and private with IAM authentication.
checks.fail_when: Provisioned.ClientAuthentication.Unauthenticated.Enabled is true.

checks.title: MSK provisioned cluster runs an ACTIVE Kafka version with no newer compatible update
frameworks: ASD Essential Eight Maturity Model - Maturity Level One (AWS)

controls.framework: ASD Essential Eight Maturity Model - Maturity Level One (AWS)
ASD Essential Eight Maturity Model - Maturity Level One (AWS)

checks.remediation: Plan a supported MSK Kafka version upgrade for a deprecated broker version or an available newer compatible target.

caveats: MSK Serverless is NOT_APPLICABLE. Broker type matters: Standard and Express can have different supported targets. An older or incomparable target, an ambiguous/missing cluster-specific source row, or incomplete version inventory remains UNKNOWN, not a reason to upgrade.

A deprecated current version can fail even when no safe target is currently available; in that case use owner/AWS support review and do not run the update example. Version downgrades are unsupported, and this check does not establish client compatibility or unattended upgrade safety.

The --current-version argument is the MSK cluster Version concurrency token from DescribeClusterV2, not the Apache Kafka version string. A rolling upgrade can affect clients and availability; verify the returned operation and workload health.

cli.label: Inspect the exact MSK cluster and current-version token
Inspect update targets compatible with this cluster
Upgrade only to a reviewed, cluster-compatible ACTIVE target

iac.code: Set Provisioned.CurrentBrokerSoftwareInfo.KafkaVersion only to a cluster-specific compatible ACTIVE target after client and availability review; preserve the current cluster Version concurrency token for the update and monitor the rolling operation. Do not select the global ListKafkaVersions maximum.
iac.label: Review the owner-controlled MSK version declaration

references.title: Amazon MSK Apache Kafka version upgrade procedure
Amazon MSK version upgrade best practices

steps: Inspect the exact provisioned cluster ARN, broker type, current KafkaVersion, ListKafkaVersions status and its own GetCompatibleKafkaVersions SourceVersion row. A deprecated current version fails independently; an ACTIVE current version fails only for a provably newer ACTIVE target returned for this cluster.

If the current version is deprecated but no valid compatible target is returned, investigate with the streaming owner and AWS support rather than selecting a global version or fabricating an upgrade path. Treat missing, older, malformed or incomparable target evidence as UNKNOWN until corrected.

For an actual cluster-specific newer ACTIVE target, review client compatibility, broker availability, partition replication, quotas, configuration compatibility, maintenance window and rollback with the streaming owner. Obtain the current cluster Version concurrency token from DescribeClusterV2 immediately before any approved change.

Only after that review, upgrade to the specifically returned compatible target, monitor the rolling operation and client health, then recollect KafkaVersion and both version inventories. A passing result means no newer ACTIVE target was reported for this cluster, not the globally newest Kafka release.
remediation_details.summary: Plan a supported MSK Kafka version upgrade for a deprecated broker version or an available newer compatible target.

checks.rationale: Checks a provisioned MSK cluster against its broker-type-compatible Kafka update targets returned by GetCompatibleKafkaVersions and listed ACTIVE/DEPRECATED version statuses. It does not trust ListKafkaVersions order or demand a globally newest version. Remediation: Review cluster-compatible ACTIVE target versions and plan a supported upgrade with the workload owner; do not assume the API list is ordered.
checks.description: Checks a provisioned MSK cluster against its broker-type-compatible Kafka update targets returned by GetCompatibleKafkaVersions and listed ACTIVE/DEPRECATED version statuses. It does not trust ListKafkaVersions order or demand a globally newest version. Remediation: Review cluster-compatible ACTIVE target versions and plan a supported upgrade with the workload owner; do not assume the API list is ordered.
checks.pass_when: The current version is ACTIVE and no newer ACTIVE compatible target is reported for this cluster.
checks.fail_when: The current version is DEPRECATED, or a newer ACTIVE compatible target exists; missing, ambiguous or malformed facts are UNKNOWN.
checks.not_applicable_when: Serverless clusters, whose Kafka version is managed by AWS.

checks.title: MSK Connect connector encrypts traffic to the cluster with TLS
frameworks: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) v1.1
National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) v2.0

controls.framework: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) v1.1
National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) Cybersecurity Framework (CSF) v2.0

checks.remediation: An MSK Connect connector fails when kafkaClusterEncryptionInTransit.encryptionType is not TLS, exposing connector-to-cluster traffic to plaintext transport.

caveats: The encryptionType field is accepted at CreateConnector but absent from UpdateConnector, so there is no in-place TLS flag. Replacement can duplicate messages, alter offsets and incur capacity cost; coordinate producer and consumer cutover.

cli.label: Inspect the exact MSK Connect connector
Create an owner-reviewed replacement connector from a complete document

iac.code: Set kafkaClusterEncryptionInTransit.encryptionType=TLS in a new connector declaration, preserving plugin, worker, authentication, network and offset settings. Test TLS and exactly-once assumptions before switching traffic.
iac.label: Review the connector owner declaration

steps: Inspect the current connector encryption type, target cluster listeners, authentication and plugin compatibility.
Have the streaming owner prepare a replacement connector with TLS and a reviewed certificate or trust chain; UpdateConnector cannot change this field.
Create the replacement, test connectivity and message offsets, cut over without duplicate processing and verify encryptionType=TLS.
remediation_details.summary: An MSK Connect connector fails when kafkaClusterEncryptionInTransit.encryptionType is not TLS, exposing connector-to-cluster traffic to plaintext transport.

checks.rationale: For each mskconnect connector, the evaluator flags FAIL when kafkaClusterEncryptionInTransit.encryptionType is not TLS. Client or service traffic may be intercepted or modified before it reaches the mskconnect connector.
checks.description: For each mskconnect connector, the evaluator flags FAIL when kafkaClusterEncryptionInTransit.encryptionType is not TLS. Client or service traffic may be intercepted or modified before it reaches the mskconnect connector.
checks.pass_when: The connector's cluster encryption type is TLS.
checks.fail_when: KafkaClusterEncryptionInTransit.encryptionType is not TLS.

checks.title: MSK Connect connector has log delivery configured
checks.remediation: An MSK Connect connector fails when logDelivery is absent from its summary, leaving worker log delivery unconfigured in the captured connector.

caveats: The condition checks only presence of logDelivery; a present but disabled or failing destination can still pass. logDelivery is create-time in the modeled API, so replacement is required, with possible offset and delivery impact.

cli.label: Inspect the exact MSK Connect connector
Create an owner-reviewed replacement connector from a complete document

iac.code: Define logDelivery.workerLogDelivery for a replacement connector, including a reviewed destination, retention and IAM permissions. Migrate plugin and offset settings, then verify actual worker log events rather than only a non-null field.
iac.label: Review the connector owner declaration

steps: Inspect logDelivery and the connector worker logging needs, destination permissions, retention and sensitive record handling.
Have the streaming and logging owners prepare a replacement connector with reviewed workerLogDelivery settings; UpdateConnector does not expose logDelivery.
Create the replacement, validate message processing and actual worker logs, then cut over and retire the old connector through a separate plan.
remediation_details.summary: An MSK Connect connector fails when logDelivery is absent from its summary, leaving worker log delivery unconfigured in the captured connector.

checks.rationale: For each mskconnect connector, the evaluator flags FAIL when logDelivery is absent from the connector summary. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the mskconnect connector is absent or delayed.
checks.description: For each mskconnect connector, the evaluator flags FAIL when logDelivery is absent from the connector summary. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the mskconnect connector is absent or delayed.
checks.pass_when: LogDelivery is present, regardless of its worker destinations.
checks.fail_when: LogDelivery is absent from the connector summary.

checks.title: SNS topic logs delivery status with a failure feedback role
frameworks: AWS Australian Cyber Security Center (ACSC) Essential Eight

controls.framework: AWS Australian Cyber Security Center (ACSC) Essential Eight

checks.remediation: An SNS topic fails when none of its protocol-specific FailureFeedbackRoleArn attributes is set, leaving delivery-failure status without a configured feedback role.

caveats: The condition passes when any one failure role is present and does not prove every protocol logs failures. A role ARN alone does not prove trust, permissions or log delivery; configure each used protocol separately.

cli.label: Set an owner-reviewed protocol failure feedback role

iac.code: In topic Attributes, configure the actual ApplicationFailureFeedbackRoleArn, FirehoseFailureFeedbackRoleArn, HTTPFailureFeedbackRoleArn, LambdaFailureFeedbackRoleArn or SQSFailureFeedbackRoleArn for each used protocol, with reviewed role trust, CloudWatch Logs grants and retention. Test a delivery failure.
iac.label: Review the SNS owner declaration

steps: Inspect the topic attributes and list its active subscription protocols and owners.
Have the SNS and IAM owners choose the matching protocol failure-feedback role, verify sns.amazonaws.com trust and CloudWatch Logs permissions, then approve logging retention.
Set the reviewed protocol-specific FailureFeedbackRoleArn attribute and verify actual failed-delivery status logs.
remediation_details.summary: An SNS topic fails when none of its protocol-specific FailureFeedbackRoleArn attributes is set, leaving delivery-failure status without a configured feedback role.

checks.rationale: Flags an SNS topic when none of the configured delivery protocol failure-feedback role attributes has an ARN. Failed message deliveries may not be reported to operators.
checks.description: Flags an SNS topic when none of the configured delivery protocol failure-feedback role attributes has an ARN. Failed message deliveries may not be reported to operators.
checks.pass_when: PASS when at least one failure-feedback role ARN is configured.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when none of the configured delivery protocol failure-feedback role attributes has an ARN.

checks.title: SNS topic policy has no unrestricted wildcard-principal Allow
checks.remediation: An SNS topic fails when its Policy contains an Allow wildcard-principal statement without a recognized restricting condition.

caveats: An absent readable Policy passes this condition. The restriction parser recognizes only selected condition forms; arbitrary Condition text is not proof of constrained access. Policy replacement can break existing fanout.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, remove unrestricted wildcard Allow statements or bind them to approved principals and recognized source-account, source-ARN or organization conditions. Preserve tested service integration grants and audit publication and subscription results.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect all Allow statements with wildcard principals, their actions and the exact Condition operators and keys.
Have the topic policy owner replace unrestricted grants with reviewed principals or restrictive source-account, source-ARN or organization conditions for the real publishers and subscribers.
Apply the complete reviewed topic Policy and verify authorized publication and subscription alongside denied unauthorized callers.
remediation_details.summary: An SNS topic fails when its Policy contains an Allow wildcard-principal statement without a recognized restricting condition.

checks.rationale: Flags an SNS topic when the topic policy has an unrestricted public Allow statement. It can permit an outside principal to invoke or read the service resource without the intended trust boundary.
checks.description: Flags an SNS topic when the topic policy has an unrestricted public Allow statement. It can permit an outside principal to invoke or read the service resource without the intended trust boundary.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the topic policy has no unrestricted public Allow statement.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the topic policy has an unrestricted public Allow statement.

checks.title: SNS topic policy does not allow public access (perimeter)
checks.remediation: An SNS topic fails the perimeter condition when its Policy allows a wildcard principal without an effective recognized restriction.

caveats: A topic with no readable Policy is not applicable here, unlike the similar strict topic control. A condition must actually constrain the caller; simply adding any condition is insufficient.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, express publisher and subscriber access with reviewed principals and effective restrictive conditions. Retain authorized fanout, test external denial and document any approved perimeter exception.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect the topic Policy and enumerate public-facing Allow statements, including condition keys and actual caller context.
Have the security and topic owners approve explicit principals or a supported restrictive source or organization condition that preserves required integrations.
Apply the reviewed replacement Policy and verify the perimeter behavior and expected delivery paths.
remediation_details.summary: An SNS topic fails the perimeter condition when its Policy allows a wildcard principal without an effective recognized restriction.

checks.rationale: Flags an SNS topic when the topic policy contains a Turbot-style public Allow statement. It can permit an outside principal to invoke or read the service resource without the intended trust boundary.
checks.description: Flags an SNS topic when the topic policy contains a Turbot-style public Allow statement. It can permit an outside principal to invoke or read the service resource without the intended trust boundary.
checks.pass_when: PASS when no topic policy statement matches that public access test.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the topic policy contains a Turbot-style public Allow statement.
checks.not_applicable_when: When the resource policy is absent.

checks.title: SNS topic policy does not let everyone publish without conditions
checks.remediation: An SNS topic fails when its Policy explicitly allows sns:Publish to a wildcard principal without a Condition block, permitting unrestricted publication.

caveats: This condition matches explicit sns:Publish only and does not match a wildcard action such as sns:*; it also skips any statement with a Condition block, even one that is ineffective. Review effective access separately.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, remove unconditioned wildcard Allow grants with explicit sns:Publish and replace them with scoped publisher permissions. Audit sns:* and ineffective Condition cases as a separate effective-access review.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect the complete Policy for Allow wildcard-principal statements whose explicit Action includes sns:Publish.
Have the topic owner replace the grant with approved publisher principals and source conditions, preserving legitimate event producers.
Apply the reviewed Policy document and verify authorized publish calls and denial for an unapproved publisher.
remediation_details.summary: An SNS topic fails when its Policy explicitly allows sns:Publish to a wildcard principal without a Condition block, permitting unrestricted publication.

checks.rationale: Flags an SNS topic when an unconditioned public principal can invoke `sns:Publish` through the topic policy. It can permit an outside principal to invoke or read the service resource without the intended trust boundary.
checks.description: Flags an SNS topic when an unconditioned public principal can invoke `sns:Publish` through the topic policy. It can permit an outside principal to invoke or read the service resource without the intended trust boundary.
checks.pass_when: PASS when no unconditioned public statement grants Publish.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when an unconditioned public principal can invoke `sns:Publish` through the topic policy.

checks.title: SNS topic policy does not let everyone subscribe or receive without conditions
checks.remediation: An SNS topic fails when its Policy explicitly allows sns:Subscribe or sns:Receive to a wildcard principal without a Condition block, permitting unreviewed consumers.

caveats: The action matcher does not catch sns:* or a grant with any Condition block, even if that condition is weak. Changing subscription rights can interrupt new enrollments but does not remove existing subscriptions.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, scope explicit sns:Subscribe and sns:Receive Allow grants to approved principals and conditions. Separately inspect wildcard actions and current subscriptions; validate delivery after policy rollout.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect Policy Allow statements with wildcard principals and explicit sns:Subscribe or sns:Receive actions.
Have the topic owner identify approved subscriber identities and endpoint enrollment flow, then replace the unconditioned public grant.
Apply the reviewed Policy and verify expected subscriptions still work while an unapproved account cannot subscribe or receive.
remediation_details.summary: An SNS topic fails when its Policy explicitly allows sns:Subscribe or sns:Receive to a wildcard principal without a Condition block, permitting unreviewed consumers.

checks.rationale: Flags an SNS topic when an unconditioned public principal can invoke `sns:Subscribe` or `sns:Receive` through the topic policy. It can permit an outside principal to invoke or read the service resource without the intended trust boundary.
checks.description: Flags an SNS topic when an unconditioned public principal can invoke `sns:Subscribe` or `sns:Receive` through the topic policy. It can permit an outside principal to invoke or read the service resource without the intended trust boundary.
checks.pass_when: PASS when no unconditioned public statement grants Subscribe or Receive.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when an unconditioned public principal can invoke `sns:Subscribe` or `sns:Receive` through the topic policy.

checks.remediation: An SNS topic fails when its Policy exposes a wildcard principal through an Allow statement that the source does not consider restricted.

caveats: The source loop can return passing early when it encounters a restrictive SourceArn statement, even if a later statement is public. Do not add a benign statement to mask a public grant; review the whole policy.

cli.label: Inspect the current complete topic Policy
Apply an owner-reviewed replacement topic Policy file

iac.code: In Attributes.Policy, remove actual public grants and preserve only reviewed principal and restrictive-condition combinations. Inspect all statements independently because a restrictive SourceArn statement can mask later exposure in this control.
iac.label: Review the SNS topic policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect every wildcard-principal Allow statement and its SourceArn, source-account, organization or endpoint conditions, not merely the first match.
Have the policy owner design a complete replacement with approved publisher and subscriber principals and restrictive conditions matching their real call paths.
Apply the reviewed replacement Policy and test access for authorized and unauthorized callers; reassess all statements manually.
remediation_details.summary: An SNS topic fails when its Policy exposes a wildcard principal through an Allow statement that the source does not consider restricted.

checks.rationale: Flags an SNS topic when the Prowler SNS policy test treats a topic policy grant as public. It can permit an outside principal to invoke or read the service resource without the intended trust boundary.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when the Prowler SNS policy test treats a topic policy grant as public.

checks.title: Confirmed SNS subscription does not use plain HTTP
checks.remediation: A confirmed SNS subscription fails when its Protocol is plain http, exposing notification delivery to transport interception.

caveats: PendingConfirmation subscriptions are not applicable to this condition. Creating an HTTPS subscription alone does not clear the old HTTP finding; removing the old one before delivery verification can lose notifications.

cli.label: Create a reviewed HTTPS replacement subscription

iac.code: Replace Protocol=http with a confirmed HTTPS subscription in the topic owner declaration. Track SubscriptionArn identities, endpoint certificate validation and message delivery; retire the old subscription only after tested cutover.
iac.label: Review the SNS owner declaration

steps: Inspect the subscription attributes, endpoint owner and any pending confirmation state; confirm whether an HTTPS endpoint is available.
Have the endpoint owner provision HTTPS with a trusted certificate, create a parallel subscription and confirm it without embedding secrets in the URL.
Verify delivery and deduplication on HTTPS, then have the subscription owner remove the old HTTP subscription through a separately reviewed cutover.
remediation_details.summary: A confirmed SNS subscription fails when its Protocol is plain http, exposing notification delivery to transport interception.

checks.rationale: Flags a sns subscription when a confirmed SNS subscription uses plaintext `http` protocol. HTTP delivery can expose notification payloads in transit.
checks.description: Flags a sns subscription when a confirmed SNS subscription uses plaintext `http` protocol. HTTP delivery can expose notification payloads in transit.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the confirmed subscription uses another protocol.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when a confirmed SNS subscription uses plaintext `http` protocol.
checks.not_applicable_when: When the SNS subscription is still PendingConfirmation.

checks.title: SQS queue has a dead-letter queue (redrive policy)
checks.remediation: An SQS queue fails when its RedrivePolicy attribute is absent or empty, so failed deliveries lack a configured dead-letter destination.

caveats: The check only detects a nonempty RedrivePolicy string; it does not validate the target queue, maxReceiveCount, replay process or actual delivery. Lower retry counts can move messages before transient failures recover.

cli.label: Inspect queue attributes and owner configuration
Apply only a reviewed RedrivePolicy attribute document

iac.code: Set Attributes.Attributes.RedrivePolicy in the queue owner declaration using an approved dead-letter queue ARN and maxReceiveCount. Review queue type, redrive permissions and replay ownership before publishing; verify a controlled failed delivery.
iac.label: Review the queue owner declaration

steps: Inspect the source queue attributes, retry pattern and poison-message handling requirements.
Have the queue owner select an authorized dead-letter queue of the same standard or FIFO type, approve maxReceiveCount and review its redrive allow policy.
Apply only the reviewed RedrivePolicy attribute, then test a failing message and verify it reaches the dead-letter queue without disrupting normal consumers.
remediation_details.summary: An SQS queue fails when its RedrivePolicy attribute is absent or empty, so failed deliveries lack a configured dead-letter destination.

checks.rationale: Flags an SQS queue when the queue has no RedrivePolicy. Queue messages may be lost, disclosed, or accepted from an unintended principal.
checks.description: Flags an SQS queue when the queue has no RedrivePolicy. Queue messages may be lost, disclosed, or accepted from an unintended principal.
checks.pass_when: PASS when a dead-letter redrive policy is present.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the queue has no RedrivePolicy.

checks.title: SQS queue is encrypted with a KMS key other than alias/aws/sqs
checks.remediation: An SQS queue fails when KmsMasterKeyId is missing or equals the literal alias/aws/sqs, so the configured key is not a selected customer key.

caveats: The condition compares a literal alias and does not independently prove key ownership for every other identifier. Existing messages may remain encrypted under their previous key, and lost KMS grants can interrupt producers or consumers.

cli.label: Inspect queue attributes and owner configuration
Apply only a reviewed KmsMasterKeyId attribute document

iac.code: Set Attributes.Attributes.KmsMasterKeyId in the queue owner declaration to the reviewed customer managed KMS key, preserving its old-key decrypt grants through message retention. Test producer and consumer paths after the update.
iac.label: Review the queue owner declaration

steps: Inspect KmsMasterKeyId and resolve any alias to the actual key ARN, then review its policy and queue producer and consumer grants.
Have the KMS and queue owners select an approved customer managed key and plan the key switch, rollback and expected KMS request cost.
Apply only the reviewed KmsMasterKeyId attribute and verify new message production, consumption and decrypt access.
remediation_details.summary: An SQS queue fails when KmsMasterKeyId is missing or equals the literal alias/aws/sqs, so the configured key is not a selected customer key.

checks.rationale: Flags an SQS queue when the queue has no KmsMasterKeyId or uses the AWS-managed `alias/aws/sqs` key. Queue messages may be lost, disclosed, or accepted from an unintended principal.
checks.description: Flags an SQS queue when the queue has no KmsMasterKeyId or uses the AWS-managed `alias/aws/sqs` key. Queue messages may be lost, disclosed, or accepted from an unintended principal.
checks.pass_when: PASS when a different KMS master key ID is set.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the queue has no KmsMasterKeyId or uses the AWS-managed `alias/aws/sqs` key.

iac.label: Review the queue policy owner declaration

steps: Inspect every queue Policy statement with Effect=Allow and a wildcard principal, including its actions, resources and conditions.
Have the policy owner replace each wildcard principal with reviewed specific principals or redesign the grant while preserving intended producer and consumer access.
Apply a separately reviewed Policy attribute document, verify access with authorized callers and rerun this exact condition.
remediation_details.summary: An SQS queue fails when its Policy has any Allow statement with a wildcard principal, even if that statement has a restricting Condition.

checks.remediation: SageMaker domain AuthMode is not SSO or it has no linked IAM Identity Center managed application identifier or ARN.

caveats: UpdateDomain does not accept AuthMode, so an IAM-authenticated domain cannot be switched in place. Create the reviewed replacement domain with AuthMode=SSO, migrate and test users and data, then verify a linked application field and successful sign-in.
remediation_details.summary: SageMaker domain AuthMode is not SSO or it has no linked IAM Identity Center managed application identifier or ARN.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when AuthMode is not SSO or both SSO application identifiers are absent.

checks.title: Active Inspector2 findings are younger than 192 days
checks.remediation: An enabled Inspector2 Region fails when any active finding firstObservedAt is more than 192 days before capture time, indicating overdue triage.

caveats: The age is based on first observation, not last update or severity. A finding can remain active despite a deployment until Inspector rescans; there is no universal safe fix API for heterogeneous vulnerabilities.

cli.label: Inspect active Inspector2 findings in the exact Region

iac.code: Measure inspector2_finding.firstObservedAt against capture_time with a 192-day threshold in the vulnerability response plan. Assign resource-specific remediation and verify finding closure rather than editing timestamps or suppressing the entire Region.
iac.label: Review the vulnerability response owner procedure

steps: List ACTIVE findings and compare each firstObservedAt with the snapshot capture time to identify those older than 192 days.
Have the affected resource owners prioritize root-cause fixes, patch windows and compensating controls for each stale finding.
Verify remediation closes the active finding, then recollect and confirm no finding remains beyond the 192-day threshold.
remediation_details.summary: An enabled Inspector2 Region fails when any active finding firstObservedAt is more than 192 days before capture time, indicating overdue triage.

checks.rationale: Compares each active Inspector2 finding’s firstObservedAt with the snapshot clock. A finding older than 192 days makes the enabled region FAIL.
checks.description: Compares each active Inspector2 finding’s firstObservedAt with the snapshot clock. A finding older than 192 days makes the enabled region FAIL.
checks.pass_when: No active finding exceeds 192 days of age.
checks.fail_when: An active Inspector2 finding's firstObservedAt is more than 192 days before snapshot time.
checks.not_applicable_when: Inspector2 account status is not ENABLED in the region.

checks.title: Active Inspector2 findings contain no CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities

iac.label: Review the vulnerability response owner procedure

caveats: Reasons EC2_INSTANCE_STOPPED, EXCLUDED_BY_TAG, NO_RESOURCES_FOUND, PENDING_DISABLE, RESOURCE_TERMINATED and SCAN_ELIGIBILITY_EXPIRED are not applicable here. No universal safe Inspector2 mutation fixes every reason; a status of ACTIVE alone does not establish recent scans.

steps: Inspect the exact covered resource scanStatus.statusCode and reason, then identify its EC2, ECR or Lambda owner.
Resolve the reported prerequisite for that resource type, such as SSM management, scanner access, supported OS or image availability, without guessing from the code alone.
Recollect coverage after the owner fixes the prerequisite and verify an ACTIVE status and completed scan.

checks.rationale: For each inspector2 coverage, the evaluator flags FAIL when scanStatus.statusCode is not ACTIVE and scanStatus.reason is not one of the explicit skip reasons. Operators can miss failures or malicious activity because the evidence from the inspector2 coverage is absent or delayed.

checks.pass_when: ScanStatus.statusCode is ACTIVE.
checks.fail_when: ScanStatus.statusCode is not ACTIVE and scanStatus.reason is not one of the explicit skip reasons.
checks.not_applicable_when: scanStatus.reason is in the evaluator’s explicit skip reason list.

checks.remediation: An ACTIVE Inspector2 covered resource fails when lastScannedAt is missing or more than three days before capture time, except a pending scan without a timestamp.

caveats: Non-ACTIVE coverage is not applicable to this check and needs separate active-status review. A missing timestamp with PENDING_INITIAL_SCAN, PENDING_REVIVAL_SCAN or SCAN_IN_PROGRESS is not applicable. Inspector2 has no universal safe force-scan operation for every covered resource type.

iac.code: Monitor lastScannedAt against capture_time for resources with scanStatus.statusCode=ACTIVE, and preserve scanStatus.reason to distinguish pending scans. Escalate stale type-specific coverage to its owner and verify a new completed scan.

steps: Inspect scanStatus, lastScannedAt, resource type and recent changes for the exact covered resource.
Have the service owner investigate stalled prerequisites, scanner permissions and scan scheduling for that resource type; confirm whether a pending initial or revival scan applies.
After the underlying cause is fixed, verify a completed scan updates lastScannedAt within three days and produces current coverage evidence.
remediation_details.summary: An ACTIVE Inspector2 covered resource fails when lastScannedAt is missing or more than three days before capture time, except a pending scan without a timestamp.

checks.rationale: For each inspector2 coverage, the evaluator flags FAIL when an ACTIVE covered resource has no lastScannedAt without a pending reason, or its last scan is more than three days before snapshot time. checks.description: For each inspector2 coverage, the evaluator flags FAIL when an ACTIVE covered resource has no lastScannedAt without a pending reason, or its last scan is more than three days before snapshot time. checks.pass_when: An ACTIVE resource has a lastScannedAt within three days of snapshot time.
checks.fail_when: An ACTIVE covered resource has no lastScannedAt without a pending reason, or its last scan is more than three days before snapshot time.

checks.title: RAM resource share principals of type accounts are reviewed against a trusted list
checks.remediation: A RAM share with associated resources contains individual account IDs in PrincipalAssociations.resourceShareAssociations; each matching principal requires a trusted-list owner decision before access can be accepted.

caveats: The native check reports MANUAL whenever this principal type is present because the required trusted list is operator-supplied, and it returns NOT_APPLICABLE when no non-FAILED resource association exists. A present principal is not automatically malicious.

Have the resource and organization owners compare all-digit associatedEntity principals with a documented, current trusted list and identify all receiving consumers.
For any untrusted principal, stage a replacement access path and approve a separate association removal only after consumer and data-access impact review.

checks.title: Resource Explorer has at least one index in the account
checks.remediation: The account scope fails when the complete Resource Explorer index inventory is empty; resources cannot be found through an account index.

caveats: The condition checks existence only; it does not prove indexing coverage, a designated aggregator, search permissions or search freshness. Indexing can expose resource metadata to authorized search users.

iac.code: Declare a Resource Explorer index in the approved account and Region, and review the resourceexplorer2_index inventory, search permissions and intended aggregation strategy. Verify indexing progress before asserting usable search.
iac.label: Review the owner declaration

steps: Inspect account indexes from the intended Region and confirm that the index inventory is complete and current.
Ask the Resource Explorer owner to choose an approved Region, resource indexing scope and access policy before creating an index.
Create a local index in the approved Region, wait for indexing, then verify ListIndexes and search access for authorized users.
remediation_details.summary: The account scope fails when the complete Resource Explorer index inventory is empty; resources cannot be found through an account index.

checks.rationale: Checks the account Resource Explorer 2 index list returned in each regional scope. An empty collected list fails.
checks.description: Checks the account Resource Explorer 2 index list returned in each regional scope. An empty collected list fails.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the collected account index list contains at least one index.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the collected account index list is empty.

checks.title: Roles Anywhere trust anchor is an active ML-DSA AWS Private CA
checks.remediation: A Roles Anywhere trust anchor is not backed by an ACTIVE AWS Private CA with an ML_DSA_44, ML_DSA_65 or ML_DSA_87 KeyAlgorithm under this certificate-trust control.

caveats: A CERTIFICATE_BUNDLE source fails this exact predicate. A CA absent from complete same-account inventory is MANUAL because it may be cross-account; do not replace it based only on missing local evidence.

A CA KeyAlgorithm is chosen at creation, not converted in place. Switching a live trust anchor can invalidate existing client certificates or credential sessions; no automatic CA creation or old-anchor deletion is offered.

cli.label: Inspect the linked or proposed Private CA
Apply only a reviewed source after certificate migration

iac.code: For trustAnchorArn, select source.sourceType=AWS_ACM_PCA and source.sourceData.acmPcaArn only after the referenced acmpca_certificate_authority has Status=ACTIVE and CertificateAuthorityConfiguration.KeyAlgorithm in ML_DSA_44/65/87; stage certificate issuance, overlap and client validation.
iac.label: Review PKI and trust-anchor owner declarations

steps: Inspect the exact trustAnchorArn and sourceType; when AWS_ACM_PCA, resolve sourceData.acmPcaArn and inspect the CA Status and KeyAlgorithm.
Have the PKI and workload owners create or select a compatible active ML-DSA Private CA, issue and test replacement certificates, and plan trust and client overlap.
After certificate and identity migration are ready, update the owner-reviewed trust anchor source or replace the anchor, then verify new credential sessions and old-client retirement.
remediation_details.summary: A Roles Anywhere trust anchor is not backed by an ACTIVE AWS Private CA with an ML_DSA_44, ML_DSA_65 or ML_DSA_87 KeyAlgorithm under this certificate-trust control.

checks.rationale: Flags a rolesanywhere trust anchor when an AWS ACM PCA trust anchor resolves to a CA that is inactive or whose key algorithm is not ML_DSA_44, ML_DSA_65, or ML_DSA_87. It leaves transport or authentication material exposed to weaker cryptographic protection.
checks.description: Flags a rolesanywhere trust anchor when an AWS ACM PCA trust anchor resolves to a CA that is inactive or whose key algorithm is not ML_DSA_44, ML_DSA_65, or ML_DSA_87. It leaves transport or authentication material exposed to weaker cryptographic protection.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the referenced CA is active and uses an accepted ML-DSA key algorithm.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when an AWS ACM PCA trust anchor resolves to a CA that is inactive or whose key algorithm is not ML_DSA_44, ML_DSA_65, or ML_DSA_87.

checks.title: Route 53 domain has auto renew enabled
checks.remediation: A registered Route 53 domain fails when Detail.AutoRenew is not true, increasing the chance of registration lapse at expiry.

caveats: Automatic renewal depends on billing, registrar eligibility and current contact details; a true flag does not guarantee successful renewal. The operation can lead to future renewal charges.

iac.code: Set Detail.AutoRenew=true in the registrar owner record through the supported Route 53 Domains API, and reconcile the actual domain detail. Keep expiry and billing alerts independent of the toggle.
iac.label: Review the domain registration owner record

steps: Inspect AutoRenew, ExpirationDate, registrar contact status and billing ownership for the exact domain.
Have the domain owner confirm renewal intent, payment method and TLD rules, then enable automatic renewal.
Verify AutoRenew=true and retain separate expiry alerts and contact monitoring.
remediation_details.summary: A registered Route 53 domain fails when Detail.AutoRenew is not true, increasing the chance of registration lapse at expiry.

checks.rationale: Flags a Route 53 domain when `Detail.AutoRenew` differs from true. An unlocked or expiring domain can be transferred or lapse, interrupting DNS and enabling takeover.
checks.description: Flags a Route 53 domain when `Detail.AutoRenew` differs from true. An unlocked or expiring domain can be transferred or lapse, interrupting DNS and enabling takeover.
checks.pass_when: PASS when `Detail.AutoRenew` equals true.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when `Detail.AutoRenew` differs from true.

checks.title: Route 53 domain admin contact privacy protection is enabled
checks.remediation: A registered Route 53 domain fails when Detail.AdminPrivacy is not true, leaving the administrative contact without the requested WHOIS privacy setting.

caveats: The check evaluates AdminPrivacy only and does not prove privacy for other contact types. Some TLDs require matching privacy values or do not support the operation; do not disable privacy to make values match.

iac.code: Set Detail.AdminPrivacy=true in the registrar owner record and review RegistrantPrivacy, TechPrivacy and BillingPrivacy for TLD requirements. Track the registrar operation and verify the final detail.
iac.label: Review the domain registration owner record

steps: Inspect AdminPrivacy and the privacy state of registrant, technical and billing contacts for the domain.
Have the registrar owner confirm TLD support and approve privacy for all required contact types.
Enable admin contact privacy, track the returned operation to completion and verify the contact privacy fields.
remediation_details.summary: A registered Route 53 domain fails when Detail.AdminPrivacy is not true, leaving the administrative contact without the requested WHOIS privacy setting.

checks.rationale: Flags a Route 53 domain when `Detail.AdminPrivacy` differs from true. Administrative contact details may be exposed in domain registration records.
checks.description: Flags a Route 53 domain when `Detail.AdminPrivacy` differs from true. Administrative contact details may be exposed in domain registration records.
checks.pass_when: PASS when `Detail.AdminPrivacy` equals true.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when `Detail.AdminPrivacy` differs from true.

checks.title: Route 53 domain has the clientTransferProhibited lock
checks.remediation: A registered Route 53 domain fails when Detail.StatusList lacks clientTransferProhibited, leaving registrar transfer lock absent.

caveats: The lock can delay an intentional transfer; coordinate any planned transfer window and registrar/TLD restrictions. A status entry is not proof of all account access protections.

iac.code: Require clientTransferProhibited in Detail.StatusList for domains under Route 53 registrar ownership and document any time-bounded approved transfer exception. Verify the registrar status after the API operation.
iac.label: Review the domain registration owner record

steps: Inspect StatusList, domain ownership, any pending transfer and the registrar operation state.
Have the domain owner confirm that a transfer is not planned and enable the transfer lock.
Track the registrar operation and verify clientTransferProhibited appears in StatusList.

checks.description: Flags a Route 53 domain when `Detail.StatusList` lacks `clientTransferProhibited`. An unlocked or expiring domain can be transferred or lapse, interrupting DNS and enabling takeover.

checks.remediation: A WAFv2 web ACL fails when LoggingConfiguration.LogDestinationConfigs is absent or empty, leaving request matches without the expected WAF log destination.

caveats: A successful API response does not prove log delivery. Logging can expose request data and incur storage costs; redaction and least-privilege destination access need owner review. CloudFront scope uses us-east-1.

iac.code: Define LoggingConfiguration.LogDestinationConfigs for the web ACL in the logging owner declaration, including reviewed redaction, retention and destination policy. Verify real log delivery after the configuration is applied.
iac.label: Review the WAF owner declaration

steps: Inspect the logging configuration for the exact web ACL ARN and confirm whether a destination is already configured.
Have the logging owner review destination permissions, retention, sensitive-field redaction and delivery costs before selecting a CloudWatch Logs, S3 or Firehose destination.
Apply a reviewed logging configuration for this ARN and verify delivered WAF log events and retention.
remediation_details.summary: A WAFv2 web ACL fails when LoggingConfiguration.LogDestinationConfigs is absent or empty, leaving request matches without the expected WAF log destination.

checks.rationale: Flags a WAFv2 web ACL when the Web ACL logging configuration has no log destination in a WAFv2 resource. It can leave activity or security events invisible during investigation and delay detection of misuse.

checks.pass_when: PASS when a logging destination is configured in a WAFv2 resource.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when the Web ACL logging configuration has no log destination in a WAFv2 resource.

checks.title: Every WAFv2 web ACL rule and rule group has CloudWatch metrics enabled
checks.remediation: A nonempty WAFv2 web ACL fails when any ACL rule or Firewall Manager process group has VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled other than true, reducing per-rule visibility.

caveats: An ACL with no rules is not applicable to this condition. Firewall Manager may own process groups; coordinate there instead of overwriting managed settings. Metrics can incur monitoring cost, and CloudFront scope uses us-east-1.

cli.label: Apply a separately reviewed complete web ACL update document

iac.code: For each WebACL.Rules rule and WebACL.PreProcessFirewallManagerRuleGroups or WebACL.PostProcessFirewallManagerRuleGroups group, set VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true in the correct owner declaration. Preserve all other ACL settings, refresh the lock token and verify metrics after representative traffic.
iac.label: Review the WAF owner declaration

steps: Inspect every WebACL.Rules entry and each pre- and post-process Firewall Manager group visibility configuration.
Have the ACL or Firewall Manager owner enable CloudWatch metrics on each disabled owned rule or group while preserving sample-request and metric-name choices.
Use a complete reviewed ACL update with a fresh lock token, then verify the per-rule metrics appear after traffic reaches the ACL.
remediation_details.summary: A nonempty WAFv2 web ACL fails when any ACL rule or Firewall Manager process group has VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled other than true, reducing per-rule visibility.

checks.rationale: Flags a WAFv2 web ACL when any Web ACL rule or Firewall Manager group lacks `VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true`. It can leave activity or security events invisible during investigation and delay detection of misuse.
checks.description: Flags a WAFv2 web ACL when any Web ACL rule or Firewall Manager group lacks `VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true`. It can leave activity or security events invisible during investigation and delay detection of misuse.
checks.pass_when: PASS when all evaluated rules and groups enable CloudWatch metrics.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when any Web ACL rule or Firewall Manager group lacks `VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true`.
checks.not_applicable_when: When the Web ACL has no rules or Firewall Manager groups to inspect.

checks.title: WAFv2 rule group has CloudWatch metrics enabled
frameworks: AWS Australian Cyber Security Center (ACSC) Essential Eight

controls.framework: AWS Australian Cyber Security Center (ACSC) Essential Eight

checks.remediation: A WAFv2 rule group fails when RuleGroup.VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled is not true, reducing visibility into the group.

caveats: The rule group update API requires a full configuration and fresh lock token; omission of rules or visibility fields can disrupt shared consumers. Metrics can incur monitoring cost; CloudFront scope uses us-east-1.

cli.label: Apply a separately reviewed complete rule group update document

iac.code: Set RuleGroup.VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled=true in the owner-managed rule group while preserving Rules, visibility metric name and sampled-request behavior. Publish the full update with a fresh lock token and verify consumers.
iac.label: Review the WAF owner declaration

steps: Inspect the rule group ARN and its VisibilityConfig, and identify the owner of any shared consumers.
Have the rule-group owner enable CloudWatchMetricsEnabled while preserving its rules, metric name and sampled-request setting in a complete reviewed update.
Apply with the current lock token and verify that metrics appear after matching traffic reaches consuming web ACLs.
remediation_details.summary: A WAFv2 rule group fails when RuleGroup.VisibilityConfig.CloudWatchMetricsEnabled is not true, reducing visibility into the group.

checks.title: Well-Architected workload has no high or medium risks
checks.remediation: A Well-Architected workload fails when RiskCounts.HIGH or RiskCounts.MEDIUM is a positive integer, indicating unresolved review risks.

caveats: A review answer update alone is not remediation and must not be used to hide unresolved risk. RiskCounts can lag lens review updates; accepted risk may still remain visible. No generic safe fix command exists because each improvement is workload-specific.

cli.label: Inspect improvements for an owner-selected lens

iac.code: Track RiskCounts.HIGH and RiskCounts.MEDIUM as review output, not configuration toggles. Manage each question improvement in the workload owner plan and only update answers after the underlying control is verified.
iac.label: Review the owner declaration

steps: Inspect the workload RiskCounts and open each lens review to identify the high and medium risk questions and recommended improvements.
Assign each risk to the workload owner, implement and verify the underlying architecture or operational change, and document accepted residual risks.
Update the review answers only after evidence supports the changed state, then verify both HIGH and MEDIUM counts are zero.
remediation_details.summary: A Well-Architected workload fails when RiskCounts.HIGH or RiskCounts.MEDIUM is a positive integer, indicating unresolved review risks.

checks.rationale: Flags a wellarchitected workload when RiskCounts contains a positive HIGH or MEDIUM count. High or medium unresolved workload risks can leave known resilience or security weaknesses untreated.
checks.description: Flags a wellarchitected workload when RiskCounts contains a positive HIGH or MEDIUM count. High or medium unresolved workload risks can leave known resilience or security weaknesses untreated.
checks.pass_when: PASS when both HIGH and MEDIUM risk counts are zero or absent.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when RiskCounts contains a positive HIGH or MEDIUM count.

checks.title: Firewall rule does not allow internet ingress to TCP/UDP 53
checks.remediation: Restrict public TCP/UDP port 53 ingress in this firewall rule to approved sources and necessary targets.

caveats: The check examines a declared allow rule, not effective reachability, priority, target attachment or hierarchical firewall policy. Source selectors and other ports may still allow exposure.

iac.code: Change source_ranges and, if needed, target_tags/target_service_accounts and allow entries on the existing google_compute_firewall resource.
iac.label: Change the existing managed rule

steps: Inspect direction, sourceRanges, allowed protocol and port entries, and target tags/service accounts for the TCP/UDP port 53 rule.
Replace world-open source ranges with tested approved CIDRs or narrow the target and allowed ports in the owning rule.
Test intended connections, reread the firewall rule and rerun this check; review higher-priority policies separately.
remediation_details.summary: Restrict public TCP/UDP port 53 ingress in this firewall rule to approved sources and necessary targets.

controls.framework: Prowler ThreatScore Compliance Framework for AWS

checks.remediation: Verify the EKS cluster security group fact and cluster platform before considering a network migration.

caveats: The native predicate tests only resourcesVpcConfig.clusterSecurityGroupId presence; it does not inspect effective node/control-plane security group rules or Kubernetes NetworkPolicy.

AWS automatically creates a cluster security group for EKS Kubernetes 1.14-eks.3 or newer. Proven older platforms used separate control-plane and node security groups and are NOT_APPLICABLE; ambiguous version/platform evidence remains UNKNOWN.
An absent or malformed modern ID is UNKNOWN, not proof of insecure traffic. Cluster replacement is disruptive and cannot be justified from this field alone.

cli.label: Inspect cluster version and AWS-managed security group fact

steps: Inspect Cluster.cluster.resourcesVpcConfig.clusterSecurityGroupId and the cluster version/platform in the exact DescribeCluster response. A valid observed sg- ID passes only this presence fact; security group rules and Kubernetes NetworkPolicy require separate review.

If a modern cluster has an absent or malformed ID, investigate collector permissions, source-response completeness and the EKS cluster VPC configuration with the owner; the evaluator returns UNKNOWN rather than asserting an insecure network or recommending replacement.

For a proven historical pre-1.14 cluster or 1.14 before platform eks.3, review its separate control-plane and node security groups under the owner's migration plan; that cluster model is NOT_APPLICABLE to this EKS-created SG ID fact.

Recollect DescribeCluster after the evidence issue is resolved and verify the exact ID and version/platform. Resolve network policy and effective security group rule questions through their own evidence and controls.
remediation_details.summary: Verify the EKS cluster security group fact and cluster platform before considering a network migration.

checks.rationale: Reads the EKS DescribeCluster resourcesVpcConfig.clusterSecurityGroupId as evidence of an EKS-created cluster security group ID. It does not inspect security group rules or Kubernetes pod NetworkPolicy. Remediation: Inspect the cluster version, platform, actual security group associations and rules; assess pod NetworkPolicy separately. Do not infer replacement or pod isolation from a missing ID.
checks.description: Reads the EKS DescribeCluster resourcesVpcConfig.clusterSecurityGroupId as evidence of an EKS-created cluster security group ID. checks.pass_when: A plausible sg- ID is observed.
checks.fail_when: No definitive FAIL: a missing, empty or malformed modern ID is UNKNOWN.
checks.not_applicable_when: A provably pre-1.14 or 1.14 pre-eks.3 cluster uses the historical security group model; ambiguous history is UNKNOWN.

For a network load balancer, this predicate requires TLS for every listener. Existing TCP pass-through can already carry end-to-end encrypted bytes; decide with the service owner whether TLS termination is appropriate, and redesign UDP/TCP_UDP traffic separately rather than forcing an incompatible protocol.

Where a supported listener conversion is approved, use a complete reviewed ModifyListener request with certificate and security policy for HTTP-to-HTTPS or TCP-to-TLS; validate clients and targets before retiring any old listener and recollect all listener protocols.

checks.title: Direct Connect has at least two connections in different locations
checks.remediation: Provision a second Direct Connect connection in a different location through the network owner's resiliency plan, then verify inventory and failover.

caveats: This is an account/Region scope predicate over all collected connections. It counts entries and distinct location strings, not connectionState, BGP health, capacity or actual traffic failover.
A second physical connection requires facility/provider coordination, lead time and recurring cost; choose the resiliency model and capacity with the network owner.
A passing count is not proof of operational failover. Validate BGP routing and schedule an owner-approved Direct Connect failover test after provisioning.

references.title: AWS Direct Connect Connection API fields

steps: List all collected Direct Connect connections in the affected account and Region; verify there are at least two connection IDs and compare each location value. No connections is NOT_APPLICABLE; fewer than two connections or fewer than two distinct locations fails.

Have the network owner choose the AWS Resiliency Toolkit model, approve capacity/provider/facility work, and provision an additional connection in a different Direct Connect location if the inventory lacks that second location.

Configure and validate the associated virtual interfaces and BGP routing, then schedule a controlled failover test with the network owner; retain existing connectivity as rollback while the new path is proved.
Recollect connection IDs and location values and rerun this scope check; separately verify operational failover because this predicate does not inspect connection health.
remediation_details.summary: Provision a second Direct Connect connection in a different location through the network owner's resiliency plan, then verify inventory and failover.

checks.fail_when: The region has exactly one connection, or all connections share one location.

checks.title: Each virtual/Direct Connect gateway has at least two virtual interfaces on distinct connections
checks.remediation: Give each associated gateway two virtual interfaces on separate Direct Connect connections, then verify identifiers and controlled failover.

caveats: This scope check groups only virtual interfaces with a nonempty virtualGatewayId or directConnectGatewayId. Two VIF IDs on one connection still fail; unassociated VIFs do not count.
A second VIF requires an available separate Direct Connect connection, approved VLAN/BGP addressing and owner-coordinated routing. Creating a VIF can incur charges or alter network paths.
The evaluator counts identifiers, not VIF state, BGP health or actual traffic failover; test a controlled path switch before treating redundancy as operational.

Validate BGP route preference and run an owner-approved controlled failover test while retaining the existing VIF as rollback.
Recollect the gateway-to-VIF-to-connection mapping and rerun the scope check; confirm at least two distinct VIF IDs on at least two distinct connection IDs for every associated gateway.

checks.remediation: Verify the exact backup vault reports a valid configured KMS key ARN; resolve missing or conflicting metadata before drawing an encryption conclusion.

caveats: AWS Backup chooses a default KMS key when no key is explicitly supplied at vault creation. An omitted EncryptionKeyArn is incomplete metadata, not an unencrypted-vault finding.
The native check now has no supported unencrypted-vault FAIL branch: valid matching observed key metadata PASS, while missing, denied, malformed or conflicting facts are UNKNOWN.
A vault key report does not prove every recovery point is encrypted; independently encrypted resource types may inherit source encryption and each recovery point needs its own IsEncrypted assessment.

cli.label: Inspect regional vault list key metadata
Inspect this exact vault key metadata

references.title: AWS Backup encryption by resource type

steps: Inspect this vault BackupVaultArn and EncryptionKeyArn from ListBackupVaults and a matching DescribeBackupVault response in the same Region; the native check accepts a valid observed key ARN and requires matching list/describe values when both are present.

If DescribeBackupVault is missing, denied, malformed, identifies another vault, omits the key, or disagrees with the list response, repair the collection or identity mismatch and rerun; the result is UNKNOWN, not evidence of an unencrypted vault.

If a valid key ARN is observed, verify that its policy and availability meet the owner backup and restore requirements. Assess each recovery point IsEncrypted and resource type separately; this vault-key metadata check alone does not establish their encryption state.
remediation_details.summary: Verify the exact backup vault reports a valid configured KMS key ARN; resolve missing or conflicting metadata before drawing an encryption conclusion.

checks.rationale: Checks matching valid Backup vault EncryptionKeyArn metadata from ListBackupVaults or DescribeBackupVault. A configured vault key does not prove encryption of every recovery point. checks.remediation: For a recovery point with IsEncrypted=false, determine its resource type and create or copy a verified encrypted replacement using that type’s supported encryption path.

caveats: The evaluator tests only IsEncrypted on this recovery point; it does not establish whether a vault-key change or copy will encrypt this resource type. Unencrypted Aurora, DocumentDB and Neptune snapshot copies can remain unencrypted.

AWS Backup independently encrypts only fully managed resource types; other types typically inherit source-resource encryption. Destination vault KMS permissions, copy support and restore permissions differ by type and account/Region.

An existing recovery point cannot be made encrypted in place. A replacement backup/copy can add cost and may alter recovery objectives; never delete the original before owner-approved restore and retention review.

iac.code: Update the owning source-resource encryption and backup-plan destination according to the AWS Backup encryption matrix for this exact resource type; if a supported encrypted copy is used, verify the destination recovery point IsEncrypted and a test restore before any retention change.
iac.label: Plan a resource-type-specific encrypted replacement

references.title: AWS Backup encryption by resource type and copy behavior

steps: Describe the exact recovery point and confirm IsEncrypted=false, its resource type, source ResourceArn, vault and retained restore requirements; compare with a fresh backup job or source-service snapshot result.

Use the AWS Backup encryption matrix for that resource type. For fully managed types, choose a vault with an approved accessible KMS key and create a new backup or supported copy. For source-encrypted types, first plan encryption of the source or supported service-specific encrypted snapshot/copy route.

Verify the new recovery point reports IsEncrypted=true and successfully restores under its KMS grants before changing the owner backup plan or retiring the old recovery point. Keep its existing retention and Vault Lock obligations.
remediation_details.summary: For a recovery point with IsEncrypted=false, determine its resource type and create or copy a verified encrypted replacement using that type’s supported encryption path.

checks.rationale: For each AWS Backup recovery point, FAILs when IsEncrypted is false. Unencrypted recovery points, for example copied from unencrypted sources, expose full copies of production data to anyone who can restore or copy them.

checks.fail_when: FAIL when isEncrypted is false.

checks.remediation: Backup vault policy denies manual recovery point deletion. Add a vault access policy Deny statement on backup:DeleteRecoveryPoint, backup:UpdateRecoveryPointLifecycle and backup:PutBackupVaultAccessPolicy for Resource "*" (or use AWS Backup Vault Lock).

caveats: Steampipe: a Deny statement whose Action array contains the three actions and Resource = "*". Relaxed to avoid false positives: wildcard actions (backup:*, *, backup:Delete*...) that cover each action, a string Action and Resource ["*"] also count. A vault without an access policy fails.
Vault policies can block backup/restore operations; validate caller permissions and existing recovery-point lifecycle before replacing policy.
The JSON/policy file must be based on current owner-approved configuration; retain unrelated fields and exact resource relationships.

checks.remediation: Replace the DAX cluster with one created using SSEEnabled=true, then migrate its clients after compatibility and cache-warmup tests.

caveats: DAX cannot enable this encryption mode on an existing cluster. The evaluator reads SSEDescription.Status; a new cluster does not make the old resource pass while it remains in inventory.
Cluster replacement changes the endpoint and cache contents, so client compatibility, startup load, capacity, VPC path, IAM grants, rollback and potential downtime need review.
DAX at-rest encryption is unsupported on dax.r3.* node types; choose a compatible replacement.

cli.label: Create only from a complete owner-reviewed replacement request

iac.code: Create a replacement AWS::DAX::Cluster with SSEEnabled=true, preserving reviewed IAM role, subnet group, security groups, node type, parameter group and node count. Migrate clients to its new endpoint only after compatibility, cache-warmup and rollback tests; retire the old cluster later.
iac.label: Replace the immutable DAX encryption setting

references.title: DAX encryption mode and immutable setting

steps: Confirm the existing cluster reports SSEDescription.Status in the failing state and record its node type, subnet group, security groups, IAM role, parameter group, node count, endpoint and client versions.
Create a parallel cluster with SSEEnabled=true and all other owner-reviewed settings preserved; use a compatible node type and test application client behavior before changing traffic.
Shift clients to the new cluster endpoint in an approved window, allow cache warmup, monitor DynamoDB origin load and latency, and keep the old cluster through the rollback window.
Recollect the replacement cluster and verify the expected encryption field before retiring the old cluster after owner approval.
remediation_details.summary: Replace the DAX cluster with one created using SSEEnabled=true, then migrate its clients after compatibility and cache-warmup tests.

checks.rationale: Reads SSEDescription.Status of each DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster, treating an omitted SSEDescription as DISABLED, and fails any cluster whose status is not ENABLED. Cached DynamoDB items on DAX node storage are then unencrypted at rest, and because SSE can only be chosen at cluster creation the cluster must be rebuilt to fix it.
checks.description: Reads SSEDescription.Status of each DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster, treating an omitted SSEDescription as DISABLED, and fails any cluster whose status is not ENABLED. Cached DynamoDB items on DAX node storage are then unencrypted at rest, and because SSE can only be chosen at cluster creation the cluster must be rebuilt to fix it.
checks.pass_when: SSEDescription.Status is ENABLED.
checks.fail_when: SSEDescription.Status is DISABLED, any value other than ENABLED, or SSEDescription is omitted.
