checks.title: DAX cluster nodes span more than one Availability Zone
checks.remediation: Scale the DAX cluster with replicas placed in at least two approved Availability Zones, then verify the actual node-zone set.

caveats: The predicate counts distinct zone names in the collected node list, not only configured subnet-group zones. An incomplete node response must be investigated before scaling.

Increasing nodes adds recurring cost and can affect cache placement/performance; availability zones and node count require owner approval. A request alone is not proof that replicas reached a second AZ.

cli.label: Add approved replicas across two or more zones

iac.code: Set the DAX cluster node count and subnet/AZ placement to at least two approved Availability Zones, then verify deployed Nodes[].AvailabilityZone has two distinct values. Review node cost and cache failover behavior.
iac.label: Review DAX replica placement

steps: Inspect Nodes[].AvailabilityZone and total replication factor. The evaluator fails when fewer than two distinct zone names occur, including an empty node list; confirm cluster status and inventory completeness.
Choose approved second-zone subnet capacity and a reviewed total node count greater than the current count; account for DAX node charges and application capacity.
Increase replication factor with explicit approved Availability Zones or update the owning cluster declaration, then wait for nodes to become available and monitor replication/client latency.
Recollect Nodes[].AvailabilityZone and rerun the check only after at least two distinct zones are visible.
remediation_details.summary: Scale the DAX cluster with replicas placed in at least two approved Availability Zones, then verify the actual node-zone set.

checks.rationale: Collects the AvailabilityZone of every node in a DAX cluster and fails the cluster when the distinct set of zones has fewer than two members (including a cluster with no listed nodes). A single-AZ DAX cluster loses its whole cache layer during an AZ outage, pushing all read load back onto DynamoDB or breaking applications that depend on it.
checks.description: Collects the AvailabilityZone of every node in a DAX cluster and fails the cluster when the distinct set of zones has fewer than two members (including a cluster with no listed nodes). A single-AZ DAX cluster loses its whole cache layer during an AZ outage, pushing all read load back onto DynamoDB or breaking applications that depend on it.
checks.pass_when: Cluster nodes are spread over at least two distinct Availability Zones.
checks.fail_when: All nodes are in one Availability Zone or the node list is empty/omitted.

checks.title: DMS certificate is not expired
checks.remediation: Import a valid DMS certificate, move dependent endpoints safely, then retire the exact expired certificate after owner review.

caveats: The evaluator fails when ValidToDate precedes the captured UTC day's 00:00 minus one second; it does not check endpoint use. An unused expired certificate still fails until removed from inventory.
DMS certificate import needs an owner-supplied valid PEM or Oracle wallet. Keep certificate material in protected local files and out of reports, shell history and finding evidence.

Changing an endpoint's CertificateArn can interrupt replication or break TLS trust. Delete the expired certificate only after every dependent endpoint has been migrated and tested; deletion is irreversible and must follow retention/rollback approval.

cli.label: Inspect certificate IDs, expiration and validity (read only)
Find endpoints referencing the expired certificate
Import an owner-approved valid replacement from a protected local file
Move each reviewed dependent endpoint after a replication change plan
Retire the exact expired certificate only after approved cutover and retention review

steps: Compare the exact certificate ARN's ValidToDate with the snapshot day's UTC midnight minus one second. List all DMS endpoints and identify each endpoint whose CertificateArn references it; the check fails even if no endpoint uses the expired certificate.

Have the DMS and database owners approve a valid replacement certificate or wallet and its trust chain. Import it with a new identifier from a protected local file; do not copy certificate contents into finding evidence.

For each dependent endpoint, schedule a replication change window, set its CertificateArn to the new ARN, test TLS connectivity and replication continuity, and retain the prior configuration for rollback until verified.

After confirming no endpoint references the expired ARN and approving retention/rollback, delete that exact expired certificate. Recollect certificate inventory and rerun the resource check; importing a new certificate alone cannot clear the old resource finding.
remediation_details.summary: Import a valid DMS certificate, move dependent endpoints safely, then retire the exact expired certificate after owner review.

checks.rationale: Compares each AWS DMS certificate's ValidToDate with the start of the snapshot day minus one second and fails the certificate when it is already past that cutoff. Expired certificates attached to DMS endpoints cause SSL verification failures or push operators to downgrade endpoint SslMode, weakening replication transport security.

checks.pass_when: ValidToDate is on or after the start of the snapshot day minus one second.
checks.fail_when: ValidToDate is earlier than that cutoff (certificate expired).

checks.title: DocumentDB instance storage is encrypted
checks.remediation: Restore the unencrypted DocumentDB parent cluster as a separate encrypted cluster, create replacement instances and migrate clients safely.

caveats: The exact resource predicate reads an Engine=docdb instance's StorageEncrypted flag; other engines are NOT_APPLICABLE. DocumentDB storage encryption is selected for the cluster at creation and covers its instances, so replacing only this DB instance does not encrypt its existing cluster.

AWS DocumentDB cannot encrypt an unencrypted cluster snapshot by copying it with KmsKeyId. Restore the source cluster snapshot as a new cluster with an approved KMS key, then create instances in that new cluster.

A restored cluster has no instances, and incomplete restore inputs can select default network/security settings. Plan snapshot data consistency, new cluster/instance cost, client endpoint cutover and rollback; the old unencrypted instance retains its resource finding until retired.

steps: Describe the exact DB instance and inspect Engine, StorageEncrypted and DBClusterIdentifier. Non-docdb engines are NOT_APPLICABLE; an unencrypted docdb instance requires parent-cluster replacement.

Have the database owner inspect the parent cluster and prepare a consistent cluster snapshot plus a complete new-cluster restore request naming an approved KMS key, subnet group, security groups and other required settings. Do not attempt to encrypt an unencrypted snapshot copy with KmsKeyId.

Restore that snapshot into a separate encrypted cluster, create replacement DB instances there, and verify instance StorageEncrypted=true, data currency, KMS access and client connectivity before endpoint cutover.
Retain the source instance/cluster for rollback and approved retention, then recollect the new and old instance flags; the old unencrypted instance keeps its finding until retired after migration.

caveats: Only Engine=docdb clusters are evaluated; the exact predicate reads the cluster StorageEncrypted boolean. Encryption cannot be enabled in place on an existing unencrypted cluster.

checks.title: Configured DRS source servers report continuous replication
checks.remediation: Restore continuous DRS replication for the named impaired source server, then verify every configured source in the Region.

caveats: This native scope check now uses a complete DescribeSourceServers inventory and dataReplicationInfo.dataReplicationState. It does not use DescribeJobs history; historical recovery jobs cannot establish current replication.
No configured source servers is NOT_APPLICABLE, not proof that all required workloads are protected. The protection scope must be established by the recovery owner.

StartReplication is documented for STOPPED sources and restarts billing. STALLED/DISCONNECTED require cause-specific repair; intermediate or unread states are UNKNOWN. No drill or recovery launch is suggested by this template.
CONTINUOUS alone does not prove recovery readiness, acceptable lag, launch configuration or workload RTO. Those require separate owner review and authorized drills.

references.title: AWS DRS StartReplication for stopped sources

steps: Confirm the complete DescribeSourceServers inventory in the exact account and Region and inspect each impaired_source_ids entry. This check fails configured sources in STOPPED, STALLED or DISCONNECTED; intermediate or unread states remain UNKNOWN, and zero configured sources are NOT_APPLICABLE without a declared protection scope.

For a verified STOPPED source whose owner intends continuous protection, correct prerequisites and restart replication for that exact sourceServerID. Restarting replication resumes protected-source billing; approve the impact before applying.

For STALLED or DISCONNECTED sources, use the DRS recovery dashboard and replication troubleshooting details to repair the observed agent, network, staging or permission cause; do not assume StartReplication repairs these states.

Re-read all source-server replication states until configured sources report CONTINUOUS, then recollect and rerun this check. Have the workload owner validate recovery drills, launch settings, lag and RTO separately.

checks.title: ElastiCache replication group older than 6.0 uses Redis AUTH
checks.remediation: Enable required Redis AUTH for eligible pre-6.0 ElastiCache replication groups after a staged client rollout.

caveats: The evaluator joins cache clusters by ReplicationGroupId; absent joined members are UNKNOWN and groups whose members are all 6.0+ are NOT_APPLICABLE. It does not test whether an enabled AUTH token is required by all clients.

AWS supports modifying AUTH on an existing group only for Redis OSS 5.0.6+ (or Valkey 7.2+) with in-transit encryption enabled. ROTATE initially permits prior/no-token access; SET is required after client migration.

The reviewed JSON carries a secret and must be generated and handled by the owner outside source control, logs and screenshots. Do not interpolate tokens into findings or code-copy examples. An immediate or replacement change may interrupt clients and incur cost.

Eligible TLS-enabled 5.0.6+ only: stage ROTATE using a reviewed secret-bearing request

iac.code: For an eligible TLS-enabled Redis OSS 5.0.6+ group, change the owner-managed replication-group configuration to stage a new AUTH token with ROTATE, migrate all clients, then require that token with SET. Keep the token out of plans, logs and findings. If eligibility or TLS is absent, use a reviewed compatible upgrade or replacement with client and data cutover.
iac.label: Stage AUTH through the approved secret owner

steps: Inspect joined ElastiCache cluster EngineVersion values for this ReplicationGroupId and the group AuthTokenEnabled and TransitEncryptionEnabled fields; the native check fails only if any joined member is below 6.0 and AUTH is false.

If the group is Redis OSS 5.0.6 or later with TLS enabled, have the owner generate a strong token through its approved secret workflow and submit a complete reviewed ModifyReplicationGroup request with ROTATE; at this stage unauthenticated clients may still connect.

Update every client to use TLS and the new token, validate connectivity, then submit a reviewed SET strategy request with the same token so authentication becomes required; schedule each change and confirm the group reaches available state.

If the version or transit-encryption prerequisites for in-place AUTH are absent, plan an owner-managed compatible upgrade or replacement with TLS and AUTH and a tested client/data cutover rather than issuing a failing ModifyReplicationGroup call.
Recollect the replication group and all joined member versions. Members all at 6.0 or later are NOT_APPLICABLE to this particular AUTH check and require separate RBAC review.

checks.title: ElastiCache replication group is encrypted at rest with an enabled KMS key
checks.remediation: Resolve the ElastiCache replication group key state, then re-enable its approved key or migrate to a reviewed encrypted replacement as the facts require.

caveats: The evaluator checks AtRestEncryptionEnabled, KmsKeyId presence and joined KMS Enabled only; it does not check KeyManager or effective StorageEncryptionType. The title CMK is stronger than the implemented predicate, and a missing key ID is not proof that cache data is plaintext.

ElastiCache at-rest encryption is chosen at replication-group creation and cannot be toggled on an existing group. Replacement with snapshot/restore can incur cost, cause endpoint changes and lose writes if the cutover is not coordinated.

Only customer-managed KMS keys can be manually re-enabled; AWS-managed and AWS-owned keys cannot. Re-enabling a key can restore other users as well, so confirm ownership, grants and policy before that command.

Inspect the exact joined key state and manager
Re-enable only an owner-approved disabled customer key
Create complete reviewed encrypted replacement when immutable settings require it

iac.code: For an owner-approved disabled customer KMS key, restore its Enabled state and required ElastiCache grants through the key owner. For an immutable missing at-rest/KmsKeyId setting, declare a separate encrypted replication group with approved key and supported backup/data migration, then validate endpoints before old-group retirement. StorageEncryptionType and KeyManager require separate review because the native predicate does not assess them.
iac.label: Choose the key repair or replacement from exact branch

references.title: ElastiCache at-rest encryption and replacement workflow

steps: Inspect AtRestEncryptionEnabled and KmsKeyId on this replication group and the joined KMS key Enabled state. The native check fails if at-rest flag is false, key ID is absent, or a uniquely joined key is disabled; an unresolved key join is UNKNOWN.

Inspect StorageEncryptionType and the key KeyManager separately before changing anything: AWS can report effective service-managed encryption even when the AtRestEncryptionEnabled flag is false, and the evaluator does not actually verify a customer-managed key.

If the sole failure is an owner-approved disabled customer-managed KMS key, restore key availability and grants with the KMS owner, then validate the cache can use the key. Never enable a disabled key solely from a stale join.

If the owner requires at-rest encryption with a selected KMS key but this group lacks it, take a reviewed backup and create a separate supported replication group with AtRestEncryptionEnabled=true and approved KmsKeyId; validate data, application endpoints, and key permissions before client cutover.
Recollect group, KMS and effective storage-encryption facts after the chosen repair. Keep the old group until data and rollback are verified; a new group does not change its old finding.
remediation_details.summary: Resolve the ElastiCache replication group key state, then re-enable its approved key or migrate to a reviewed encrypted replacement as the facts require.

checks.rationale: For each ElastiCache replication group, fails when AtRestEncryptionEnabled is false, when no KmsKeyId is set (default service-managed key), or when the joined KMS key's KeyMetadata.Enabled is false. checks.remediation: For a Regional EFS file system with only one mount target, add a reviewed target in another Availability Zone; a One Zone file system requires a separate Regional migration.

steps: Inspect AvailabilityZoneId, AvailabilityZoneName and NumberOfMountTargets. A nonempty AvailabilityZoneId is a One Zone file system and fails this check; otherwise a Regional file system with zero or one mount target fails.

caveats: The predicate classifies an effective 0.0.0.0/0 route to igw- as a public subnet; it does not prove that the mount target itself has a public IP or that NFS is reachable from the internet. Review security groups and network controls separately.

Deleting a mount target forcibly breaks mounts using it and can disrupt applications. Keep backups, client coordination and a validated rollback plan; a shared route-table change can affect all resources in its subnet.

references.title: EFS mount-target placement and one-per-AZ limit

steps: List the file system’s public_mount_targets IDs and resolve each mount target SubnetId, VPC and Availability Zone. Inspect its explicit route-table association or the VPC main table for 0.0.0.0/0 to igw-.
Choose a private subnet in the same Availability Zone with no effective IGW default route and review NFS security groups, IP capacity, DNS and every client using the current mount target.

Plan a maintenance window: an EFS file system permits only one mount target per Availability Zone, so replacing a target in another subnet normally requires deleting that AZ’s existing target before creating the reviewed replacement. Test alternate-AZ access and rollback before cutover.
Verify the new mount target is available, clients can remount and the complete joined subnet/route-table inventory has no flagged target; rerun the check.

checks.remediation: Disable automatic public IPv4 assignment on the subnet hosting the flagged EFS mount target, after reviewing other workloads that launch there.

steps: Confirm the mount target SubnetId and the joined subnet.MapPublicIpOnLaunch=true. This flag belongs to the subnet, not to the EFS mount-target interface.

checks.remediation: Replace the EFS access point exposing / with one rooted at an approved application directory, then migrate its mounts.

caveats: RootDirectory and PosixUser are immutable on an EFS access point. A new access point does not reconfigure current mounts or make the old root-exposing access point pass.

checks.title: EMR cluster security configuration enables encryption at rest
checks.remediation: Launch replacement EMR capacity with a reviewed security configuration that enables at-rest encryption.

caveats: At-rest encryption applies to the storage modes explicitly configured; enabling the flag alone does not encrypt historical S3 objects or disks on a running cluster.

Security configurations are chosen when an EMR cluster is created. A new configuration does not change a running cluster; replacement can incur compute, data-transfer and KMS costs and interrupt jobs.
This template is bound to the named cluster and its joined configuration; do not substitute another cluster or change a shared security configuration without checking all consumers.

cli.label: Create an owner-reviewed replacement security configuration

iac.code: In the EMR owner IaC, declare a new security configuration with Set EnableAtRestEncryption=true with reviewed S3 and/or local-disk encryption providers. Preserve unrelated security configuration fields and provider dependencies, then create reviewed replacement cluster capacity referencing the new name. Validate jobs and data before retiring the old cluster; the old cluster is not changed in place.
iac.label: Create a new security configuration and replace affected cluster

references.title: Create EMR security configuration and encryption JSON
Specify security configuration when creating an EMR cluster

steps: Resolve Cluster.Cluster.SecurityConfiguration and the joined DescribeSecurityConfiguration JSON; an absent cluster attachment fails, while a referenced configuration absent from complete inventory remains UNKNOWN.
Review the exact EncryptionConfiguration.EnableAtRestEncryption value with the cluster owner. Set EnableAtRestEncryption=true with reviewed S3 and/or local-disk encryption providers.

Create a new reviewed security configuration rather than trying to edit the stored one; preserve other encryption, authentication, EMRFS roles, certificates and key-provider settings in the complete JSON.

Launch replacement EMR capacity with the new security configuration through the owner deployment plan, migrate jobs and data, validate application access and encryption, then retire old capacity under the owner retention plan. The existing cluster keeps its old finding.
remediation_details.summary: Launch replacement EMR capacity with a reviewed security configuration that enables at-rest encryption.

checks.rationale: Fails an EMR cluster that has no SecurityConfiguration, or whose joined security configuration does not have EncryptionConfiguration.EnableAtRestEncryption set to true. An unresolvable configuration name gives UNKNOWN. Without at-rest encryption, EMRFS objects in S3 and local or EBS disks on cluster nodes hold processed data in plaintext.
checks.description: Fails an EMR cluster that has no SecurityConfiguration, or whose joined security configuration does not have EncryptionConfiguration.EnableAtRestEncryption set to true. An unresolvable configuration name gives UNKNOWN. Without at-rest encryption, EMRFS objects in S3 and local or EBS disks on cluster nodes hold processed data in plaintext.
checks.pass_when: The joined security configuration has EnableAtRestEncryption true.
checks.fail_when: No security configuration is attached, or EnableAtRestEncryption is false or absent.

caveats: CSE-Custom and SSE-KMS are mutually exclusive EncryptionMode values; the sibling SSE-KMS check requests the opposite mode. A choice of CSE-Custom is a policy decision and does not prove all S3 objects are encrypted.

steps: Inspect Cluster.Cluster.KerberosAttributes in the complete DescribeCluster detail; an absent object fails this predicate, which does not test actual KDC health or client authentication.
With the identity owner, choose supported EMR release, cluster-dedicated or external KDC, realm, certificate/network prerequisites, principals, client migration and ticket/keytab lifecycle.

Create a new reviewed EMR security configuration with AuthenticationConfiguration.KerberosConfiguration, then create replacement cluster capacity referencing it and including matching KerberosAttributes in the complete owner request.

checks.rationale: Uses the DescribeCluster detail (Cluster.Id proves it was read) and fails when KerberosAttributes is absent, which means the cluster was launched without Kerberos authentication. caveats: This predicate applies only to RUNNING or WAITING clusters and fails the joined subnet MapPublicIpOnLaunch=true. It assesses a future-launch subnet setting, not current primary public address, route, or reachability.

Changing this shared subnet setting can clear the check without removing an existing EMR public IPv4 address and affects other future launches in that subnet. Confirm owner intent and assess those consumers first.

cli.label: Inspect exact running EMR cluster and subnet ID
Disable future public IPv4 auto-assignment only after subnet-owner review

steps: Confirm Status.State is RUNNING or WAITING, resolve Cluster.Cluster.Ec2InstanceAttributes.Ec2SubnetId, and inspect the joined subnet MapPublicIpOnLaunch=true; missing subnet identity or join is UNKNOWN.

Review the subnet policy with the network owner and inspect the current primary EC2 address and route facts separately; the evaluator reads the configured default for future launches, not the present primary address.

If future auto-assignment is disallowed, disable MapPublicIpOnLaunch for this exact reviewed subnet through its configuration owner; assess other workloads that launch there and retain explicit public-IP settings where separately approved.

Recollect the subnet policy. Changing MapPublicIpOnLaunch affects future launches only and does not remove a current primary public address; if current exposure is separately confirmed and disallowed, plan conditional private-subnet replacement with jobs, data, client and rollback review.

checks.rationale: For EMR clusters in the RUNNING or WAITING state, looks up Ec2InstanceAttributes.Ec2SubnetId in the subnet inventory and fails if that subnet has MapPublicIpOnLaunch true (Security Hub EMR.1). A missing subnet gives UNKNOWN. Nodes launched there automatically get public IPv4 addresses, which puts the primary node on the internet.

caveats: The native predicate uses the MasterPublicDnsName .amazonaws.com suffix, not an actual public IP, route, open security group or reachable access test.

EMR cluster subnet placement is fixed at creation, but DNS suffix alone does not authorize disruptive replacement. If a private replacement is warranted, it changes endpoint identity, incurs capacity cost and requires job/data cutover.

cli.label: Inspect current cluster state and primary DNS
Resolve the primary EC2 instance from this cluster
Inspect the resolved EC2 network address

steps: Inspect Status.State and Cluster.Cluster.MasterPublicDnsName; this check skips terminated states and fails the .amazonaws.com public DNS form on any other state.

Resolve the primary EC2 instance and verify its actual public IPv4 address, subnet routing, security groups and reachable access paths. A DNS suffix alone does not establish a permitted internet path.

If the network owner confirms actual exposure conflicts with policy, plan a replacement EMR cluster in an approved private subnet with necessary S3, service endpoint, NAT and client paths; a running cluster cannot be moved to a different subnet.
Migrate jobs, data and clients only under that conditional plan and validate new addressing and workflow health; otherwise document the separate network-control evidence and owner disposition.

checks.rationale: Fails a non-terminated EMR cluster whose MasterPublicDnsName contains '.amazonaws.com', which means the primary node has a public IP. Private names such as *.ec2.internal pass. A primary node with a public address can be reached from the internet whenever its security groups allow it, which exposes cluster management interfaces.

checks.remediation: Remove the exact all-traffic public ingress rule from a security group attached to a public EMR cluster.

caveats: The native check applies to nonterminated EMR clusters with public-form MasterPublicDnsName and fails only a joined primary or core/task managed/additional SG with all-protocol ingress or a full 0-65535 port range from a global CIDR; a DNS suffix and an SG rule do not alone prove a successful internet connection.

The snapshot provides flagged group IDs, not rule IDs. Resolve and reverify the current exact rule before revocation; an SG can be shared with other clusters and changing it may break jobs, administration or service traffic.

EMR can add required internal rules to managed groups and SG associations are selected at cluster launch. Review owner-managed IaC and EMR block-public-access policy to prevent recurrence; do not broadly revoke internal cluster rules.

Inspect ingress rule IDs for the exact flagged group

iac.code: In the owning EC2 security group declaration for the flagged EMR primary or core/task group, remove only the reviewed all-protocol or full-port-range public-CIDR rule and retain required EMR internal and approved operator traffic. Review shared-group consumers and apply through the group owner; validate cluster jobs and current rule IDs after propagation.
iac.label: Narrow the exact owner-managed ingress rule

steps: Confirm the EMR cluster is not terminated and its MasterPublicDnsName has the public .amazonaws.com form; this predicate does not inspect a cluster without that public DNS form.

Resolve all EmrManagedMasterSecurityGroup, AdditionalMasterSecurityGroups, EmrManagedSlaveSecurityGroup and AdditionalSlaveSecurityGroups from Ec2InstanceAttributes. For each public_master_groups or public_slave_groups ID, inspect ingress rules and map the exact matching CIDR/protocol/port tuple to its current security-group-rule ID.

Review the rule with the EMR and network owners, then revoke only the identified ingress rule that allows all protocols or the full 0-65535 port range from a global IPv4/IPv6 network; preserve required narrow cluster management and workload paths.

Reinspect the group rules and recollect the cluster/security-group join. If moving the entire cluster to a private subnet is the chosen repair, use a separately reviewed replacement and client/job cutover because current cluster placement is fixed at launch.
remediation_details.summary: Remove the exact all-traffic public ingress rule from a security group attached to a public EMR cluster.

checks.rationale: For a non-terminated EMR cluster with public Amazon master DNS, fails if a managed or additional primary or core/task security group admits all protocols or the full 0-65535 port range from a public CIDR. Such ingress can expose Hadoop or Spark service ports and web interfaces to the Internet.
checks.description: For a non-terminated EMR cluster with public Amazon master DNS, fails if a managed or additional primary or core/task security group admits all protocols or the full 0-65535 port range from a public CIDR. Such ingress can expose Hadoop or Spark service ports and web interfaces to the Internet.
checks.pass_when: The cluster has no public DNS name, or none of its node security groups opens all traffic or all ports to a public CIDR.
checks.fail_when: The cluster has public DNS, and a primary or core/task group allows all traffic or 0-65535 from a public CIDR.
checks.not_applicable_when: The cluster state is TERMINATED or TERMINATED_WITH_ERRORS.

checks.remediation: Migrate a public-endpoint OpenSearch domain to a separately created VPC domain with reviewed data and client cutover.

caveats: The evaluator tests only VPCOptions.VPCId presence; it does not prove public reachability or assess policy, security groups, routing or client accessibility.

OpenSearch public-versus-VPC endpoint mode cannot change in place. A replacement has a new endpoint and billable capacity; snapshot/reindex compatibility, data freshness, private client routes and cutover/rollback need owner validation.
Do not delete the public domain or its snapshots merely to clear this count. Retire it only after verified migration and retention review.

iac.code: Declare a new OpenSearch domain with reviewed VPCOptions, subnets and security groups alongside the current public domain. Migrate data and clients with validation and rollback, then retire the old domain through a later approved lifecycle change. Updating VPCOptions on the existing public domain cannot perform this migration.
iac.label: Create a VPC replacement in the domain owner IaC

steps: Inspect Domain.DomainStatus.VPCOptions.VPCId on the named domain; this check fails when the ID is absent and does not evaluate subnet routes or effective access policy.

Choose the approved VPC, subnets across required Availability Zones, security groups, IP capacity, domain version, encryption, access policies, logging and private client network paths with the domain owner.
Create a separate VPC-access domain from the complete reviewed owner configuration; AWS cannot change an existing public endpoint domain into a VPC domain.

Migrate index data with an owner-tested snapshot restore or reindex plan, validate document counts and queries, then move every client and endpoint dependency to the new private domain with rollback available.
Recollect the replacement VPCOptions and validate VPCId, client health and data before retiring the old public domain under its retention plan; the old domain remains a separate finding until then.
remediation_details.summary: Migrate a public-endpoint OpenSearch domain to a separately created VPC domain with reviewed data and client cutover.

checks.rationale: For each opensearch domain, the evaluator flags FAIL when DomainStatus.VPCOptions.VPCId is empty or absent. The network path can expose the opensearch domain to traffic from outside its intended boundary.

checks.title: Elasticsearch domain has the internal user database enabled
checks.remediation: Enable the OpenSearch internal user database only when the owner selected that authentication model for this domain.

caveats: This evaluator only checks InternalUserDatabaseEnabled=true; it does not prove that internal users, passwords or role mappings are safe. Another native policy check expects the flag disabled, so the owner must select the intended authentication profile.

Fine-grained access control needs OpenSearch/Elasticsearch 6.7+, HTTPS, encryption at rest and node-to-node encryption and cannot be disabled after enablement. Changing the master-user model or access policy can interrupt clients.

The reviewed update file can contain a master password. Keep it in the owner secret workflow and out of source control, logs, findings and copyable command text; no credential value is interpolated here.

cli.label: Inspect exact domain security options and engine version

iac.code: Only for a domain whose owner requires the internal user database, update its OpenSearch security configuration to enable fine-grained access control and InternalUserDatabaseEnabled, with HTTPS and encryption prerequisites and secret-managed master credentials. Review role mappings, clients and irreversible FGAC enablement before applying. If an external identity profile is selected, document the conflicting policy expectation instead.
iac.label: Update owner-selected authentication profile

references.title: OpenSearch fine-grained access control and internal users

steps: Inspect Domain.DomainStatus.AdvancedSecurityOptions.InternalUserDatabaseEnabled and the domain engine/version; this count check fails when the internal database flag is false or absent, even if IAM or federation is the approved authentication model.

Confirm the policy profile with the domain owner because the separate internal-database-disabled check requests the opposite state. If IAM, Cognito, SAML or another external identity model is intentional, record the policy conflict instead of adding password users to clear this finding.

For a domain where internal users are required and OpenSearch/Elasticsearch version is at least 6.7, review prerequisites for fine-grained access control: HTTPS, encryption at rest and node-to-node encryption; plan role mappings and the client/Dashboards migration.

Submit a complete reviewed domain security update through the secret owner, enabling fine-grained access control and InternalUserDatabaseEnabled with protected master credentials. Migrate clients and validate role mappings during the supported transition period.

Recollect AdvancedSecurityOptions and validate application access. Fine-grained access control cannot be disabled once enabled, and an older incompatible domain needs a separately planned upgrade or replacement.
remediation_details.summary: Enable the OpenSearch internal user database only when the owner selected that authentication model for this domain.

checks.rationale: Tests the source-specific OpenSearch internal user database enabled profile. It is incompatible on one domain with the disabled profile and does not alone prove secure authentication. Remediation: Enable the internal user database only when the source profile calls for it, and review fine-grained access control and identity governance.
checks.description: Tests the source-specific OpenSearch internal user database enabled profile. It is incompatible on one domain with the disabled profile and does not alone prove secure authentication. Remediation: Enable the internal user database only when the source profile calls for it, and review fine-grained access control and identity governance.
checks.pass_when: InternalUserDatabaseEnabled is true.
checks.fail_when: InternalUserDatabaseEnabled is false or omitted.

checks.remediation: For an in-use ACM certificate expiring within seven days, restore eligible managed renewal or reimport an issuer-renewed imported certificate before expiry.

caveats: This check applies to in-use certificates and requires NotAfter more than seven days away. A non-ISSUED certificate without NotAfter is NOT_APPLICABLE; an ISSUED certificate without NotAfter is UNKNOWN.

The renew-certificate command is not a general renewal switch: AWS supports forced renewal only for previously exported eligible ACM-issued public or private certificates, not imported certificates. Exported public certificate renewal can incur a fee.

Imported certificate reimport needs owner-held certificate, matching private key and chain; never paste private key material into a command template or this rulepack. Reimport keeps the ARN but has key-type and size constraints and no rollback.
Certificate replacement can interrupt TLS clients; verify every InUseBy association, validation, issuance, region, and rollout with service owners before changing listeners or distributions.

cli.label: Inspect certificate type, validity, associations, and renewal status (read only)

iac.code: For an Amazon-issued certificate, keep the required DNS validation record and in-use service attachment under their real owners; review Private CA issuance permissions where applicable. For an imported certificate, the certificate owner obtains and reimports renewed material through the ACM console; an IaC declaration alone does not rotate it. Stage replacement certificate ARN and listener/distribution changes through the existing service deployment only when renewal or reimport cannot complete; verify clients and rollback before cutover.

references.title: AWS ACM check certificate renewal status

steps: Inspect the named in-use certificate in ACM Certificates > select certificate > Details and Renewal status, or use describe-certificate; record Type, Status, NotAfter, InUseBy, RenewalEligibility, RenewalSummary, and validation method before choosing an action.

For an Amazon-issued public certificate, repair failed DNS CNAME, email, or applicable HTTP validation with the domain owner and confirm ACM managed renewal; if renewal cannot complete before expiry, issue a replacement certificate and migrate each listener or distribution after validation.

For an ACM-issued private certificate, verify the issuing AWS Private CA remains active and can issue, the ACM service principal has renewal permission, and integrated associations remain eligible; coordinate certificate and client rollout with the CA and service owners.

For an IMPORTED certificate, obtain a renewed certificate and matching private key from its issuer through the certificate owner, then use ACM Certificates > select certificate > Actions > Reimport certificate to retain its ARN and associations; if reimport constraints prevent this, issue a replacement and migrate attachments.

Renew or re-import the certificate, or enable ACM managed renewal, before it expires. Verify NotAfter is more than seven days away, confirm TLS on every in-use association, and recollect the check; do not infer a safe renewal from absent metadata.

checks.title: In-use ACM certificate does not use an insecure key algorithm (RSA-1024, P-192)
frameworks: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) v4.0

controls.framework: Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard (PCI DSS) v4.0

checks.remediation: Replace an in-use RSA-1024 or P-192 ACM certificate with a separately issued stronger certificate and migrate every consuming service.

caveats: Only certificates with nonempty InUseBy are evaluated. The failure set is exactly RSA-1024 or P-192 after underscore-to-hyphen normalization; other algorithms pass this predicate even if a consuming service has narrower support.

ACM reimport cannot change a certificate's key type or size. Imported and ACM-issued certificates need a new certificate ARN with a supported stronger key and an explicit migration of each InUseBy association.

Changing TLS certificates can break clients or renewals. Validate domain names, chain, service-specific algorithms, ownership and rollback before switching associations; the old in-use ARN keeps failing until detached.

cli.label: Inspect exact native resource without secret values (read only)

references.title: AWS ACM certificate key algorithm support

steps: Describe the exact certificate ARN; inspect InUseBy, Type and KeyAlgorithm. An unused certificate is NOT_APPLICABLE; an in-use RSA-1024 or P-192 certificate fails after underscore-to-hyphen normalization.

Have the certificate and each consuming-service owner choose a stronger algorithm supported by that service. Request and validate a new ACM-issued certificate or import a new externally issued certificate under a new ARN; reimporting the old ARN cannot change key type or size.

Stage the new ARN in every InUseBy service association, verify TLS handshake, hostname and trust chain from representative clients, and retain the prior association for owner-approved rollback during the cutover.

Recollect the new and old certificate details. The old ARN remains a failed resource finding while in use; only after all consumers have moved does it become NOT_APPLICABLE, while the new ARN should pass the key-algorithm check.
remediation_details.summary: Replace an in-use RSA-1024 or P-192 ACM certificate with a separately issued stronger certificate and migrate every consuming service.

checks.title: AWS Private CA uses a post-quantum (ML-DSA) key algorithm
checks.remediation: Plan an ML-DSA Private CA replacement with the PKI owner, migrate issuance and trust safely, then verify the new CA key algorithm.

caveats: The evaluator skips only DELETED CAs; every other status fails unless CertificateAuthorityConfiguration.KeyAlgorithm is ML_DSA_44, ML_DSA_65 or ML_DSA_87. It does not test the signing algorithm or relying-party compatibility.

A CA key algorithm is chosen at creation. A replacement root or subordinate CA requires an owner-approved trust hierarchy, supported parent algorithm, certificate/profile compatibility, issuance migration and trust-store rollout; changing the CA can stop renewal or break validation.

AWS Private CA charges for additional CAs and issued certificates. Do not disable or delete the old CA until every dependent issuer, client and relying party has been migrated and rollback is documented.

references.title: AWS Private CA key and signing algorithm requirements

steps: Describe the exact CA ARN and inspect Status, Type and CertificateAuthorityConfiguration.KeyAlgorithm. DELETED is NOT_APPLICABLE; any other status with a key algorithm outside ML_DSA_44/65/87 fails.

Have the PKI owner inventory the CA hierarchy, issued certificates, integrated services and client trust stores; choose a supported ML-DSA key and matching signing algorithm only where parents and relying parties support it.

Create a separate owner-approved replacement CA through the existing PKI declaration and complete its certificate, revocation, permissions and trust distribution. Stage new issuance and renewals, validate representative clients, and retain the old CA during rollback.

Recollect the new CA's KeyAlgorithm and rerun the check. The old non-ML-DSA CA remains a resource finding until an owner-approved retirement after all dependent certificates and clients have migrated.

Deregistering a CA certificate can break LDAPS or client authentication. If it is the last registered certificate, AWS requires LDAPS disablement before deregistration, so preserve a validated replacement and owner-approved rollback.

checks.title: Bedrock custom model is encrypted with a customer managed KMS key

caveats: Native check targets owned ListCustomModels entries and the GetCustomModel Model.modelKmsKeyArn field; failed detail reads or incomplete facts remain UNKNOWN.

checks.remediation: Repair a failed scan or ship a tested patched ECR image, then confirm the newest scannable digest has a complete scan with no MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL findings.

caveats: The evaluator applies only to scan-on-push repositories with at least one scannable image; it excludes signature tags and picks the latest by imagePushedAt. A FAILED scan or observed MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL count fails, while historical COMPLETE DescribeImages snapshots with valid count maps remain evaluable.

Current ECR Basic Scanning omits scan status and finding summary from DescribeImages, so the collector requests DescribeImageScanFindings for the exact latest digest. A clean result cannot be inferred from DescribeImages alone, missing counts, a missing completion timestamp or an ACTIVE/pending scan.

Rebuilding and pushing an image can execute code and incur build, registry and scanning costs. Use the repository owner pipeline; no scan-start command or unreviewed tag deletion is part of this guidance.

cli.label: Inspect exact native resource without secret values (read only)
Inspect scan findings for the exact image digest (read only)

references.title: AWS ECR image scanning and DescribeImages limitation

steps: Confirm imageScanningConfiguration.scanOnPush=true, collect every image detail, and select the newest scannable non-signature image by imagePushedAt. Use only that exact imageDigest for DescribeImageScanFindings; disabled scan-on-push or no scannable image is NOT_APPLICABLE.

For FAILED status, investigate the exact digest scan failure and repository scanning configuration with the owner. For a COMPLETE scan with observed aggregate MEDIUM/HIGH/CRITICAL counts above zero, identify affected packages from the authorized scan report and patch the build in the repository owner pipeline.

Build, test, scan and push a replacement image through the owner delivery process. Validate downstream consumers before promoting the new digest; keep prior tags and images until rollout and rollback are reviewed.

Recollect the latest scannable digest and rerun the check. A PASS requires COMPLETE status, a present valid aggregate count map and a valid observed scan completion time from DescribeImageScanFindings; missing media, pending/ACTIVE status, denied or malformed facts and incomplete pagination remain UNKNOWN.

checks.pass_when: The selected exact-digest scan is COMPLETE with valid counts, observed completion time and zero MEDIUM, HIGH and CRITICAL findings; valid historical DescribeImages snapshots are supported.
checks.fail_when: The selected scan is FAILED or has a positive MEDIUM, HIGH or CRITICAL count; pending, denied, missing, malformed or incomplete facts are UNKNOWN.
checks.not_applicable_when: Scan on push is disabled or there are no scannable images.

checks.rationale: For each non-root credential-report user, FAILs when an enabled password or active access key was last used before 00:00 UTC of the capture date minus 45 days, or was never used and was created/rotated before that cutoff. Enabled but unused credentials are attack surface with no business value, and their abuse often goes unnoticed.

checks.pass_when: PASS when Every enabled password and active key was used, or created when never used, within the last 45 days.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when at least one enabled password or active key is stale beyond the 45-day cutoff.

checks.remediation: Set the storage-account key expiration reminder policy to the source's exact 90-day value.

caveats: This policy is a reminder, not key regeneration. Azure requires creation timestamps for both keys before setting it; older accounts may need staged key rotation first. Existing keys and clients are unchanged by the policy update.

iac.code: Set properties.keyPolicy.keyExpirationPeriodInDays = 90 on the owning storage account declaration.
iac.label: Change the existing managed declaration

steps: Inspect properties.keyPolicy.keyExpirationPeriodInDays and keyCreationTime for both keys on the named storage account; identify current key users and rotation process.
If both key creation timestamps exist, set the expiration reminder to 90 days through the account owner; otherwise plan staged key rotation before setting the policy.
Read the policy again and rerun this check; verify rotation separately using key creation metadata.
remediation_details.summary: Set the storage-account key expiration reminder policy to the source's exact 90-day value.

checks.rationale: For a storage account, FAIL means keyPolicy is absent or keyExpirationPeriodInDays is not exactly 90. This is a reminder setting; actual key regeneration is a separate check.
checks.description: For a storage account, FAIL means keyPolicy is absent or keyExpirationPeriodInDays is not exactly 90. This is a reminder setting; actual key regeneration is a separate check.
checks.pass_when: PASS when the key policy specifies exactly 90 days.
checks.fail_when: FAIL when keyPolicy is absent or the configured days differ from 90.

checks.remediation: Give each app client an explicit WriteAttributes allowlist excluding authorization-like custom claims, including plan, then validate self-signup, federation mappings, and existing claim provenance before trusting the pool.

caveats: Omitted WriteAttributes is a broad default in the AWS Developer Guide, not an empty allowlist; attribute-name matches are a risk heuristic, not proof of application authorization. Immutable custom claims can be user-supplied at self-service signup. An explicit empty list has unverified API response semantics and cannot establish no-write by itself.
Where name or ID is not safely auto-bound, verify the exact collected identity before replacing the visible placeholder. No command is executed.

Preserve every other client setting during updates; review signup, profile and IdP mapping compatibility, then reconcile historical claims.
iac.label: Update the owning infrastructure declaration

references.title: AWS Cognito: attributes for access control
AWS Cognito: user attribute permissions and immutable signup
AWS Cognito: update app client settings

steps: Inspect the complete user-pool schema, self-signup policy and every app-client detail; an omitted WriteAttributes list must not be read as an empty allowlist.

Review each authorization-like custom claim, including plan, all client write permissions and any IdP attribute mapping; configure explicit least-privilege write allowlists while preserving required signup and profile fields.
Treat an immutable custom claim as potentially self-supplied during signup; separately reassert existing claim values through a trusted administrator or use server-controlled authorization data.
Recollect the pool and rerun aws.htbp.cognito.client_no_writable_authorization_attributes; resolve missing or partial facts before claiming PASS.
remediation_details.summary: Give each app client an explicit WriteAttributes allowlist excluding authorization-like custom claims, including plan, then validate self-signup, federation mappings, and existing claim provenance before trusting the pool.

checks.rationale: Flags a Cognito user pool when a collected app client can write an authorization-like custom claim (including plan) that is mutable, or an immutable claim during allowed self-service signup. Omitted WriteAttributes is Cognito broad default access when the client detail is complete. Attribute names are a risk heuristic; the application authorization use must be reviewed. Empty explicit write lists remain UNKNOWN because their response semantics are unverified.
checks.description: Flags a Cognito user pool when a collected app client can write an authorization-like custom claim (including plan) that is mutable, or an immutable claim during allowed self-service signup. Omitted WriteAttributes is Cognito broad default access when the client detail is complete. Attribute names are a risk heuristic; the application authorization use must be reviewed. Empty explicit write lists remain UNKNOWN because their response semantics are unverified.

checks.title: CloudFront origin failover names two existing origins and status codes
checks.remediation: Configure a valid two-origin CloudFront failover group for this distribution.

remediation_details.summary: Configure a valid two-origin CloudFront failover group for this distribution.
steps: Inspect Config.DistributionConfig.Origins and OriginGroups on the exact distribution; identify any missing or duplicate origin IDs and missing or unsupported failover status codes.
Choose a tested secondary origin and status-code criteria with the application owner, then update the reviewed complete distribution configuration without dropping existing behaviors or origins.
Test primary and secondary response paths, read back both origin members and status codes, recollect and rerun this check.
caveats: Changing a CloudFront distribution can alter production routing and incur secondary-origin costs; review cache behavior targeting the group and rollback before deployment.
The predicate verifies declared origin-group metadata, not live failover availability or origin health.

checks.rationale: For a collected CloudFront distribution, checks that each declared origin group has two distinct existing origin IDs and at least one provider-supported failover status code. This signed predicate evaluates declared groups; it does not establish that a cache behavior references a group.
checks.description: For a collected CloudFront distribution, checks that each declared origin group has two distinct existing origin IDs and at least one provider-supported failover status code. This signed predicate evaluates declared groups; it does not establish that a cache behavior references a group.
checks.fail_when: OriginGroups is omitted or has zero groups in a complete distribution configuration, or any complete group has missing/duplicate origin members or no status codes.
checks.pass_when: At least one group exists and every group has exactly two distinct member origin IDs present in the distribution origin inventory and a nonempty list containing only provider-supported status codes.

checks.remediation: Restore continuous, all-supported AWS Config recording in this Region.

remediation_details.summary: Restore continuous, all-supported AWS Config recording in this Region.
steps: Inspect the matching config_recorder.name, recordingGroup.allSupported, default recordingMode.recordingFrequency, every recordingModeOverride frequency and Status.ConfigurationRecordersStatus[].recording.

Review resource type coverage, recording charges, delivery channel and approved exclusions with the account owner, then configure this recorder for all-supported continuous recording and start it if paused.
Confirm the matching recorder reports recording=true, allSupported=true and CONTINUOUS as both default and every override frequency, then recollect and rerun this check.
caveats: Continuous all-supported recording can materially increase Config configuration-item and rule-evaluation costs, particularly for ephemeral resources; confirm the owner policy before changing scope.
This predicate checks the recorder declaration and status only; it does not verify delivery-channel health or all account Regions.

references.title: AWS Config resource recording with CLI

checks.rationale: For a regional AWS Config recorder, checks the matching recorder status, all-supported recording group flag, default recording frequency, and every resource-type frequency override. A paused, narrowed, or daily recorder does not provide the requested continuous inventory.
checks.description: For a regional AWS Config recorder, checks the matching recorder status, all-supported recording group flag, default recording frequency, and every resource-type frequency override. A paused, narrowed, or daily recorder does not provide the requested continuous inventory.
checks.fail_when: A complete matching recorder has recording=false, allSupported=false, default recordingFrequency=DAILY, or any DAILY resource-type override.
checks.pass_when: The matching recorder is recording, allSupported is true, and default and all override frequencies are CONTINUOUS.

checks.title: In-use ACM certificate is issued, unexpired, and renewed or renewal eligible
frameworks: Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue C5

controls.framework: Cloud Computing Compliance Criteria Catalogue C5

checks.remediation: Renew or replace this in-use ACM certificate before it becomes unusable.

remediation_details.summary: Renew or replace this in-use ACM certificate before it becomes unusable.
steps: Inspect Certificate.Certificate.InUseBy, Status, NotAfter and RenewalEligibility against the snapshot time for the exact certificate.
If the certificate is expired, non-ISSUED, or within 30 days and INELIGIBLE, restore its validation/renewal path or replace it through an owner-reviewed certificate and listener migration.
Validate the certificate actually served by each listed consumer and its new expiry, then recollect and rerun this check.
caveats: Renewal eligibility is not proof renewal has completed or the new certificate was deployed; inspect consumer endpoints before declaring recovery.
Replacing a certificate can break TLS clients, names or trust chains; stage and test the replacement before cutover.

checks.rationale: For an in-use ACM certificate, compares issuance and expiration against the snapshot clock and checks renewal eligibility inside the 30-day window. The result describes certificate metadata and does not prove the renewed certificate is already deployed.
checks.description: For an in-use ACM certificate, compares issuance and expiration against the snapshot clock and checks renewal eligibility inside the 30-day window. The result describes certificate metadata and does not prove the renewed certificate is already deployed.
checks.fail_when: An in-use certificate is not ISSUED, expired, or within 30 days of expiry and INELIGIBLE for renewal.
checks.not_applicable_when: The complete ACM certificate metadata has an empty InUseBy list.
checks.pass_when: An in-use certificate is ISSUED, unexpired, and has more than 30 days remaining or is renewal eligible within 30 days.

checks.title: CloudWatch alarm actions are enabled and at least one state action exists
checks.remediation: Enable CloudWatch actions and configure an approved state action on this alarm.

remediation_details.summary: Enable CloudWatch actions and configure an approved state action on this alarm.
steps: Inspect ActionsEnabled and all three AlarmActions, OKActions and InsufficientDataActions lists on the exact metric alarm.
Choose an owner-approved SNS, Auto Scaling or other supported target and state transition, then configure its action and enable actions without discarding existing destinations.
Trigger or simulate an approved alarm transition, confirm delivery, read back the switch and action lists, recollect and rerun this check.
caveats: Alarm actions can invoke scaling or automation with cost and availability impact; review the selected action and test it safely.
The predicate verifies a configured action and enabled switch, not that the destination is healthy or receives notifications.

checks.rationale: For a CloudWatch metric alarm, checks that ActionsEnabled is true and at least one complete ALARM, OK or INSUFFICIENT_DATA action list contains an ARN. A configured ARN cannot invoke while actions are disabled.
checks.description: For a CloudWatch metric alarm, checks that ActionsEnabled is true and at least one complete ALARM, OK or INSUFFICIENT_DATA action list contains an ARN. A configured ARN cannot invoke while actions are disabled.
checks.fail_when: ActionsEnabled is false or all three complete state-action lists are empty.
checks.pass_when: ActionsEnabled is true and at least one of the three state-action lists is nonempty.

checks.remediation: Add a supported lifecycle rule to the flagged versioned Cloud Storage bucket.

remediation_details.summary: Add a supported lifecycle rule to the flagged versioned Cloud Storage bucket.
steps: Inspect versioning.enabled and lifecycle.rule on the exact bucket and inventory current/noncurrent object retention requirements.
Choose a supported action and condition with the data owner, stage a reviewed full lifecycle policy and test its effect on representative object versions.
Read back the lifecycle rule, verify retention behavior, recollect and rerun this check.
caveats: Lifecycle actions may delete objects or change storage class, and can increase retrieval cost; review legal holds and retention policies before applying.
This predicate tests rule presence and syntax, not whether its condition enforces the intended business retention period.

checks.rationale: For a Cloud Storage bucket with versioning explicitly enabled, checks that the full bucket metadata declares at least one supported lifecycle action with a condition. A versioned bucket without a lifecycle rule can accumulate noncurrent objects indefinitely.
checks.description: For a Cloud Storage bucket with versioning explicitly enabled, checks that the full bucket metadata declares at least one supported lifecycle action with a condition. A versioned bucket without a lifecycle rule can accumulate noncurrent objects indefinitely.
checks.fail_when: Versioning is true and lifecycle rules are empty or omitted in a FULL bucket projection.
evaluated: bucket.versioning.enabled (omitted means disabled in FULL projection)
checks.pass_when: Versioning is false or omitted in a FULL bucket projection, or true with a supported conditional lifecycle rule.

checks.remediation: Set an approved positive retention period on the flagged versioned bucket.

steps: Inspect versioning.enabled and retentionPolicy.retentionPeriod for this exact bucket and identify data preservation obligations.
Choose a positive duration with the data/legal owner, test restore and deletion behavior, then apply the reviewed bucket retention policy.
Read back the retention period, confirm intended objects remain recoverable, recollect and rerun this check.
caveats: A retention policy prevents early deletion and can materially increase storage cost; locking the policy is a distinct irreversible action and is not requested here.
A positive period passes this predicate without proving that the duration meets an organization's retention requirement.

checks.rationale: For a Cloud Storage bucket with versioning explicitly enabled, checks that the full bucket metadata declares a positive retentionPolicy.retentionPeriod in seconds. Retention changes can prevent deletion and need owner/legal review.

evaluated: bucket.versioning.enabled (omitted means disabled in FULL projection)

checks.title: Pub/Sub topic declares a customer-managed encryption key

checks.pass_when: The complete topic names a nonempty Cloud KMS key in kmsKeyName.

checks.title: Issued ACM certificates expire later than 30 days from capture
frameworks: AWS Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC)

controls.framework: AWS Federal Financial Institutions Examination Council (FFIEC)

checks.remediation: Issued ACM certificate expires at or before 30 days after the scan capture instant. Inspect the exact ARN, renewal path and consuming services; have the owner renew or replace it with a validated rollback plan.

caveats: This predicate applies only to ISSUED certificates and fails at the exact capture instant plus 30 days as well as earlier; other recognized statuses are NOT_APPLICABLE. Missing, denied, stale or incomplete inventory/detail remains UNKNOWN.

RenewalEligibility is not a predicate input. ACM-managed renewal depends on certificate type, validation and use; never assume a certificate will renew or that a renewed certificate is already deployed.
Replacing an in-use certificate can interrupt clients. Preserve the prior certificate and consumer configuration for an owner-approved rollback until replacement and TLS behavior are verified.

cli.label: Inspect exact ACM certificate metadata (read only)

iac.code: In the existing owner-managed ACM certificate, domain-validation and service-consumer declarations, review the exact issued certificate ARN and expiration against the captured 30-day boundary. For ACM-managed certificates, correct renewal validation and confirm deployment; for imported or otherwise non-managed certificates, plan owner-controlled reimport or a validated replacement. Review a staged consumer cutover and rollback to the prior certificate before applying any change.
iac.label: Review certificate and consumer ownership

steps: Confirm the scan captured a complete regional ACM certificate inventory. Inspect the exact CertificateArn with DescribeCertificate and compare Certificate.Certificate.Status and NotAfter with context.created_at plus 30 days; an ISSUED certificate at the boundary fails.

If the issued certificate is within or at that window, identify its ACM-managed or imported renewal path, validation records, and dependent services with the certificate owner; do not infer renewal from RenewalEligibility or presume a live endpoint already serves a renewed certificate.

Have the owner validate renewal or stage a replacement/reimport and consumer cutover. Keep the previous certificate and attachment available for rollback until certificate status, expiration and client TLS behavior are verified.
Recollect the scoped inventory and rerun aws.nist.acm_all_certificates_expiry_30_days. Preserve NOT_APPLICABLE for a recognized non-ISSUED status and UNKNOWN for incomplete or denied evidence.

remediation_details.summary: Enable CloudWatch metrics for the exact scoped WAFv2 rule group while retaining its reviewed visibility settings.
steps: Inspect the exact rule-group ARN, scope and GetRuleGroup detail; confirm the observed CloudWatchMetricsEnabled value and current MetricName.
Ask the rule-group owner to enable CloudWatchMetricsEnabled and retain a nonempty MetricName, existing Rules and complete VisibilityConfig in a reviewed full update.
Use a fresh lock token for the complete update, then recollect the same scoped group and verify CloudWatchMetricsEnabled is true; observe metric delivery separately after matching traffic.
caveats: Missing GetRuleGroup detail or ownership is UNKNOWN; a metrics setting does not establish effective web-ACL protection or log delivery.

UpdateRuleGroup replaces the mutable group specification and requires a fresh lock token; preserve all rules and visibility fields. CloudFront scope uses us-east-1 and CloudWatch metrics may incur charges.

rule-group ARN, Scope and exact GetRuleGroup.RuleGroup.ARN
checks.pass_when: The collection is complete and the exact scoped rule group has CloudWatchMetricsEnabled true.

complete vm/nic/subnet/nsg inventories and full ARM joins, NIC properties.virtualMachine.id and IP configurations

resolvedServiceTags status and numeric prefixes when tags occur; unresolved ASGs remain UNKNOWN

archived_checks.title: etcd trusts a CA file different from the kube-apiserver client CA
frameworks: Prowler ThreatScore Compliance Framework for Kubernetes

controls.framework: Prowler ThreatScore Compliance Framework for Kubernetes

archived_checks.remediation: Use a dedicated CA for etcd (--trusted-ca-file) distinct from the Kubernetes client CA.
archived_checks.rationale: Compares the etcd static Pod's --trusted-ca-file path with every kube-apiserver --client-ca-file path in the complete Pod inventory and FAILs when they are the same file. If etcd trusts the cluster client CA, any certificate issued for Kubernetes clients (including kubelets) can authenticate directly to etcd and read or rewrite all cluster state and Secrets. Differing paths are MANUAL because certificate contents are not compared.

Differing paths are MANUAL because certificate contents are not compared.
archived_checks.pass_when: Never PASS automatically: distinct paths yield MANUAL for content comparison.

archived_checks.title: Kubelet configuration declares an x509 client CA file
frameworks: Prowler ThreatScore Compliance Framework for Kubernetes

controls.framework: Prowler ThreatScore Compliance Framework for Kubernetes

archived_checks.remediation: Set authentication.x509.clientCAFile in the kubelet configuration.
archived_checks.rationale: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose authentication block exists but authentication.x509.clientCAFile is unset or empty. Without a client CA the kubelet cannot verify x509 client certificates, so the API server's kubelet client identity cannot be authenticated and the kubelet API falls back to weaker or anonymous authentication.

archived_checks.title: Kubelet streaming connection idle timeout is not zero
archived_checks.remediation: Set streamingConnectionIdleTimeout to a non-zero duration (for example 4h0m0s).
archived_checks.rationale: Flags a supplied kubelet configuration whose streamingConnectionIdleTimeout is a Go duration where every numeric part is zero (e.g. '0' or '0s'). A zero timeout disables idle cut-off for exec/attach/port-forward streams, letting abandoned or hijacked interactive sessions stay open indefinitely and exhausting kubelet resources.

archived_checks.title: Kubelet TLS cipher suites are limited to strong ciphers
frameworks: Prowler ThreatScore Compliance Framework for Kubernetes

archived_checks.remediation: Restrict tlsCipherSuites to the CIS strong-cipher list.

spec.data_source: Complete paged Microsoft.Compute/virtualMachines GET and instanceView: properties.storageProfile.osDisk.osType, properties.osProfile.linuxConfiguration.ssh.publicKeys[] and PowerState status.
spec.predicate: For each running Linux VM with complete launch-configuration evidence, FAIL if properties.osProfile.linuxConfiguration.ssh.publicKeys is a nonempty array; PASS if that array is explicitly present and empty. UNKNOWN if OS type, running state, launch-key array, or inventory completeness is unresolved or malformed. Windows and nonrunning VMs are NOT_APPLICABLE. This is a literal launch-key presence criterion, not a claim about effective guest authentication.
spec.title: Running Linux VM launch configuration has no SSH public key
spec.description: Checks the literal Azure PCI source criterion: a running Linux VM is noncompliant when its recorded launch configuration contains an SSH public key. This checks the stored launch configuration only; it does not measure guest SSH or password authentication.
spec.remediation_hint: Review the VM's recorded launch SSH public keys against the approved access policy. If this literal source criterion applies, use an approved deployment configuration without a launch SSH public key; assess guest authentication separately.

provenance.criterion_scope: recorded VM launch SSH public-key presence; no runtime authentication claim

spec.title: Cloud SQL protection against repeated failed sign-ins
spec.description: Preserves the original lockout-or-rate-limit requirement. A positive configured-lockout verdict requires a dated explicitly approved customer-account responsibility boundary matching the entire complete API-visible account universe, and documented managed MySQL lockout on every account. It does not assert protection of provider-internal principals or observed runtime login behavior.
spec.data_source: Read-only SQL Admin instances.list and exact project/instance users.list: databaseVersion, state, instance passwordValidationPolicy.enablePasswordPolicy, User.passwordPolicy.enableFailedAttemptsCheck and allowedFailedAttempts, host-qualified identity and collection provenance.
spec.predicate: Retain the original account lockout-or-rate-limit requirement. For serving managed MySQL 8.0+ with enabled instance password policy, complete current exact-bound users.list and a dated approved customer-controlled account scope equal to the entire API-visible user universe, PASS only when every account is BUILT_IN with enableFailedAttemptsCheck=true and positive integer allowedFailedAttempts. The operator-approved responsibility boundary is normative input, not a cloud observation; provider-internal managed accounts are outside the asserted customer scope. Missing, expired, mismatched, broader, mixed-authentication, malformed, denied, partial or unsupported scope/evidence remains UNKNOWN with any valid bounded configuration witness. Disabled or absent policy never proves FAIL because independent rate limiting may exist. No runtime login test is claimed.
spec.remediation_hint: Establish the full in-scope authentication-account inventory and approved lockout or rate-limiting controls. For supported managed MySQL built-in accounts, review instance password-policy enablement and each user's passwordPolicy.enableFailedAttemptsCheck and positive allowedFailedAttempts; verify other authentication paths separately without inferring a violation from missing metadata.

provenance.original_requirement: When repeated failed login attempts are made in a short timeframe, the account must be locked out or rate-limited to prevent further login attempts.
provenance.criterion_scope: Original account lockout or rate limiting: configured PASS is limited to the explicitly approved customer-account boundary, exactly matched to the complete API-visible roster; native witness alone does not establish that boundary or provider-internal/runtime protection
